mcqs.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He can to sing very well.
mcqs.explanation: A modal is always followed by the base form (V1) without "to" and without "-s".

mcqs.q: It is compulsory. You ___ pay the fee before Friday.
mcqs.explanation: "Must" expresses strong obligation/compulsion, which the phrase "It is compulsory" demands.

mcqs.q: When I was young, I ___ swim in the river every morning.
mcqs.explanation: "Used to + V1" expresses a habit of the past that no longer continues.

mcqs.q: Find the part with the error: She (A) dare not (B) to ask (C) any question (D) in the class.
mcqs.explanation: "Dare" used as a modal (dare not) is followed by the base verb "ask" without "to".

mcqs.q: ___ I use your mobile phone for a moment, Sir?
mcqs.explanation: "May" is the correct modal for seeking formal permission.

mcqs.q: The office closed at 6 pm and it is 9 pm now, so he ___ have left already.
mcqs.explanation: "Must + have + V3" expresses a strong logical conclusion about the past.

mcqs.q: How ___ you talk to your father like that!
mcqs.explanation: In such present-tense exclamations of indignation, "dare" is used as a modal without "-s".

mcqs.q: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I cannot be able to come tomorrow.
I can not able to come tomorrow.
I could not be able to come tomorrow.
mcqs.explanation: 'Can' and 'be able to' express the same ability, so using both together is superfluous. Correct form: I cannot come tomorrow or I will not be able to come tomorrow.

mcqs.q: When I was young, I ___ climb trees easily.
mcqs.explanation: Past ability is expressed by could (the past form of 'can'). 'Can' refers to present ability, so it cannot describe a childhood habit.

mcqs.q: You ___ not smoke here; it is strictly prohibited.
mcqs.explanation: Must not expresses prohibition (something is strictly forbidden). 'Need not' only means absence of necessity — the act is optional, not forbidden.

mcqs.q: He dare not ___ me a liar.
mcqs.explanation: When dare is a modal (followed by 'not'), it takes the bare infinitive: dare not call. 'To call' would be used only in the main-verb form: does not dare to call.

mcqs.q: ___ God bless you with success!
mcqs.explanation: Formal wishes and blessings begin with May + subject + V1: May God bless you! 'Can' expresses ability, not a blessing.

mcqs.q: We ___ respect our elders.
mcqs.explanation: Ought to expresses moral duty and always takes 'to'. 'Must to' and 'should to' are wrong because must/should already take the bare infinitive.

mcqs.q: How ___ you speak to me like this?
mcqs.explanation: In indignation questions, dare acts as a modal and takes V1 directly: How dare you speak...? No 'to' and no '-s' is added.

mcqs.q: He ___ swim across the river when he was young.
mcqs.explanation: Past ability = could।

mcqs.q: You ___ to obey the rules of the school.
mcqs.explanation: 'Ought to' = moral duty, always with 'to'.

mcqs.q: ___ you pass me the salt, please?
mcqs.explanation: Polite request = Could।

mcqs.q: She ___ not speak rudely to her teachers.
mcqs.explanation: Must not = prohibition।

mcqs.q: I ___ rather die than beg.
mcqs.explanation: Preference = would rather + V1।

mcqs.q: He ___ not come without permission.
mcqs.explanation: 'Dare not + V1' (modal form).

mcqs.q: You ___ have informed me earlier.
mcqs.explanation: Past obligation = ought to have + V3।

mcqs.q: ___ that I were a king!
mcqs.explanation: Wish = Would that + subject + V2।

mcqs.q: How ___ you talk to me like that?
mcqs.explanation: Indignation uses 'dare' as modal + V1।

mcqs.q: He ___ have been a doctor, but he chose engineering.
mcqs.explanation: Past unrealised = could have + V3।

mcqs.q: We ___ respect our national flag.
mcqs.explanation: Moral duty = ought to / should (both take V1).

mcqs.q: You ___ not worry; everything will be fine.
mcqs.explanation: 'Need not' = absence of necessity।

mcqs.q: She ___ be at home; the lights are on.
mcqs.explanation: Strong certainty = must be।

mcqs.q: The news ___ be true, but I doubt it.
mcqs.explanation: Weak possibility = may।

mcqs.q: You ___ better leave now, or you'll miss the train.
mcqs.explanation: 'Had better + V1' = strong advice।

mcqs.q: She ___ have left already; her bag is gone.
mcqs.explanation: Logical certainty about past = must have + V3।

mcqs.q: Children ___ be seen, not heard.
mcqs.explanation: Proverbial advice uses 'should'.

mcqs.q: It ___ rain tonight, so carry an umbrella.
mcqs.explanation: Possibility of future = may।

mcqs.q: He ___ not come yesterday despite the invitation.
mcqs.explanation: 'Dared not + V1' — past indignation।

mcqs.q: We ___ to take care of our parents in old age.
mcqs.explanation: 'Ought to' = moral duty।

mcqs.q: I ___ not have said that to her.
mcqs.explanation: Regret = should not have + V3।

mcqs.q: You ___ to apologize for the delay.
mcqs.explanation: 'Ought to' = moral obligation।

mcqs.q: She ___ play tennis when she was young.
mcqs.explanation: Past ability = 'could'.

mcqs.explanation: 'Must' expresses obligation/compulsion.

mcqs.q: You ______ have taken my permission before borrowing my book.

mcqs.q: It ______ rain this evening; the sky is cloudy.

mcqs.q: How ______ you speak to me like that!
mcqs.explanation: 'Dare' in the interrogative expresses indignation: 'How dare you'.

mcqs.q: ______ you please pass me the salt?
mcqs.explanation: 'Would you please' is the most polite request form.

mcqs.q: He said that he ______ come, but he did not.

mcqs.q: You ______ not smoke in the hospital.

mcqs.q: I ______ rather stay at home than go out in this rain.
mcqs.explanation: 'Would rather ... than' expresses preference.

mcqs.q: There ______ be a temple here; now it is a mall.

mcqs.q: You ______ hurry; there is plenty of time.
mcqs.explanation: 'Needn't' = absence of necessity.

mcqs.q: He ______ be at home; his car is in the porch.
mcqs.explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong logical deduction.

mcqs.q: A modal verb is always followed by the ______ form of the verb.
mcqs.explanation: Modals take the bare infinitive (base form) without 'to' and without '-s'.

mcqs.q: ______ we start the meeting now?

mcqs.q: She ______ speak four languages fluently.

mcqs.q: The door is locked. He ______ have gone out.
mcqs.explanation: 'Must have + V3' expresses a certain conclusion about the past.

mcqs.explanation: Two past actions — the one that happened first goes into the Past Perfect (had left); the later one stays in simple past (reached).

mcqs.q: I ___ him yesterday.
mcqs.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a definite past time, so the simple past (met) is used. Present perfect never pairs with yesterday/ago/last week.

mcqs.q: Water ___ at 100°C.
mcqs.explanation: A universal/general truth is always expressed in the simple present, regardless of when it is spoken.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: She writes a letter.
options: A letter is written by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter has been written by her.
mcqs.explanation: Simple present active (writes) → passive is/am/are + V3: A letter is written by her.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: The boy killed the snake.
options: The snake is killed by the boy.
The snake was killed by the boy.
The snake has been killed by the boy.
The snake had been killed by the boy.
mcqs.explanation: Simple past (killed) → was/were + V3: The snake was killed by the boy.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: Open the door.
mcqs.explanation: An order/imperative becomes passive with Let + object + be + V3: Let the door be opened.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: Who taught you English?
options: By whom were you taught English?
By whom you were taught English?
Whom was English taught by you?
mcqs.explanation: 'Who' → By whom; then auxiliary + subject + V3: By whom were you taught English?

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: They are building a bridge.
options: A bridge is built by them.
A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge was being built by them.
A bridge has been built by them.
mcqs.explanation: Present continuous → is/are being + V3: A bridge is being built.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: You must obey the orders.
options: The orders must have been obeyed.
mcqs.explanation: Modal passive = modal + be + V3: The orders must be obeyed. The by-phrase (by you) is dropped as it is unimportant.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct passive: Someone has stolen my purse.
options: My purse was stolen by someone.
mcqs.explanation: Present perfect → has/have been + V3. When the doer is vague ('someone'), the by-phrase is omitted: My purse has been stolen.

mcqs.q: Who broke this cup? → Passive
options: By whom was this cup broken?
By who was this cup broken?
mcqs.explanation: Who → By whom + aux + subject + V3।

mcqs.q: Can anybody cure this disease? → Passive
options: Can this disease be cured by anybody?
Can this disease cured by anybody?
mcqs.explanation: Modal passive = modal + be + V3।

mcqs.q: Close the door. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: Imperative → Let + object + be + V3।

mcqs.q: Did she sing a song? → Passive
options: Did a song sing by her?
Was a song sung by her?
Was a song sang by her?
Was a song being sung by her?
mcqs.explanation: Past interrogative → Was/Were + subject + V3।

mcqs.q: Don't touch it. → Passive
options: Both A and B are correct
mcqs.explanation: Negative imperative → Let + obj + not + be + V3 OR obj + should not + be + V3।

mcqs.q: I remember my father taking me to the zoo. → Passive
options: I remember being taken to the zoo by my father.
I remember taken to the zoo by my father.
I remember to be taken to the zoo.
I remembered being taken to the zoo.
mcqs.explanation: After 'remember', use gerund passive 'being + V3'।

mcqs.q: It is time to shut the shop. → Passive
options: It is time the shop is shut.
It is time for the shop to be shut.
It is time to be shut the shop.
It is time the shop shut.
mcqs.explanation: 'It is time + for + obj + to be + V3'।

mcqs.q: Someone is reading the newspaper. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: Present Continuous → is/are being + V3।

mcqs.q: Why did she not do the work? → Passive
options: Why was the work not done by her?
Why the work was not done?
Why was not the work done?
Why was the work not do?
mcqs.explanation: Question passive: Wh + aux + subject + not + V3।

mcqs.q: Someone has stolen my pen. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: By 'someone' is dropped in passive।

mcqs.q: The principal promised him a reward. → Passive
options: He was promised a reward by the principal.
A reward was promised to him by the principal.
He was promised by the principal a reward.
mcqs.explanation: Ditransitive verbs form two passives।

mcqs.q: One should keep one's word. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: Modal: should + be + V3।

mcqs.q: The police arrested the thief. → Passive
options: The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.
The thief had arrested by the police.
The thief arrested by the police.
mcqs.explanation: Past Simple → was/were + V3।

mcqs.q: She will write a poem. → Passive
options: A poem will be written by her.
A poem will written by her.
A poem will be wrote by her.
A poem will be write by her.
mcqs.explanation: Future → will be + V3।

mcqs.q: We are building a new school. → Passive
options: A new school is being built.
A new school was being built.
A new school has been built.
mcqs.explanation: Present Continuous → is/are being + V3।

mcqs.q: Let us play football. → Passive
options: Let football be played by us.
mcqs.explanation: 'Let us + V1' → Let + obj + be + V3।

mcqs.q: She has done the work. → Passive
options: The work has been done by her.
The work is done by her.
The work was done by her.
The work had been done by her.
mcqs.explanation: Present Perfect → has/have been + V3।

mcqs.q: We must obey the law. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: Modal passive = modal + be + V3।

mcqs.q: They were painting the walls. → Passive
mcqs.explanation: Past Continuous → was/were being + V3।

mcqs.q: Who wrote the Ramayana? → Passive
options: By whom was the Ramayana written?
By who was the Ramayana written?
mcqs.explanation: Who → By whom + was/were + subject + V3।

mcqs.q: Has someone informed the police? → Passive
mcqs.explanation: 'Police' is plural; passive = have been + V3।

mcqs.q: Post the letter at once. → Passive
options: Let the letter be posted at once.
The letter is posted at once.
Let the letter posted at once.
mcqs.explanation: Imperative → Let + obj + be + V3।

mcqs.q: Who killed the spider? → Passive
options: By whom was the spider killed?
By who was the spider killed?
Whom was the spider killed by?
mcqs.explanation: Who → By whom + was/were + subject + V3।

mcqs.q: They have built a new house. → Passive
options: A new house is built by them.
A new house was built by them.
A new house had been built by them.
A new house has been built by them.
mcqs.explanation: Present Perfect → has/have been + V3।

mcqs.q: I saw him crossing the road. → Passive
options: He was seen crossing the road.
He was being seen crossing the road.
He is seen crossing the road.
mcqs.explanation: Perception verb passive: was/were + V3 + V-ing।

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, "I am reading a book."
options: He said that I am reading a book.
He said that he was reading a book.
He said that he is reading a book.
He told that he had read a book.
mcqs.explanation: Present Continuous back-shifts to Past Continuous and I → he.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said to me, "Do you like coffee?"
options: She asked me did I like coffee.
She asked me whether I liked coffee.
She said me if I like coffee.
She asked that I liked coffee.
mcqs.explanation: Yes/No question → asked + whether/if + assertive order, with back-shift (like → liked).

mcqs.q: The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the sun." The correct indirect speech is —
options: The teacher said that the earth revolved around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had revolved around the sun.
The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher told the earth revolved around the sun.
mcqs.explanation: A universal truth keeps the simple present even after a past reporting verb.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: "Please help me," he said to me.
options: He ordered me to help him.
He requested me to help him.
He said to me that I should help him.
He asked that I helped him.
mcqs.explanation: "Please" signals a request → requested + object + to + V1.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, "I saw a film here yesterday."
options: He said that he saw a film there yesterday.
He said that he had seen a film there the previous day.
He said that he had seen a film here yesterday.
He said that he has seen a film there the previous day.
mcqs.explanation: Simple Past → Past Perfect; here → there; yesterday → the previous day.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said to her, "Where do you live?"
options: He asked her where did she live.
He asked her where she lived.
He asked her where she lives.
He said her where she lived.
mcqs.explanation: The wh-word stays, the question order becomes assertive (she lived), and do is dropped.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The officer said to the clerk, "Do not leave the office."
options: The officer ordered the clerk not to leave the office.
The officer ordered the clerk to not leave the office.
The officer requested the clerk not leaving the office.
The officer said the clerk not leave the office.
mcqs.explanation: Negative command → ordered + not to + V1.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: He said, "I am happy."
options: He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
He said that I am happy.
He said that he had been happy.
mcqs.explanation: Present (am) backshifts to past (was); 'I' (first person, subject) changes to 'he'. Result: He said that he was happy.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: She said to me, "Do you like coffee?"
options: She asked me that did I like coffee.
She asked me if I liked coffee.
She told me do you like coffee.
She asked did I like coffee.
mcqs.explanation: Yes-no question → asked + if/whether + statement order (subject before verb, no auxiliary 'did'). 'Do you like' → 'I liked'.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: The teacher said, "The earth revolves round the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth revolved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth revolves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had revolved round the sun.
The teacher said the earth was revolving round the sun.
mcqs.explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense in indirect speech — no backshift. This is the classic exception.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: He said, "Alas! I am ruined."
options: He said alas he is ruined.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
He cried that he had been ruined.
He exclaimed with joy that he was ruined.
mcqs.explanation: 'Alas!' expresses grief → reporting verb becomes exclaimed with sorrow, then backshift am → was.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: Mother said to me, "Do not go out in the rain."
options: Mother said me not to go out in the rain.
Mother forbade me to go out in the rain.
Mother asked that I should not go out in the rain.
Mother ordered do not go out in the rain.
mcqs.explanation: A negative order is reported with forbade + object + to + V1 — the negative is carried by 'forbade' itself, so 'not to go' is redundant.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: He said, "I shall come tomorrow."
options: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he would come the next day.
He said that he would come tomorrow.
He said he shall come the next day.
mcqs.explanation: shall → would and tomorrow → the next day. Both the modal and the time word must change.

mcqs.q: Indirect speech: She said, "Hurrah! We won the match."
options: She exclaimed with joy that they won the match.
She said hurrah they have won the match.
She applauded that they would win the match.
She exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
mcqs.explanation: 'Hurrah!' → exclaimed with joy; past simple (won) backshifts to past perfect (had won); we → they.

mcqs.q: She said to me, "Where do you live?" → Indirect speech:
options: She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where I live.
She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where I lived.
mcqs.explanation: Wh-question → asked + wh + statement order; do→did; live→lived.

mcqs.q: He said, "I am busy now." — Choose the correct indirect speech.
options: He said that he is busy now.
He said that he was busy then.
He says that he was busy then.
He said that he had been busy now.
mcqs.explanation: Present "am" backshifts to past "was" and "now" changes to "then" in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the Sun." — Indirect speech?
options: The teacher said that the earth revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the earth had revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher told that the earth revolved around the Sun.
mcqs.explanation: Universal truths keep the present tense — no backshift is applied.

mcqs.q: He said to her, "Do you like coffee?" — Indirect speech?
options: He asked her did she like coffee.
He asked her that she liked coffee.
He asked her if she liked coffee.
He told her whether she likes coffee.
mcqs.explanation: Yes/No questions are joined with if/whether, with backshift (do → did).

mcqs.q: "Please open the door," he said to me. — Indirect speech?
options: He ordered me to open the door.
He requested me to open the door.
He said me please open the door.
He told that I open the door.
mcqs.explanation: "Please" signals a polite request, so the reporting verb is "requested" + to-infinitive.

mcqs.q: "Don't touch the live wire," the electrician said to me. — Indirect speech?
options: The electrician warned me not to touch the live wire.
The electrician said me don't touch the live wire.
The electrician ordered do not touch the live wire.
The electrician asked that I don't touch the wire.
mcqs.explanation: Negative commands take "warned/ordered + not + to-infinitive".

mcqs.q: "Hurrah! We have won the match," they said. — Indirect speech?
options: They said with joy that they won the match.
They exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
They exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the match.
They told with joy that they have won the match.
mcqs.explanation: "Hurrah" becomes "exclaimed with joy" and present perfect backshifts to past perfect.

mcqs.q: He said to me, "Good morning!" — Indirect speech?
options: He said good morning to me.
mcqs.explanation: Greetings are reported with "wished".

mcqs.q: "Let's go for a walk," she said. — Indirect speech?
options: She said that let us go for a walk.
She proposed going for a walk.
She ordered to go for a walk.
She asked that they should go for walk.
mcqs.explanation: A "let's" suggestion is reported with proposed/suggested + gerund.

mcqs.q: "I shall meet you tomorrow," he said to me. — Indirect speech?
options: He said that he will meet me tomorrow.
He told me that he would meet me the next day.
He said that he would meet you tomorrow.
He said to me that he shall meet me the next day.
mcqs.explanation: Shall → would and tomorrow → the next day in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: "I met her here yesterday," he said. — Indirect speech?
options: He said that he had met her there the previous day.
He said that he met her here yesterday.
He said that he has met her there yesterday.
He said that he had met her here the previous day.
mcqs.explanation: here → there and yesterday → the previous day; simple past backshifts to past perfect.

mcqs.q: "You must submit the form tonight," the clerk said to me. — Indirect speech?
options: The clerk said that I must submit the form that night.
The clerk told that I had to submit the form that night.
The clerk said that I had to submit the form tonight.
The clerk said to me that I must submit the form tonight.
mcqs.explanation: must (obligation) usually becomes had to, and tonight becomes that night.

mcqs.q: Which reporting verb correctly converts: He said to me, "..." ?
mcqs.explanation: "Said to + object" changes to "told + object" in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: He said, "Why are you late today?" — Indirect speech?
options: He asked why I was late that day.
He asked why was I late that day.
He asked that why I am late today.
He asked why am I late that day.
mcqs.explanation: Keep the wh-word, use statement word order, backshift the tense and change today → that day.

mcqs.q: "I have already finished my work," she said. — Indirect speech?
options: She said that she has already finished her work.
She said that she had already finished her work.
She said that she finished her work already.
She said she has finished already her work.
mcqs.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: "Stand up," the teacher said to the boys. — Indirect speech?
options: The teacher said the boys to stand up.
The teacher ordered the boys to stand up.
The teacher asked that the boys stand up.
The teacher told stand up to the boys.
mcqs.explanation: A command is reported with ordered + to-infinitive.

mcqs.q: "Congratulations! You have passed," he said to me. — Indirect speech?
options: He congratulated me and said that I had passed.
He congratulate me that I have passed.
He said congratulations that I had passed.
He congratulated that I have passed.
mcqs.explanation: Exclamations like "Congratulations!" are reported with the verb congratulated.

mcqs.q: "What a beautiful painting it is!" she said. — Indirect speech?
options: She exclaimed that it was a very beautiful painting.
She said what a beautiful painting it was.
She exclaimed what a beautiful painting it is.
She told that the painting was very beautiful.
mcqs.explanation: Exclamatory "What a..." becomes "exclaimed that ... very ...", with tense backshift.

mcqs.q: "May you live long!" the saint said to him. — Indirect speech?
options: The saint wished that he might live long.
The saint wished that he may live long.
The saint prayed that he will live long.
The saint said that he might live long life.
mcqs.explanation: Blessings take "wished/prayed + might".

mcqs.q: Which time-word change is INCORRECT in indirect speech?
mcqs.explanation: tomorrow → the next day (yesterday → the previous day), so option D is wrong.

mcqs.q: He said, "I am busy." → Indirect speech:
options: He said that he is busy.
He said that he was busy.
He said that I am busy.
He says that he was busy.
mcqs.explanation: Present tense shifts to past and 'I' changes to 'he' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: She said, "I will help you tomorrow." → Indirect speech:
options: She said she will help me tomorrow.
She said she would help me the next day.
She said she would help you tomorrow.
She says she will help me the next day.
mcqs.explanation: 'Will' → 'would', 'tomorrow' → 'the next day', 'you' → 'me' (the listener).

mcqs.q: The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the Sun." → Indirect speech:
options: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher told that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.
mcqs.explanation: Universal truths keep the present tense in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: He said to me, "Please open the window." → Indirect speech:
options: He said to me to please open the window.
He requested me to open the window.
He ordered me open the window.
He asked that I open the window please.
mcqs.explanation: Requests take 'requested + object + to-infinitive'.

mcqs.q: Mother said to me, "Do not go out in the rain." → Indirect speech:
options: Mother said me not to go out in the rain.
Mother told me do not go out in the rain.
Mother forbade me to go out in the rain.
Mother asked that I should not go out in the rain.
mcqs.explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'forbade ... to' or 'told ... not to'.

mcqs.q: He said, "Alas! I am ruined." → Indirect speech:
options: He said alas he was ruined.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
He cried that he is ruined.
He exclaimed with joy that he was ruined.
mcqs.explanation: 'Alas' expresses sorrow → 'exclaimed with sorrow' + past tense.

mcqs.q: She said, "Hurrah! We have won the match." → Indirect speech:
options: She exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
She said hurrah they have won the match.
She exclaimed with joy that they have won the match.
She happily said that they win the match.
mcqs.explanation: 'Hurrah' → 'exclaimed with joy'; present perfect shifts to past perfect.

mcqs.q: He said, "Where do you live?" → Indirect speech:
options: He asked where did I live.
mcqs.explanation: Wh-questions keep the question word but use statement order (no 'did').

mcqs.q: She said to him, "Are you coming to the party?" → Indirect speech:
options: She asked him if he was coming to the party.
She asked him that was he coming to the party.
She said him are you coming to the party.
She asked if he is coming to the party.
mcqs.explanation: Yes/No questions are reported with 'if/whether' and statement word order.

mcqs.q: He said, "I bought this car last year." → Indirect speech:
options: He said he bought this car last year.
He said he had bought that car the previous year.
He said he has bought that car last year.
He said he had bought this car last year.
mcqs.explanation: Past simple → past perfect; 'this' → 'that'; 'last year' → 'the previous year'.

mcqs.q: The doctor said to me, "You must take rest." → Indirect speech:
options: The doctor said to me that I must take rest.
The doctor told me that I had to take rest.
The doctor advised me that I have to take rest.
The doctor said to me that you had to take rest.
mcqs.explanation: With a past reporting verb, 'must' (obligation) becomes 'had to', and 'you' changes to 'me/I'.

mcqs.q: He said, "Let us go for a walk." → Indirect speech:
options: He said let us go for a walk.
He proposed that they should go for a walk.
He told that let them go for a walk.
He said that we went for a walk.
mcqs.explanation: 'Let us' (suggestion) is reported with 'proposed/suggested that ... should'.

mcqs.q: She says, "I like coffee." → Indirect speech:
options: She says that she likes coffee.
She says that she liked coffee.
She said that she likes coffee.
mcqs.explanation: If the reporting verb is in the present ('says'), the tense does not change.

mcqs.q: He said to me, "Congratulations on your success!" → Indirect speech:
options: He congratulated me on my success.
He said congratulations to my success.
He greeted me on my success.
He congratulated me for my success.
mcqs.explanation: Congratulations are reported as 'congratulated ... on'.

mcqs.q: He said, "Good morning, friends." → Indirect speech:
options: He wished his friends good morning.
He told his friends good morning.
He bade his friends that good morning.
mcqs.explanation: Greetings are reported with 'wished'.

mcqs.q: The stranger said, "Which is the way to the station?" → Indirect speech:
options: The stranger said which is the way to the station.
The stranger asked which was the way to the station.
The stranger asked that which is the way to the station.
The stranger told which way was to the station.
mcqs.explanation: Wh-question: 'asked + question word + statement order', tense back-shifted.

mcqs.q: He said, "I can solve this sum." → Indirect speech:
options: He said he can solve this sum.
He said that he could solve that sum.
He said that he can solve that sum.
He said he could solve this sum.
mcqs.explanation: 'Can' → 'could'; 'this' → 'that' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: She said to her son, "May you live long!" → Indirect speech:
options: She said to her son that he may live long.
She prayed that her son might live long.
She wished that her son may live long.
She blessed her son that he might live long.
mcqs.explanation: Blessings/prayers take 'prayed/blessed that ... might'.

mcqs.q: He said, "What a beautiful scene it is!" → Indirect speech:
options: He said what a beautiful scene it is.
He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful scene.
He exclaimed what a beautiful scene it was.
He told that it is a very beautiful scene.
mcqs.explanation: Exclamatory 'What a ...' becomes 'exclaimed that ... a very ...'.

mcqs.q: Father said to me, "Work hard if you want to succeed." → Indirect speech:
options: Father told me work hard if you want to succeed.
Father advised me to work hard if I wanted to succeed.
Father said that work hard if I want to succeed.

mcqs.q: Each of the boys ___ given a prize.
mcqs.explanation: 'Each of' + plural noun still takes a singular verb: Each of the boys was…

mcqs.q: The news ___ very shocking.
mcqs.explanation: News is uncountable and singular in English grammar — it always takes a singular verb (The news is…).

mcqs.q: One of my friends ___ gone to America.
mcqs.explanation: One of + plural noun → singular verb: One of my friends has gone… The real subject is 'One', not 'friends'.

mcqs.q: The quality of the mangoes ___ good.
mcqs.explanation: The subject is the quality (singular), not 'mangoes'. Prepositional phrases never change agreement.

mcqs.q: Either he or I ___ mistaken.
mcqs.explanation: With either…or / neither…nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject — here 'I', so am.

mcqs.q: A number of students ___ absent today.
mcqs.explanation: A number of = many → plural verb (are). But The number of → singular: The number of students is large.

mcqs.q: Neither of the two answers ___ correct.
mcqs.explanation: Neither of takes a singular verb in formal English: Neither of the two answers is correct.

mcqs.q: Either of the answers ___ correct.
mcqs.explanation: 'Either of' takes singular verb।

mcqs.q: Neither he nor his friends ___ coming.
mcqs.explanation: With 'neither…nor', verb agrees with nearer subject।

mcqs.q: The news ___ shocking.
mcqs.explanation: 'News' is singular despite plural form।

mcqs.q: The committee ___ divided in opinion.
mcqs.explanation: Collective noun takes singular when acting as unit।

mcqs.q: Each boy and each girl ___ a prize.
mcqs.explanation: 'Each…and each…' takes singular verb।

mcqs.q: Neither of the two boys ___ passed.
mcqs.explanation: 'Neither of + plural noun' → singular verb।

mcqs.q: She, not I, ___ responsible.
mcqs.explanation: When subjects joined by 'not', verb agrees with first।

mcqs.q: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ present.
mcqs.explanation: With 'neither…nor' verb agrees with nearer subject (teachers — plural).

mcqs.q: He gave me some useful ___.
mcqs.explanation: "Information" is uncountable; it has no plural and takes no article.

mcqs.q: The scissors ___ on the table.
mcqs.explanation: Pair nouns like scissors are always plural and take a plural verb.

mcqs.q: The plural of "criterion" is —
mcqs.explanation: "Criterion" is a Greek-origin noun; its plural is "criteria".

mcqs.q: The news ___ quite encouraging.
mcqs.explanation: "News" looks plural but is always singular.

mcqs.q: The plural of "passer-by" is —
mcqs.explanation: In compound nouns the plural -s goes to the principal (first) word: passers-by.

mcqs.q: Find the part with the error: "The sceneries (A) of Kashmir (B) are (C) very (D) charming."
mcqs.explanation: "Scenery" is uncountable — "The scenery of Kashmir is very charming."

mcqs.q: There ___ many species of birds in this sanctuary.
mcqs.explanation: "Species" is same in form for both numbers; with "many" it is plural here.

mcqs.q: The police ___ investigating the case.
mcqs.explanation: Police is a plural-only noun (like people, cattle) and takes a plural verb — The police are investigating.

mcqs.q: He played two ___ in the match.
mcqs.explanation: Innings is same in singular and plural: one innings, two innings. 'Inning' (American style) is wrong in SSC English.

mcqs.q: The shepherd has fifty ___.
mcqs.explanation: Sheep (and deer, fish, series, species) does not change in the plural — one sheep, fifty sheep.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct plural: criterion
mcqs.explanation: Latin/Greek plurals: criterion → criteria, phenomenon → phenomena, datum → data, analysis → analyses, crisis → crises.

mcqs.q: I bought two ___ yesterday.
mcqs.explanation: Pair nouns — trousers, scissors, spectacles, jeans — are always plural: two trousers, a pair of trousers.

mcqs.q: The ___ are grazing in the field.
mcqs.explanation: 'Cattle' has no plural -s।

mcqs.q: He gave me a lot of ___.
mcqs.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable।

mcqs.q: She bought three ___ of socks.
mcqs.explanation: 'Pair' pluralises normally।

mcqs.q: The ___ were grazing in the field.
mcqs.explanation: 'Sheep' has same singular and plural।

mcqs.q: He gave me some ___ on planting trees.
mcqs.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable।

mcqs.q: He has many ___.
mcqs.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable; use 'pieces of luggage'।

mcqs.q: The ___ of this book are interesting.
mcqs.explanation: 'Contents' (table of contents) pluralises normally।

mcqs.q: Several ___ gathered to protest.
mcqs.explanation: 'People' is already plural (of person)।

mcqs.q: He bought two ___ of bread.
mcqs.explanation: 'Loaf' → 'loaves' (f → ves)।

mcqs.q: The ___ are playing in the garden.
mcqs.explanation: 'Child' → 'children' (irregular)।

mcqs.q: Two ___ stood at the gate.
mcqs.explanation: 'Policeman' → 'policemen' (irregular)।

mcqs.q: The ___ of the books are torn.
mcqs.explanation: 'Leaf' → 'leaves' (f → ves)।

mcqs.q: He gave her a piece of ___.
mcqs.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable; use 'a piece of'।

mcqs.q: The ___ are migrating south for winter.
mcqs.explanation: 'Goose' → 'geese' (irregular)।

mcqs.q: The team ___ well today.
mcqs.explanation: Team as unit → singular verb।

mcqs.q: He has two ___-in-law.
mcqs.explanation: 'Brother-in-law' → 'brothers-in-law'।

mcqs.q: Many ___ took part in the rally.
mcqs.explanation: 'Woman' → 'women' (irregular)।

mcqs.q: His ___ are well-known.
mcqs.explanation: 'Analysis' → 'analyses' (Greek plural)।

mcqs.q: He bought two ___ of milk.
mcqs.explanation: 'Litre' (countable unit) pluralises normally।

mcqs.q: The ___ are very useful.
mcqs.explanation: 'Tooth' → 'teeth' (irregular)।

mcqs.q: The ___ in the sky are dark.
mcqs.explanation: 'Cloud' pluralises normally।

mcqs.q: These ___ are reading.
mcqs.explanation: 'Boy' (consonant + y) → 'boys'।

mcqs.q: Five ___ flew away.
mcqs.explanation: 'Sparrow' (consonant + y, but ends in -ow) → 'sparrows'।

mcqs.q: He gave me three ___ of paper.
mcqs.explanation: 'Piece' pluralises normally।

mcqs.q: The plural of 'datum' is:
mcqs.explanation: 'Datum' → 'data' (Latin plural).

mcqs.q: Between you and ___, this plan will never work.
mcqs.explanation: The preposition "between" always takes the objective case — "me".

mcqs.q: Ram and ___ are going to the market.
mcqs.explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject, so the subjective case "I" is required.

mcqs.q: Let you and ___ finish this work today.
mcqs.explanation: After "let", the objective case is used: let you and me.

mcqs.q: The book ___ you gave me yesterday is very interesting.
mcqs.explanation: "Book" is a thing; the relative pronoun for things is "which" (or "that").

mcqs.q: Find the part with the error: "He is one (A) of those officers (B) who has (C) never (D) told a lie."
mcqs.explanation: "Who" refers to the plural "officers", so it takes a plural verb — "who have never told a lie".

mcqs.q: He is taller than ___, but I am stronger.
mcqs.explanation: "Than" is a conjunction; the subject form "I" is used in formal English (taller than I am).

mcqs.q: The two sisters love ___ dearly.
mcqs.explanation: For exactly two persons, "each other" is the correct reciprocal pronoun.

mcqs.q: She is taller than ___.
mcqs.explanation: An implied verb follows 'than' — taller than I (am) — so the subject form I is correct in formal English.

mcqs.q: It was he who ___ responsible for the loss.
mcqs.explanation: After 'It is/was + he/she/I + who', the verb agrees with that pronoun: It was he who was responsible.

mcqs.q: One should do ___ duty honestly.
mcqs.explanation: One is followed by one's in standard British English (which SSC follows): One should do one's duty.

mcqs.q: The two sisters love ___ .
mcqs.explanation: Each other is used for two persons; one another for more than two. Here only two sisters are involved.

mcqs.q: ___ do you want to meet?
mcqs.explanation: The blank receives the action of 'meet' — object case Whom. Test: answer 'I want to meet him' (object form).

mcqs.q: Let you and ___ finish the work.
mcqs.explanation: 'Let' takes the object case: Let you and me finish… Similarly: between you and me.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct order:
options: I, you and he have won the match.
You, he and I have won the match.
He, you and I have won the match.
You, I and he have won the match.
mcqs.explanation: For a happy/shared credit the polite order is 231 — You, he and I. (Order 312 — I, you and he — is used while accepting blame.)

mcqs.q: Each of the boys must do ___ duty.
mcqs.explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' takes singular 'his'।

mcqs.q: It is ___ who broke the window.
mcqs.explanation: Pronoun after 'It is' takes subjective form।

mcqs.q: He and ___ are good friends.
mcqs.explanation: Pronouns joined by 'and' → subjective form when subject।

mcqs.q: She did it ___.
mcqs.explanation: Reflexive pronoun 'herself'।

mcqs.q: ___ of the two boys is taller?
mcqs.explanation: Choice between two → 'which'।

mcqs.q: I have ___ to help me.
mcqs.explanation: 'Nobody' is correct indefinite pronoun।

mcqs.q: This is the boy ___ I taught last year.
mcqs.explanation: Object relative pronoun 'whom'।

mcqs.q: He is taller than ___.
mcqs.explanation: After 'than' subjective 'I' (formal) is acceptable।

mcqs.q: Each girl must bring ___ own pen.
mcqs.explanation: 'Each girl' → singular 'her'।

mcqs.q: The dog wags ___ tail.
mcqs.explanation: 'Its' is possessive (no apostrophe)।

mcqs.q: He cut ___ while shaving.
mcqs.explanation: Reflexive 'himself'।

mcqs.q: The book is ___.
mcqs.explanation: Possessive 'ours' = 'our book'।

mcqs.q: There is ___ in the room; it is empty.
mcqs.explanation: Negative statement → 'nobody'।

mcqs.q: One should love ___ country.
mcqs.explanation: After 'one' → 'one's' is formal correct।

mcqs.q: I myself did it. Here 'myself' is ___.
mcqs.explanation: 'Myself' used for emphasis is emphatic।

mcqs.q: They enjoyed ___ at the picnic.
mcqs.explanation: 'Themselves' is correct reflexive plural।

mcqs.q: He is superior ___ all his colleagues in honesty.
mcqs.explanation: Latin comparatives like "superior" always take the preposition "to".

mcqs.q: Find the part with the error: "This is (A) the more (B) interesting (C) book I have ever read (D)."
options: D — book I have ever read
mcqs.explanation: "Ever read" signals a superlative — "the most interesting book".

mcqs.q: She sings ___ than her sister.
mcqs.explanation: "Than" demands the comparative form of the adverb well — "better".

mcqs.q: I have ___ money, so I can lend you some.
mcqs.explanation: "A little" = some (positive sense); "little" would mean almost none, contradicting the sentence.

mcqs.q: There were ___ students in the class today than yesterday.
mcqs.explanation: "Students" is countable, so the countable comparative "fewer" is correct.

mcqs.q: Work ___ if you want to succeed.
mcqs.explanation: "Hard" (मेहनत से) is the adverb here; "hardly" means "almost not".

mcqs.explanation: OSASCOMP: Opinion (lovely) → Colour (blue) → Material (silk).

mcqs.q: Mumbai is ___ city in India.
mcqs.explanation: A superlative needs 'the': Mumbai is the biggest city in India. Without 'the', a comparative with 'than any other city' would be needed.

mcqs.q: He is senior ___ me by three years.
mcqs.explanation: Latin comparatives — senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, preferable — are followed by to, never 'than'.

mcqs.q: The higher you climb, ___ it gets.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel comparative: The + comparative, the + comparative — The higher you climb, the cooler it gets.

mcqs.q: The soup tastes ___ .
mcqs.explanation: After the sense verb taste, an adjective describes the subject: The soup tastes delicious.

mcqs.q: He ___ ever misses his classes.
mcqs.explanation: Hardly = almost never (negative adverb). 'Hard' is the adverb of effort: He works hard. The two are not interchangeable.

mcqs.q: Choose the correctly ordered phrase:
mcqs.explanation: Adjective order: size → colour → material (origin) → noun: a big brown leather bag.

mcqs.q: He is the ___ boy in the class.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative for one-of-many।

mcqs.q: She sings ___ than her sister.
mcqs.explanation: Comparative for two।

mcqs.q: He runs ___.
mcqs.explanation: 'Fast' has same adj/adv form।

mcqs.q: This is the ___ interesting book I have ever read.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative of long adjective = 'most + adj'।

mcqs.q: He spoke ___ to me.
mcqs.explanation: Adverb modifies verb → ends in -ly।

mcqs.q: She is as ___ as her mother.
mcqs.explanation: 'As…as' takes positive degree।

mcqs.q: He is ___ in class.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative takes 'the'।

mcqs.q: This is the ___ book I have ever read.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative of long adj = 'most + adj'।

mcqs.q: He arrived ___ than expected.
mcqs.explanation: 'Late' → comparative 'later'।

mcqs.q: He is a ___ man.
mcqs.explanation: Adjective ends in -able; passive sense।

mcqs.q: She is ___ than her brother.
mcqs.explanation: Comparative 'older' for general comparison; 'elder' for family only।

mcqs.q: He works ___ here.
mcqs.explanation: 'Hard' = diligent; 'hardly' = scarcely।

mcqs.q: This is the ___ day of the year.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative of 'long' = 'longest'।

mcqs.q: She is ___ to me.
mcqs.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to' (not 'than')।

mcqs.q: This book is ___ than that one.
mcqs.explanation: Comparative of 'good' = 'better'।

mcqs.q: She is the ___ singer in the group.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative of 'good' = 'best'।

mcqs.q: He is ___ than I expected.
mcqs.explanation: Two-syllable adj → 'more + adj'।

mcqs.q: She is the ___ girl in the class.
mcqs.explanation: Superlative for one of many — 'prettiest'.

mcqs.q: He is ___ honest man, respected by all.
mcqs.explanation: "Honest" begins with a silent h — a vowel sound "o", so "an" is used.

mcqs.q: She has done ___ MBA from a reputed institute.
mcqs.explanation: MBA is pronounced "em-be-a", starting with a vowel sound → "an".

mcqs.q: He is ___ European by birth.
mcqs.explanation: "European" starts with the consonant sound "yu", so "a" is used.

mcqs.q: ___ sun rises in ___ east.
mcqs.explanation: Unique objects (the sun) and directions (the east) take "the".

mcqs.q: He plays ___ cricket every evening and ___ flute at night.
mcqs.explanation: Sports take no article; musical instruments take "the" (the flute).

mcqs.q: One who knows everything:
mcqs.explanation: Omniscient = knowing everything (omni = all + scire = to know). Omnipotent = all-powerful; omnipresent = present everywhere; omnivorous = eating everything.

mcqs.q: One who loves mankind:
mcqs.explanation: Philanthropist (phil = love + anthropos = mankind). Misanthrope hates mankind; philatelist collects stamps.

mcqs.q: Government by the officials:
mcqs.explanation: Bureaucracy = rule by officials (bureau = office). Democracy = by the people; monarchy = by a king/queen; plutocracy = by the wealthy.

mcqs.q: That which cannot be corrected:
mcqs.explanation: Incorrigible = that cannot be corrected (used for habits). Incredible = unbelievable; inevitable = unavoidable; illegible = unreadable.

mcqs.q: Fear of heights:
mcqs.explanation: Acrophobia = fear of heights. Hydrophobia = fear of water; claustrophobia = fear of closed spaces; xenophobia = fear of foreigners.

mcqs.q: A place where bees are kept:
mcqs.explanation: Apiary = bee-house. Aviary = bird-house; aquarium = fish-tank; granary = grain-store.

mcqs.q: Story of a person's life written by himself/herself:
mcqs.explanation: Autobiography = self-written life story (auto = self). Biography is written by another person.

mcqs.q: Study of birds:
mcqs.explanation: Ornithology = study of birds. Entomology = insects; astronomy = stars; anthropology = mankind.

mcqs.q: One who loves books:
mcqs.explanation: Bibliophile = book lover।

mcqs.q: A place where birds are kept:
mcqs.explanation: Aviary = bird enclosure।

mcqs.q: One who eats everything:
mcqs.explanation: Omnivore = eats everything।

mcqs.q: A government by the rich:
mcqs.explanation: Plutocracy = rule by wealthy।

mcqs.q: That cannot be corrected:
mcqs.explanation: Incorrigible = cannot be corrected।

mcqs.q: A speech made without preparation:
mcqs.explanation: Impromptu = without preparation (preferred for unprepared speech)।

mcqs.q: Study of insects:
mcqs.explanation: Entomology = insect study।

mcqs.q: A person who writes dictionaries:
mcqs.explanation: Lexicographer = dictionary writer।

mcqs.q: One who does not believe in God:
mcqs.explanation: Atheist = no belief in God।

mcqs.q: One who believes in many gods:
mcqs.explanation: Polytheist = many gods।

mcqs.q: A medicine that counteracts poison:
mcqs.explanation: Antidote = counteracts poison।

mcqs.q: One who walks in sleep:
mcqs.explanation: Somnambulist = sleep walker।

mcqs.q: That which cannot be avoided:
mcqs.explanation: Inevitable = unavoidable।

mcqs.q: A word that reads the same backward:
mcqs.explanation: Palindrome = same backward/forward।

mcqs.q: One who loves his country:
mcqs.explanation: Patriot = lover of country।

mcqs.q: A person who cannot read or write:
mcqs.explanation: Illiterate = cannot read/write।

mcqs.q: A list of books for reading:
mcqs.explanation: Bibliography = list of books।

mcqs.q: That cannot be read:
mcqs.explanation: Illegible = unreadable।

mcqs.q: One who collects coins:
mcqs.explanation: Numismatist = coin collector।

mcqs.explanation: To smell a rat = to suspect that something is wrong or dishonest.

mcqs.q: He was asked to stop ___ and come straight to the point.

mcqs.q: "To face the music" means —
mcqs.explanation: To face the music = to accept criticism or punishment for one's actions.

mcqs.q: "Once in a blue moon" means —
mcqs.explanation: The idiom means something that happens very rarely.

mcqs.q: "A white elephant" is —
mcqs.explanation: A white elephant is a burdensome possession — expensive to keep but of little use.

mcqs.q: "To turn a deaf ear to" means to —
mcqs.explanation: To turn a deaf ear = to refuse to listen; to ignore advice or requests.

mcqs.q: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Reading is an outdated habit in the digital age
Daily, attentive reading builds the mind steadily like a compounding investment
Social media platforms should be banned for students
Only a formal university course can build true knowledge
mcqs.explanation: The passage presents daily reading as a discipline whose benefits 'compound like savings', with each book adding to what the next one builds upon — the core argument of the passage.
mcqs.passage:
Passage 1 — The Reading Habit

Few habits enrich the mind as quietly as reading does. A reader who spends thirty minutes a day with a book consumes nearly twenty books a year — an entire university course gathered at the cost of a daily bus ride. Reading is not passive entertainment; it is a disciplined conversation with the finest minds of every century. Unlike the swift scroll of a social feed, a book demands patience: it withholds its rewards until attention is paid, and precisely for that reason it trains attention itself. Studies of comprehension repeatedly find that readers of long-form text outperform screen-skimmers in reasoning, vocabulary and empathy. The benefit compounds like savings: each book quietly deposits context, analogy and perspective that the next book draws upon. In an age of infinite notifications, the deliberate reader performs a small act of resistance — choosing depth over noise, one page at a time.

mcqs.q: The author calls reading 'a disciplined conversation' because —
options: books reply to the reader's spoken questions
reading a book demands patient, sustained attention to another mind's ideas
every book is written in dialogue form
readers must discuss books in groups to understand them
mcqs.explanation: The phrase is explained in the passage itself: a book 'demands patience' and 'withholds its rewards until attention is paid' — i.e., the reader must discipline attention to engage with the writer's ideas.

mcqs.q: Why do fresh graduates, according to the passage, often prefer returning to the office?
options: They dislike working from home because of slow internet
They miss the informal mentoring and culture-learning that physical presence provides
Their homes are too crowded for work
Companies force junior staff to attend daily
mcqs.explanation: The passage says newcomers 'learned its culture through screens, missing the informal mentoring that hallways provide' — which explains why fresh graduates asked to return.
mcqs.passage:
Passage 2 — Redesigning the Workplace

When offices closed in 2020, millions of workers discovered that the commute could be replaced by a corridor. Remote work promised freedom, and for many it delivered: hours once lost to travel returned to family, fitness and sleep. Yet the same freedom carried hidden costs. Newcomers to a company learned its culture through screens, missing the informal mentoring that hallways provide. Surveys soon revealed a split — experienced employees preferred home, while fresh graduates often asked to return. The wisest employers stopped treating the question as either-or and adopted hybrid models: offices for collaboration and onboarding, home for deep, uninterrupted work. The lesson generalises beyond the workplace. Any technology that removes friction also removes the accidental encounters where ideas and relationships grow. Progress, therefore, is not the abolition of the office but the deliberate redesign of when physical presence is worth its price.

options: offices became smaller after the pandemic

mcqs.explanation: It is an ironic image: the long daily commute shrank to the short walk ('a corridor') from bed or kitchen to the home workstation.

mcqs.q: What is the unit digit of 7^95?
mcqs.explanation: Cycle of 7 is (7, 9, 3, 1) repeating every 4. 95 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 3, so the 3rd digit of the cycle = 3.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest number that must be added to 1056 to make it exactly divisible by 23?
Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
The sum of the first 50 natural numbers is —
The remainder when 2^96 is divided by 7 is —
mcqs.explanation: 2³ = 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7). 2^96 = (2³)³² ≡ 1³² = 1, so the remainder is 1.

mcqs.q: A number n leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7. What is the remainder when n² is divided by 7?
mcqs.explanation: n = 7k + 3, so n² = 49k² + 42k + 9 ≡ 9 ≡ 2 (mod 7). Remainder = 2.

mcqs.q: How many numbers between 100 and 300 (both inclusive) are divisible by 9?
The unit digit of 7¹⁰⁵ is:
mcqs.explanation: Powers of 7 end in the cycle (7, 9, 3, 1) of period 4. 105 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 1, so the unit digit is the 1st member = 7.

mcqs.q: The least number by which 72 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square:
mcqs.explanation: 72 = 2³ × 3². For a perfect square every prime needs an even power; 2 appears 3 times, so multiply by 2 (72×2 = 144 = 12²).
