mcqs.q: Pointing to a man, Rita said, "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is the man related to Rita?
mcqs.explanation: Grandfather's only son = Rita's father; the son of Rita's father is Rita's brother.

mcqs.q: A is B's brother, B is C's sister, C is D's father. How is A related to D?
mcqs.explanation: B and C are siblings; A, being B's brother, is also C's brother. Since C is D's father, A is D's paternal uncle.

mcqs.q: Introducing a boy, a girl said, "He is the son of my father's only son." How is the boy related to the girl?
mcqs.explanation: The girl's father's only son is the girl's brother; her brother's son is the girl's nephew.

mcqs.q: A + B means A is the father of B; A × B means A is the brother of B. In "A + B × C", how is A related to C?
mcqs.explanation: A is the father of B; B and C are siblings (B × C), so A is the father of C as well.

mcqs.q: X is the mother of Y and Z. If Z is the husband of W, how is W related to X?
mcqs.explanation: Z is X's son; the wife of X's son is X's daughter-in-law.

mcqs.q: A is the father of B, but B is not the son of A. How is B related to A?
mcqs.explanation: B is A's child but not the son — so B must be A's daughter.

mcqs.q: Pointing to a lady, Vikas said, "She is the only daughter of my mother's only son." How is the lady related to Vikas? (Vikas is male)
mcqs.explanation: Vikas's mother's only son is Vikas himself; his only daughter is his own daughter.

mcqs.q: A is the father of B. B is the mother of C. How is A related to C?
mcqs.explanation: A → B (father) → C: A is C's grandfather.

mcqs.q: Pointing to a photograph, Ram said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is she related to Ram?
mcqs.explanation: Grandfather's ONLY son = Ram's father; his daughter = Ram's sister.

mcqs.q: 'He is the son of my father's sister.' The speaker is describing his:
mcqs.explanation: Father's sister = aunt; her son = the speaker's cousin.

mcqs.q: P is the brother of Q. R is the mother of Q. S is the father of R. How is S related to P?
mcqs.explanation: S → R → (P, Q): S is the mother's father = grandfather (maternal).

mcqs.q: X is the wife of Y. Y is the son of Z. Z is the wife of W. How is W related to X?
mcqs.explanation: W → Z → Y → X: W is the husband of Y's mother = Y's father = X's father-in-law.

mcqs.q: 'My mother's brother's only sister's son' — who is he to me?
mcqs.explanation: Mother's brother's only sister = my mother; her son = myself.

mcqs.q: If P + Q means P is the father of Q, and P − Q means P is the wife of Q, then P + Q − R means:
options: P is the father of R
P is the father-in-law of R
P is the grandfather of R
P is the uncle of R
mcqs.explanation: P + Q → P is Q's father; Q − R → Q is R's wife. So P is the father-in-law of R.

mcqs.q: Pointing to a man, Reena said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to Reena?
mcqs.explanation: Reena's mother's only daughter = Reena herself. So the man's mother is Reena → man is Reena's son. Wait, re-read: 'his mother is the only daughter of MY mother' → his mother = Reena. So man is Reena's son. Answer: Son.

mcqs.q: If A is brother of B, B is sister of C, and C is father of D, how is A related to D?
mcqs.explanation: A-B-C are siblings (A brother, B sister, C brother). C's child D → A is paternal uncle of D.

mcqs.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my father.' How is the man related to the woman?
mcqs.explanation: Woman's father's only daughter = woman herself. So man's wife = woman → man is woman's husband.

mcqs.q: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?
mcqs.explanation: A's mother = C; C's father = D → D is A's maternal grandfather → A is D's granddaughter.

mcqs.q: Pointing to a photograph, Raju said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to Raju?
mcqs.explanation: Raju's grandfather's only son = Raju's father. Father's daughter = Raju's sister (or Raju herself if no other sister). Assuming photograph not of Raju → sister.

mcqs.q: P is the father of Q and R. Q is the son of P. How is R related to P?
mcqs.explanation: P is father of Q (son) and R. R could be son or daughter — gender not specified.

mcqs.q: If 'A + B' means A is the mother of B; 'A - B' means A is the brother of B; 'A × B' means A is the father of B, then how is P related to R in 'P + Q × R'?
mcqs.explanation: P + Q means P is Q's mother; Q × R means Q is R's father → P is R's grandmother.

mcqs.q: A man said to a woman, 'Your mother's husband's sister is my aunt.' How is the woman related to the man?
mcqs.explanation: Woman's mother's husband = woman's father; father's sister = aunt. If father's sister is man's aunt → they share father's sister → man and woman are siblings (brother-sister) or cousins.

mcqs.q: If Reeta is the sister of Sita, and Sita is the mother of Gita, how is Reeta related to Gita?
mcqs.explanation: Reeta is sister of Gita's mother → maternal aunt (Mausi).

mcqs.q: A man looks at a photo and says, 'I have no brother, but that man's father is my father's son.' How is the man in photo related to him?
mcqs.explanation: No brother → 'my father's son' = himself. So that man's father = the man himself → man in photo is his son.

mcqs.q: Anil introduces Rohit as the son of the only brother of his father's wife. How is Rohit related to Anil?
mcqs.explanation: Anil's father's wife = Anil's mother; mother's brother = maternal uncle (Mama); uncle's son = cousin.

mcqs.q: A woman introduces a man as 'he is the son of the only daughter of my grandfather.' How is the man related to the woman?
mcqs.explanation: Woman's grandfather's only daughter = woman's mother; mother's son = brother (or woman herself if son) → brother.

mcqs.q: A is B's brother, B is C's mother. How is A related to C?
mcqs.explanation: A is brother of C's mother → maternal uncle (Mama).

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 3 km, turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start?
mcqs.explanation: North 5 km and South 5 km cancel; the net movement is 3 km East.

mcqs.q: If South-East becomes North and North-East becomes West, then West becomes:
mcqs.explanation: SE (135°) → N (0°) means a −135° rotation; West 270° − 135° = 135° = South-East.

mcqs.q: A man facing North turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise, then 90° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
One morning, Sneha walks towards the rising sun and then turns left. Which direction is she facing now?
mcqs.explanation: Rising sun = East, so she faces East; a left turn from East (90° anticlockwise) = North.

mcqs.q: A person walks 10 m South, turns left and walks 10 m, turns left again and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 5 m. How far is he from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Path: S10 → E10 (left of South) → N10 (left of East) → E5 (right of North). Net: 10−10 = 0 N-S; East 10+5 = 15 m East.

mcqs.q: P is 5 m North of Q. R is 5 m South of Q. S is 5 m East of R. In which direction is S with respect to P?
mcqs.explanation: Take Q as origin: P(0,5), R(0,−5), S(5,−5). S is East and South of P → South-East.

mcqs.q: Kishan walks 4 m North and then 3 m East. What is the shortest distance between his start and end points?
mcqs.explanation: √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 m — the classic 3-4-5 right triangle.

mcqs.q: A person facing North turns right by 90°. Now he faces:
mcqs.explanation: Right of North = East.

mcqs.q: In the evening, the shadow of the sun falls towards:
mcqs.explanation: Evening sun sets in the West → shadows fall East. (Morning: shadows west.)

mcqs.q: A man walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 3 km, turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the start?
mcqs.explanation: 5 N + 3 E + 5 S: the north and south legs cancel → net displacement = 3 km East.

mcqs.q: Going 3 km East and then 4 km North, the straight-line distance from the start is:
mcqs.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km (3-4-5 Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: Which direction lies exactly between North and East?
mcqs.explanation: Between North and East = North-East.

mcqs.q: A man facing West turns 90° clockwise. He now faces:
mcqs.explanation: Clockwise from West: W → N. (Anti-clockwise would give South.)

mcqs.q: A man walks 5 km North, turns right, walks 3 km, turns right, walks 5 km. How far is he from start?
mcqs.explanation: After walking pattern, net displacement is 3 km East.

mcqs.q: A person facing North turns right 90°. Now he faces:
mcqs.explanation: Right of North = East.

mcqs.q: If South becomes North-East, then what does West become?
mcqs.explanation: 180° rotation; South→North-East means West→East.

mcqs.q: A person walks 7 km North, then 24 km East, then 7 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 24 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 7 km towards North, then turns right and walks 24 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(7² + 24²) = 25 km.

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 6 km towards North, then turns right and walks 8 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(6² + 8²) = 10 km.

mcqs.q: A man walks 5 km towards East, then turns left and walks 12 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 9 km towards North, then turns right and walks 12 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

mcqs.q: A man walks 8 km towards East, then turns left and walks 15 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 3 km towards North, then turns right and walks 4 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 8 km towards North, then turns right and walks 15 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(8² + 15²) = 17 km.

mcqs.q: A man walks 7 km towards East, then turns left and walks 24 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(7² + 24²) = √625 = 25 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: A person walks 6 km North, then 8 km East, then 6 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 8 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: Ravi walks 5 km towards North, then turns right and walks 12 km towards East. What is his shortest distance from the start?
mcqs.explanation: Shortest distance = straight line = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km.

mcqs.q: A man walks 3 km towards East, then turns left and walks 4 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: A person walks 5 km North, then 12 km East, then 5 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 12 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: A person walks 3 km North, then 4 km East, then 3 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 4 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: A man walks 9 km towards East, then turns left and walks 12 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: A man walks 6 km towards East, then turns left and walks 8 km towards North. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular: distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km (Pythagoras triple).

mcqs.q: A person walks 8 km North, then 15 km East, then 8 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 15 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: A person walks 9 km North, then 12 km East, then 9 km South. How far is he from the starting point?
mcqs.explanation: The North and South walks cancel; only the 12 km Eastward displacement remains.

mcqs.q: A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing North. C sits exactly in the middle. E sits immediately left of C. B sits immediately right of A. Who is at the extreme right end?
mcqs.explanation: C = 3, E = 2; the A-B pair fits only seats 4-5, so A = 4, B = 5 and D = 1. Extreme right = B.

mcqs.q: Six persons sit around a circular table facing the centre. If P is to the immediate right of Q, then P is to the ______ of Q.
mcqs.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right-hand side is the anticlockwise neighbour.

mcqs.q: Five persons A, B, C, D, E live on floors 1-5 (1 = ground). C lives on the top floor, D lives on floor 2, and B lives immediately above A. Who lives on floor 3?
mcqs.explanation: C = 5, D = 2; the B-above-A block fits only floors 3-4, so A = 3, B = 4, E = 1.

mcqs.q: Four friends W, X, Y, Z sit at four corners of a square table facing the centre. Y sits diagonally opposite W, and X sits to the immediate right of W. Who sits to the immediate left of Y?
mcqs.explanation: Seat W=1 clockwise. Immediate right of W (facing centre) = anticlockwise → X = seat 4. Y opposite W = seat 3, Z = seat 2. Immediate left of Y = clockwise next = seat 4 = X.

mcqs.q: In a row of 19 students facing North, A is 7th from the left end and B is 9th from the right end. They interchange seats. How many students now sit between A and B?
mcqs.explanation: B is at seat 19 − 9 + 1 = 11 from left; A is at seat 7. After the swap only occupants change. Between seats 7 and 11 = 3 students.

mcqs.q: Among five friends, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is shorter than B. E is taller than C. Who is the tallest?
mcqs.explanation: Chaining the clues: E > C > A > B > D. Hence E is the tallest.

mcqs.q: Seven friends sit in a row facing North. M sits exactly in the middle. N sits immediately to the left of M, and O sits at the extreme right. How many people sit between N and O?
mcqs.explanation: Seats 1-7; M = 4, N = 3, O = 7. People between seats 3 and 7 = seats 4, 5, 6 = 3 people.

mcqs.q: Five friends P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north. R is in the middle. P is at the extreme left. Q sits between P and R. S sits immediately right of R. Who is at the extreme right?
mcqs.explanation: Positions: P(1), Q(2), R(3), S(4) → T must be at position 5 (extreme right).

mcqs.q: In a stack of books: the Red book is above the Blue book but below the Green book; the Yellow book is at the top; the Black book is below the Blue book. Which book is at the BOTTOM?
mcqs.explanation: Order top→bottom: Yellow > Green > Red > Blue > Black → bottom = Black.

mcqs.q: If the day before yesterday was Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
mcqs.explanation: Day before yesterday = Monday → today = Wednesday → day after tomorrow = Friday.

mcqs.q: Ram is taller than Shyam but shorter than Mohan. Sohan is taller than Mohan. Who is the tallest?
mcqs.explanation: Chain: Sohan > Mohan > Ram > Shyam → tallest = Sohan.

mcqs.q: P, Q, R, S have exams on Monday–Thursday (one each). P's exam is immediately before Q's. R's exam is on Thursday. S's exam is NOT on Monday. Whose exam is on Monday?
mcqs.explanation: R = Thursday. Pair P-Q must be Mon-Tue (S cannot take Monday) → S = Wednesday. Monday = P.

mcqs.q: In a class, Mohan ranks 7th from the top and 28th from the bottom. The total number of students is:
mcqs.explanation: Total = 7 + 28 − 1 = 34 (Mohan is counted twice).

mcqs.q: 5 friends sit in a row: A, B, C, D, E. A is to left of C, but right of B. D is to right of E but left of B. Who is at extreme left?
mcqs.explanation: Order: E, D, B, A, C — extreme left is E.

mcqs.q: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing north. C sits in the middle. A sits to the immediate left of C. B sits at the extreme right. E sits immediately next to A (between A and D). Who is at the extreme left?
mcqs.explanation: Order left→right: E, A, C, D, B — E is at the extreme left.

mcqs.q: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a row facing north. P is at the extreme left. Q is second from the right. S sits between P and Q. T sits immediately right of P. U sits immediately left of Q. Who is the fourth from the left?
mcqs.explanation: Order: P, T, S, R, U, Q — the fourth from the left is R.

mcqs.q: In a row of students facing north, Rahul is 8th from the left and 17th from the right. How many students are in the row?
Six friends A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a circular table facing the centre, in clockwise order: B, A, C, D, E, F. Who sits opposite A?
mcqs.explanation: In a six-seat circle opposite seats lie three apart: B-D, A-E, C-F — so A faces E.

mcqs.q: Five boxes of colours — red, blue, green, yellow, white — are stacked one above the other. Green is at the bottom. Red is immediately above green. Blue is at the top and white is immediately below blue. Which box is in the middle (third) position?
mcqs.explanation: Bottom to top: Green, Red, Yellow, White, Blue — the middle box is Yellow.

mcqs.q: In a row of children facing north, Riya is 12th from the left. If she shifts 4 places to the right, she becomes 9th from the right. How many children are in the row?
mcqs.explanation: New position from left = 16; total = 16 + 9 − 1 = 24.

mcqs.q: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, M, N, O watch a movie in a row. P is at the extreme left with R between P and N. M sits exactly in the middle, N is immediately left of M, and O is immediately right of M. Q is at the extreme right and S sits between O and Q. Who sits immediately right of O?
mcqs.explanation: Order: P, R, N, M, O, S, Q — the person immediately right of O is S.

mcqs.q: Four towers P, Q, R, S are built in a row facing east. R is between P and Q. S is immediately west of Q. P is the westernmost? If P is west of R and S is immediately west of Q, which tower is easternmost?
mcqs.explanation: West→east: P, R, S, Q — so Q is the easternmost.

mcqs.q: In a class photo, boys and girls stand in one line: G1, B1, G2, B2, G3, B3, G4, B4 from left. Which position does B3 occupy from the left?
mcqs.explanation: B3 is the 6th person from the left in the given line.

mcqs.q: Five cars — red, black, white, green, silver — are parked in a row. Black is the leftmost and white is immediately right of black. Silver is not adjacent to white, and green is not adjacent to silver. Which car is parked third from the left?
mcqs.explanation: Forced order left to right: black, white, green, red, silver — the third car is green.

mcqs.q: Six coins are arranged in a row: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 paise. Which coin is third from the right end?
mcqs.explanation: From the right: 50, 20, 10, 5, 2, 1 — the third from the right is the 5-paise coin.

mcqs.q: A, B, C, D sit around a square table, one per side, facing the centre. A faces D? If A is opposite C, and B is to the immediate right of A (clockwise), who is opposite B?
mcqs.explanation: Order clockwise A, B, C, D: B sits opposite D.

mcqs.q: In a queue, V is 14th from the front and W is 17th from the back. If there are 4 persons between them and V is ahead of W, what is the total number of persons in the queue?
Five students P, Q, R, S, T have heights such that Q is taller than P but shorter than R. S is shorter than P. T is taller than R. Who is the second tallest?
mcqs.explanation: Order (tall→short): T, R, Q, P, S — the second tallest is R.

mcqs.q: Six flats are in a row numbered 1-6 (left to right). The doctor lives in flat 3. The engineer lives immediately right of the doctor. The teacher lives in flat 1. The lawyer lives in flat 6. The remaining two flats (2 and 5) have the painter and the writer; the writer lives left of the painter. Who lives in flat 2?
mcqs.explanation: Engineer is in flat 4; flats 2 and 5 hold painter/writer, and writer must be left of painter → flat 2 = writer.

mcqs.q: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Conclusion: Some roses fade quickly.
options: Either conclusion or its negative follows
mcqs.explanation: The "fade quickly" overlap may cover only non-rose flowers, so a possible diagram exists where no rose fades quickly — it does not follow.

mcqs.q: Statements: All A are B. All B are C. Which conclusion definitely follows?
mcqs.explanation: A sits inside B, and B inside C, so A is inside C; converting "All A are C" gives "Some C are A".

mcqs.q: Statements: Some cats are rats. All rats are bats. Conclusion I: Some cats are bats. Conclusion II: All bats are rats.
mcqs.explanation: The cat-rat overlap lies inside bats, so some cats are bats (I follows). Bats also include non-rats, so II fails.

mcqs.q: In a group of 50 people, 25 drink tea, 30 drink coffee and 12 drink both. How many drink neither?
mcqs.explanation: At least one = 25 + 30 − 12 = 43; neither = 50 − 43 = 7.

mcqs.q: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship: Engineer, Human, Dog?
options: Engineer circle inside Human circle; both separate from Dog
mcqs.explanation: Every engineer is a human (subset), while dogs are separate from humans entirely.

mcqs.q: Statements: No pen is a pencil. All pencils are erasers. Conclusion: Some erasers are not pens.
mcqs.explanation: All pencils are erasers, and no pencil is a pen — so those erasers (the pencils) are definitely not pens.

mcqs.q: Of 100 students, 45 play cricket, 40 play football and 20 play both. How many play exactly one game?
mcqs.explanation: At least one = 45 + 40 − 20 = 65; exactly one = 65 − 20 = 45.

mcqs.q: Statements: Some doctors are fathers. All fathers are men. Conclusion?
mcqs.explanation: Those doctors who are fathers are definitely men → 'some doctors are men' follows; its converse 'some men are doctors' also follows. But NOT 'all doctors are men'.

mcqs.q: 'Some doctors are women' is best represented by:
mcqs.explanation: 'Some A are B' → overlapping circles with a common region.

mcqs.q: In a class of 60, 35 like tea and 30 like coffee; every student likes at least one. The MINIMUM number who like both:
mcqs.explanation: Minimum both = 35 + 30 − 60 = 5.

mcqs.q: If some cats are dogs and some dogs are rats, then:
options: None of these can be definitely concluded
mcqs.explanation: No definite conclusion can be drawn from 'some A are B' and 'some B are C'.

mcqs.q: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Therefore:
mcqs.explanation: 'All A are B' and 'Some B are C' → no definite conclusion about A and C.

mcqs.q: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. Some flowers are roses. Which follows?
mcqs.explanation: "Some flowers are red" does not link roses to red; but "All roses are flowers" makes "Some flowers are roses" valid.

mcqs.q: Statements: All cats are animals. No animal is a plant. Conclusion: No cat is a plant. Does it follow?
mcqs.explanation: Cats ⊂ animals and animals ∩ plants = ∅, so no cat can be a plant.

mcqs.q: Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are pencils. Conclusion: Some books are pencils.
options: Only if all books are pens
mcqs.explanation: The overlapping "books∩pens" region lies entirely inside pencils, so some books are definitely pencils.

mcqs.q: Statements: All A are B. All B are C. Conclusion: All A are C.
mcqs.explanation: Transitive containment gives A ⊂ B ⊂ C, hence all A are C.

mcqs.q: Statements: No bird is a fish. All sparrows are birds. Conclusion: No sparrow is a fish.
mcqs.explanation: Sparrows are a subset of birds, and birds are fully excluded from fish.

mcqs.q: Statements: Some doctors are singers. All singers are dancers. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are dancers. II. All dancers are singers.
mcqs.explanation: Doctors∩Singers ⊂ Dancers, so I follows; II reverses "All singers are dancers" and is invalid.

mcqs.q: Statements: All keys are locks. Some locks are doors. Conclusions: I. Some keys are doors. II. Some locks are keys.
mcqs.explanation: "Some locks are doors" need not touch keys, so I fails; II follows from All keys are locks.

mcqs.q: Statements: Every student is clever. Some clever people are rich. Conclusion: Some students are rich.
mcqs.explanation: The rich-clever overlap may exclude students entirely — conclusion is only possible, not definite.

mcqs.q: Statements: All cups are plates. No plate is a bowl. Conclusion: No cup is a bowl.
mcqs.explanation: Cups ⊂ plates and plates ∩ bowls = ∅, hence no cup is a bowl.

mcqs.q: Statements: Some mangoes are sweet. All sweet things are tasty. Conclusions: I. Some mangoes are tasty. II. All tasty things are sweet.
mcqs.explanation: Sweet mangoes are tasty (I follows); II is an invalid conversion of "All sweet are tasty".

mcqs.q: Statements: All chairs are tables. Some tables are desks. Conclusion: Some chairs are desks.
mcqs.explanation: The desks overlap may lie only outside the chairs — the conclusion is not definite.

mcqs.q: Statements: No pen is a pencil. All pencils are erasers. Conclusions: I. Some erasers are pencils. II. No pen is an eraser.
mcqs.explanation: I follows from All pencils are erasers; II is wrong because pens may still overlap erasers outside pencils.

mcqs.q: Statements: All laptops are computers. All computers are machines. Conclusion: All laptops are machines.
mcqs.explanation: Chain of two universal positives: Laptops ⊂ Computers ⊂ Machines.

mcqs.q: Statements: Some poets are writers. Some writers are editors. Conclusion: Some poets are editors.
mcqs.explanation: The two "some" statements do not guarantee the same writers overlap both sets.

mcqs.q: Statements: All houses are buildings. All buildings need paint. Conclusion: All houses need paint.
mcqs.explanation: Houses ⊂ Buildings ⊂ (things that need paint), so all houses need paint.

mcqs.q: If + means ×, − means ÷, × means − and ÷ means +, then 9 − 3 + 2 ÷ 4 × 6 = ?
In a row of 60 students, Mohan is 24th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
mcqs.explanation: Position from right = 60 − 24 + 1 = 37.

mcqs.q: Ravi is 11th from either end of a row. How many students are in the row?
P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is heavier than R. T is lighter than Q. Who is the heaviest?
mcqs.explanation: Chaining: S > R > P > Q > T — S tops the chain.

mcqs.q: If − means ×, × means +, + means ÷ and ÷ means −, then 10 + 5 × 8 − 2 ÷ 4 = ?
In a class, Anil ranks 9th from the top and 38th from the bottom. How many students are in the class?
mcqs.explanation: Total = 9 + 38 − 1 = 46 students.

mcqs.q: Suresh is 7 ranks ahead of Ramesh in a class of 39 students. If Ramesh ranks 15th from the last, what is Suresh's rank from the top?
mcqs.explanation: Ramesh from top = 39 − 15 + 1 = 25; Suresh is 7 ranks ahead → 25 − 7 = 18.

mcqs.q: If '+' means '×', '−' means '÷', '×' means '−' and '÷' means '+', then 8 + 6 − 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = ?
If A > B and B > C, then which is definitely true?
mcqs.explanation: Transitivity: A > B > C ⇒ A > C.

mcqs.q: If '−' means '+' and '+' means '−', then 10 − 5 + 3 = ?
mcqs.explanation: New expression: 10 + 5 − 3 = 12.

mcqs.q: If the signs '×' and '+' are interchanged, the value of 4 + 6 × 2 becomes:
mcqs.explanation: After interchange: 4 × 6 + 2 = 24 + 2 = 26.

mcqs.q: In a queue of students, Ram is 11th from the front and 27th from the back. Total students in the queue:
In a row of 45 students, X is 16th from the left and Y is 11th from the right. How many students sit between X and Y?
In a row of 30 girls, R is 9th from the right. What is her position from the left?
mcqs.explanation: From left = 30 − 9 + 1 = 22.

mcqs.q: If "+" means "×", "−" means "÷", "×" means "+", "÷" means "−", then 8 + 2 − 4 × 6 ÷ 3 = ?
A is heavier than B but lighter than C. D is heavier than C. E is lighter than B. Who is the heaviest?
mcqs.explanation: Chain: E < B < A < C < D — D is the heaviest.

mcqs.q: In a queue of 60 people, M is 25th from the front. What is M's position from the back?
mcqs.explanation: From back = 60 − 25 + 1 = 36.

mcqs.q: P is 7th from either end of a row. How many people are in the row?
If "×" means "−", "+" means "×", "−" means "÷" and "÷" means "+", then 15 − 3 + 4 × 2 ÷ 5 = ?
mcqs.explanation: Substituting symbols: 15 ÷ 3 × 4 − 2 + 5 = 20 − 2 + 5 = 23.

mcqs.q: Among five friends, T is taller than only S. R is taller than Q but shorter than P. Who is the tallest?
mcqs.explanation: Only S is below T; R < P with Q between them — P tops the order P, R, Q, T, S.

mcqs.q: In a row of trees, one tree is 7th from either end. How many trees are in the row?
If A ÷ B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; then in "P ÷ Q − R", how is P related to R?
mcqs.explanation: P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother, so P is also R's mother.

mcqs.q: Ravi ranks 13th in a class of 42. What is his rank from the last?
mcqs.explanation: From last = 42 − 13 + 1 = 30.

mcqs.q: If "−" means "added to", "+" means "divided by", "×" means "subtracted from" and "÷" means "multiplied by", then 20 + 4 ÷ 5 × 3 − 6 = ?
mcqs.explanation: Substituting symbols: 20 ÷ 4 × 5 − 3 + 6 = 25 − 3 + 6 = 28.

mcqs.q: Five girls took part in a race. J finished before K but behind L. M finished after K but before N. Who finished second?
mcqs.explanation: Order of finish: L, J, K, M, N — the second finisher is J.

mcqs.q: Who is the current (2024-25) Chief Justice of India?
mcqs.explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna became 51st CJI on 11 November 2024 — succeeded Justice D.Y. Chandrachud.

mcqs.q: Who is the current President of India (2024-25)?
mcqs.explanation: Droupadi Murmu is the 15th President of India (since 25 July 2022) — first tribal and second woman President.

mcqs.q: Who is the current (2024-25) Vice President of India?
mcqs.explanation: Jagdeep Dhankhar is the Vice President of India (since 11 August 2022) — succeeded M. Venkaiah Naidu.

mcqs.q: Who became the World Bank President in June 2023?
mcqs.explanation: Ajay Banga (Indian-American) became World Bank President on 2 June 2023 — succeeded David Malpass.

mcqs.q: Narendra Modi became Prime Minister of India for the 3rd term on:
mcqs.explanation: Narendra Modi became PM for 3rd consecutive term on 9 June 2024 — BJP-led NDA won 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

mcqs.q: Who became the UK Prime Minister in July 2024?
mcqs.explanation: Keir Starmer (Labour Party) became UK PM on 5 July 2024 — Labour won after 14 years; succeeded Rishi Sunak.

mcqs.q: Who is the current Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India?
mcqs.explanation: General Anil Chauhan (retired) became 2nd CDS on 30 September 2022 — succeeded General Bipin Rawat (died in helicopter crash on 8 Dec 2021).

mcqs.q: Who is the current UN Secretary-General?
mcqs.explanation: António Guterres (former PM of Portugal) is UN Secretary-General since 1 January 2017; re-elected for 2nd term (till 2026).

mcqs.q: Who is the current Chief Election Commissioner of India (2024-25)?
mcqs.explanation: Rajiv Kumar became Chief Election Commissioner on 15 May 2022 — succeeded Sushil Chandra.

mcqs.q: Droupadi Murmu is the ___ President of India.
mcqs.explanation: Droupadi Murmu is the 15th President of India (since 25 July 2022).

mcqs.q: Who is the current (2024-25) IMF Managing Director?
mcqs.explanation: Kristalina Georgieva (Bulgarian) is IMF MD since 1 October 2019 — succeeded Christine Lagarde.

mcqs.q: Who is the current (2024-25) WHO Director-General?
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Ethiopian) is WHO Director-General since 1 July 2017 — first African to hold the post.

mcqs.q: Who is the current (2024-25) Governor of RBI?
mcqs.explanation: Shaktikanta Das is RBI Governor since 12 December 2018 — succeeded Urjit Patel.

mcqs.q: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud retired as CJI on:
mcqs.explanation: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud retired on 10 November 2024 (turned 65); succeeded by Justice Sanjiv Khanna on 11 November 2024.

mcqs.q: Who is the current Chief Justice of India as of November 2024?
mcqs.explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna became 51st CJI on 11 November 2024.

mcqs.q: Which country became the 32nd member of NATO in March 2024?
mcqs.explanation: Sweden joined NATO on 7 March 2024, ending 200 years of neutrality; Finland had joined in April 2023.

mcqs.q: Atal Setu, India's longest sea bridge, is located in which city?
mcqs.explanation: The Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (Atal Setu, ~21.8 km) connecting Sewri to Nhava Sheva was inaugurated in January 2024.

mcqs.q: Which state's legislature first passed a Uniform Civil Code law in India?
mcqs.explanation: The Uttarakhand Assembly passed the UCC in February 2024 — the first state to legislate it.

mcqs.q: The Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty was launched at which summit?
mcqs.explanation: Brazil's G20 presidency (Rio de Janeiro, Nov 2024) launched the Global Alliance Against Hunger & Poverty.

mcqs.q: The total solar eclipse of April 2024 was mainly visible over —
mcqs.explanation: The "Great North American Eclipse" of 8 April 2024 swept from Mexico through the USA to Canada.

mcqs.q: Which South Asian leader resigned and left the country in August 2024 amid mass protests?
mcqs.explanation: Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigned on 5 August 2024 after student quota protests and flew to India.

mcqs.q: Belarus was admitted as a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation at the 2024 summit held in —
mcqs.explanation: At the Astana SCO Summit (July 2024), Belarus became the 10th full member.

mcqs.q: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed on Moon's south pole on:
mcqs.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram lander + Pragyan rover) landed on Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023 — 23 August is now National Space Day.

mcqs.q: India became which country to land on Moon's south pole?
mcqs.explanation: India became the FIRST country to land on Moon's south pole, and 4th country to land on Moon (after USA, USSR, China).

mcqs.q: G20 Summit 2023 was held in:
mcqs.explanation: G20 Summit 2023 was held in New Delhi on 9-10 September 2023 — theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'.

mcqs.q: The theme of India's G20 presidency was:
mcqs.explanation: G20 2023 theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future) — Sanskrit phrase from Maha Upanishad.

mcqs.q: Paris Olympics 2024 was held from:
mcqs.explanation: Paris Olympics 2024: 26 July to 11 August 2024; opening ceremony on Seine river — first time ever.

mcqs.q: Who won India's silver medal at Paris Olympics 2024?
mcqs.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won silver in javelin throw at Paris Olympics 2024 — Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem won gold.

mcqs.q: How many medals did India win at Paris Paralympics 2024?
mcqs.explanation: India won 29 medals at Paris Paralympics 2024 — 7 gold, 9 silver, 13 bronze; best-ever performance.

mcqs.q: Who won the 2024 US Presidential elections?
mcqs.explanation: Donald Trump (Republican) defeated Kamala Harris (Democrat) on 5 November 2024; 2nd term starts 20 January 2025.

mcqs.q: BRICS 2024 summit was held in which city?
mcqs.explanation: BRICS 2024 summit — Kazan, Russia (22-24 October 2024); Egypt, Iran, UAE, Ethiopia joined as new members.

mcqs.q: National Space Day in India is celebrated on:
mcqs.explanation: 23 August declared as National Space Day in 2023 — to commemorate Chandrayaan-3's landing on Moon's south pole.

mcqs.q: Narendra Modi became PM for the 3rd consecutive term on:
mcqs.explanation: Narendra Modi took oath as PM for 3rd consecutive term on 9 June 2024 — NDA won 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

mcqs.q: National Sports Day is observed on:
mcqs.explanation: National Sports Day — 29 August — birthday of Major Dhyan Chand (hockey legend, 'Hockey Wizard').

mcqs.q: Which city hosted the G20 Summit 2023?
mcqs.explanation: New Delhi hosted G20 Summit 2023 (9-10 September 2023) — first time India hosted G20 summit.

mcqs.q: Operation Sindoor, launched by India in May 2025, targeted —
options: piracy in the Gulf of Aden
mcqs.explanation: After the Pahalgam attack (22 April 2025), India struck nine terror sites in Pakistan/PoK in the early hours of 7 May 2025.

mcqs.q: The Ram Mandir consecration (Pran Pratishtha) in Ayodhya took place on —
mcqs.explanation: The Pran Pratishtha ceremony led by PM Modi was held on 22 January 2024.

mcqs.q: Atal Setu, India's longest sea bridge (21.8 km), connects —
mcqs.explanation: The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL), inaugurated January 2024, links Sewri (Mumbai) to Nhava Sheva (Navi Mumbai).

mcqs.q: In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, which alliance formed the government?
mcqs.explanation: The BJP-led NDA won 240+ seats and formed the government (PM Modi's third term) in June 2024.

mcqs.q: India won how many medals at the Paris Olympics 2024?
mcqs.explanation: India won 6 medals — Manu Bhaker's two bronzes, Neeraj Chopra's silver, and bronzes in hockey, swap shooting and wrestling.

mcqs.q: GST 2.0 (September 2025) rationalised slabs mainly into —
mcqs.explanation: From 22 September 2025, GST moved to a two-slab 5%/18% structure with a 40% rate for sin/luxury goods.

mcqs.q: "Maratha Military Landscapes" was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2025 — India's —
mcqs.explanation: The 12-component Maratha Military Landscapes became India's 44th World Heritage property in July 2025.

mcqs.q: The "Moidams" of Assam, inscribed by UNESCO in 2024, are —
options: royal burial mounds of the Ahom dynasty
mcqs.explanation: The Moidams at Charaideo, burial mounds of Ahom royals, became India's 43rd World Heritage Site in July 2024.

mcqs.q: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS in June 2025 as part of which mission?
mcqs.explanation: IAF officer Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian on the ISS and second Indian in space via Axiom-4.

mcqs.q: The Navi Mumbai International Airport began operations in —
mcqs.explanation: NMIA, built by Adani group, was inaugurated on 8 October 2025, easing Mumbai airport congestion.

mcqs.q: "Ladki Bahin" Yojana, paying ₹1,500/month to eligible women, is a scheme of —
mcqs.explanation: The Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme was launched by Maharashtra in 2024.

mcqs.q: India's first indigenous aircraft INS Vikrant was —
mcqs.explanation: INS Vikrant (IAC-1), India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, was commissioned in September 2022.

mcqs.q: The 2025 IPCC-style global assessment COP30 was hosted by —
mcqs.explanation: COP30, the UN climate conference, was held in Belém (Amazon region), Brazil in November 2025.

mcqs.q: India hosted the G20 Summit in 2023 in New Delhi; the 2024 G20 Summit was hosted by —
mcqs.explanation: Brazil hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in Rio de Janeiro in November 2024.

mcqs.q: Vizhinjam International Seaport, India's first deepwater mother port, is in —
mcqs.explanation: The Adani-built Vizhinjam port near Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala) received its first mother ship in 2024.

mcqs.q: The Pran Pratishtha ceremony of Ram Lalla at Ayodhya was held on —
mcqs.explanation: The consecration took place on 22 January 2024, led by PM Modi.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was NOT awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024?
mcqs.explanation: The 2024 list had 5 names — Thakur, Advani, Rao, Charan Singh, Swaminathan; Mulayam Singh Yadav was not on it.

mcqs.q: The Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bonds scheme on —
mcqs.explanation: On 15 Feb 2024 a 5-judge Constitution bench unanimously held electoral bonds unconstitutional.

mcqs.q: India's first underwater metro section, opened in March 2024, runs under which river?
mcqs.explanation: Kolkata Metro's Howrah Maidan-Esplanade stretch passes beneath the Hooghly river.

mcqs.q: XPoSat, launched on 1 January 2024, is designed to study —
options: Polarisation of X-rays from cosmic sources
mcqs.explanation: XPoSat (PSLV-C58) measures X-ray polarisation from black holes, neutron stars etc. — only the world's 2nd such mission after NASA's IXPE.

mcqs.q: Which country became the 5th nation to soft-land a spacecraft on the Moon in January 2024?
mcqs.explanation: JAXA's SLIM lander touched down on 19 January 2024, making Japan the 5th moon-landing nation.

mcqs.q: Who was the chief guest at India's 75th Republic Day parade (26 Jan 2024)?
mcqs.explanation: French President Emmanuel Macron was the chief guest; the parade had an all-women tri-services contingent dimension.

mcqs.explanation: 2024 पद्म पुरस्कार: ५ पद्मविभूषण, १७ पद्मभूषण, ११० पद्मश्री — एकूण 132 पुरस्कार.
