mcqs.q: The Earth is approximately how many billion years old?
mcqs.explanation: Earth is approximately 4.54 billion years old — determined by radiometric dating of meteorites and oldest rocks.

mcqs.q: The outermost layer of the Earth is called:
mcqs.explanation: Crust is the outermost layer — thickness 5-70 km; continental (granite, 30-70 km) and oceanic (basalt, 5-10 km).

mcqs.q: The inner core of the Earth is made up of:
mcqs.explanation: Inner core (5100-6371 km) — solid iron-nickel; outer core (2900-5100 km) — liquid iron-nickel (causes magnetic field).

mcqs.q: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
mcqs.explanation: Ozone layer is in stratosphere (12-50 km altitude) — protects Earth from UV radiation.

mcqs.q: Which layer of the atmosphere is closest to the Earth?
mcqs.explanation: Troposphere (0-12 km) — closest layer; contains most weather phenomena; temperature decreases with altitude.

mcqs.q: The Earth's atmosphere contains approximately what percentage of oxygen?
mcqs.explanation: Atmosphere composition: 78% Nitrogen, 21% Oxygen, 1% other gases (argon, CO2, neon, helium, etc.).

mcqs.q: The largest lithospheric plate is:
mcqs.explanation: Pacific Plate (~103 million sq km) — largest lithospheric plate; entirely oceanic.

mcqs.q: Earth's circumference at the equator is approximately:
mcqs.explanation: Earth's equatorial circumference: 40,075 km; polar circumference: 40,008 km — slight equatorial bulge.

mcqs.q: Who first measured the Earth's circumference?
mcqs.explanation: Eratosthenes (Greek, ~240 BCE) measured Earth's circumference using shadows at Syene and Alexandria — very accurate.

mcqs.q: Earth's magnetic field is generated by:
mcqs.explanation: Liquid outer core (2900-5100 km) — convective motion of liquid iron-nickel generates Earth's magnetic field.

mcqs.q: How many major lithospheric plates are there?
mcqs.explanation: There are 7 major lithospheric plates — Pacific, North American, South American, Eurasian, African, Antarctic, Indo-Australian.

mcqs.q: The temperature of the inner core is approximately:
mcqs.explanation: Inner core temperature ~6000°C — as hot as Sun's surface; despite this, iron is solid due to extreme pressure.

mcqs.q: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is:
mcqs.explanation: Nitrogen — 78% of Earth's atmosphere; Oxygen 21%; Argon 0.93%; CO2 0.04%.

mcqs.q: The ozone layer protects Earth from:
mcqs.explanation: Ozone (O3) layer absorbs harmful UV radiation from Sun — protects life on Earth.

mcqs.q: The Northern Plains of India have been formed by the deposits of —
mcqs.explanation: The Indus-Ganga-Brahmaputra river systems deposited alluvium over millions of years forming the world's largest alluvial plain.

mcqs.q: Anaimudi, the highest peak of South India, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Anaimudi (2,695 m) rises in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala.

mcqs.q: Which soil is best suited for cotton cultivation?
mcqs.explanation: Black regur soil of the Deccan Trap retains moisture perfectly, making it ideal for cotton.

mcqs.q: Bhabar plain is characterised by —
options: Porous pebbly soil where streams disappear
mcqs.explanation: In Bhabar (8-16 km wide belt), rivers flowing from the Himalayas disappear into porous pebble-strewn soil.

mcqs.q: India's only active volcano is located on —
mcqs.explanation: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only confirmed active volcano.

mcqs.q: How many physiographic divisions does India have?
mcqs.explanation: India has 6 major physiographic divisions — Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands.

mcqs.q: The Himalayas are approximately how long?
mcqs.explanation: Himalayas stretch ~2500 km east-west — from Indus river (west) to Brahmaputra (east); 150-400 km wide.

mcqs.q: The Greater Himalayas are also called:
mcqs.explanation: Greater Himalayas = Himadri — highest range, avg 6000 m; contains Mt Everest (8848 m), Kangchenjunga (8586 m).

mcqs.q: Which hill stations are located in the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)?
mcqs.explanation: Lesser Himalayas (Himachal, 3700-4500 m) — most popular hill stations: Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling, Manali, Srinagar.

mcqs.q: The Northern Plains of India are formed by the alluvium deposits of which rivers?
mcqs.explanation: Northern Plains — alluvial deposits of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra river systems; covers ~7 lakh sq km; fertile.

mcqs.q: The Peninsular Plateau of India is divided by which river?
mcqs.explanation: Narmada river flows west in rift valley — divides Peninsular Plateau into Central Highlands (north) and Deccan Plateau (south).

mcqs.q: The Thar Desert is mainly located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Thar Desert — mostly in Rajasthan (~200,000 sq km); extends into Pakistan; arid region with low rainfall.

mcqs.q: India's coastline is approximately how long?
mcqs.explanation: India's coastline: 7517 km — mainland: 5422 km; islands: 2095 km.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is India's largest island group?
mcqs.explanation: Andaman & Nicobar Islands (572 islands, 8249 sq km) — India's largest island group; in Bay of Bengal.

mcqs.q: Lakshadweep Islands are located in which sea?
mcqs.explanation: Lakshadweep (36 coral islands) — located in Arabian Sea; off the coast of Kerala.

mcqs.q: The Deccan Plateau was formed by which geological process?
mcqs.explanation: Deccan Plateau formed by volcanic lava flows (Deccan Traps) ~65 million years ago; covers much of south-central India.

mcqs.q: India's total geographical area is approximately:
mcqs.explanation: India's total area: 3.28 million sq km (2.4% of world's area); 7th largest country.

mcqs.q: The Shivalik range is also known as:
mcqs.explanation: Shivalik = Outer Himalaya — youngest and lowest range (900-1200 m); foothills.

mcqs.q: The Malabar Coast is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Malabar Coast — southwestern coast of India (Kerala); known for spices; wet climate.

mcqs.q: The Coromandel Coast is in which part of India?
mcqs.explanation: Coromandel Coast — southeastern coast of India (Tamil Nadu); faces Bay of Bengal.

mcqs.q: The northernmost, highest range of the Himalayas is called —
mcqs.explanation: The Himadri or Greater Himalaya holds the highest peaks with an average height above 6,000 m.

mcqs.q: Duns such as Dehra Dun are located in which Himalayan division?
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal valleys between the Shivaliks and Himachal are called Duns.

mcqs.q: Kanchenjunga, the highest peak of India, lies in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the Sikkim–Nepal border and is India's highest peak.

mcqs.q: Which hill station valley lies between the Lesser Himalayan ranges of Himachal?
mcqs.explanation: Kullu valley lies between the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges of the Lesser Himalaya.

mcqs.q: Nathu La pass is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Nathu La connects Sikkim with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

mcqs.q: The Bhabar belt is characterised by —
options: porous gravel beds where streams disappear
mcqs.explanation: South of the Shiwaliks, the Bhabar is a narrow porous belt of pebbles where rivers vanish underground.

mcqs.q: Bhangar and Khadar are types of —
mcqs.explanation: Bhangar is older alluvium above flood level; Khadar is newer, renewed floodplain alluvium.

mcqs.q: The Aravalli range, one of the world's oldest fold mountains, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: The heavily eroded Aravallis run through Rajasthan, ending near Delhi.

mcqs.q: Anamudi, the highest peak of South India, is in which range?
mcqs.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala's Anaimalai hills is the highest peak south of the Vindhyas.

mcqs.q: Doddabetta, the highest peak of the Nilgiris, is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Doddabetta (2,637 m) lies in Tamil Nadu where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet.

mcqs.q: The Malabar coast corresponds to which present-day states?
mcqs.explanation: The Malabar (western) coast spans Kerala and coastal Karnataka.

mcqs.q: The Coromandel coast is on which side of India?
mcqs.explanation: The Coromandel is the Tamil Nadu portion of the eastern coastal plain.

mcqs.q: Lakshadweep islands are mainly made of —
mcqs.explanation: Lakshadweep is an archipelago of coral atolls in the Arabian Sea.

mcqs.q: India's only active volcano is on which island?
mcqs.explanation: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only confirmed active volcano.

mcqs.q: The northernmost range of the Himalayas is called:
mcqs.explanation: Himadri/Greater Himalaya holds the highest peaks with ice-covered cores.

mcqs.q: The highest mountain peak located entirely within India is:
mcqs.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) on the Sikkim-Nepal border is the highest peak of India; K2 is in PoK region.

mcqs.q: The Aravalli hills are located mainly in:
mcqs.explanation: The Aravalli runs through Rajasthan — among the world's oldest fold mountains.

mcqs.q: The Western Ghats are also known as:
mcqs.explanation: Sahyadri = Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage biodiversity hotspot.

mcqs.q: The Deccan Plateau is made largely of:
mcqs.explanation: Deccan Traps are ancient volcanic basalt flows.

mcqs.q: Mawsynram, one of the wettest places on Earth, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Meghalaya's Khasi hills — Mawsynram/Cherrapunji record extreme rainfall.

mcqs.q: The meeting point of the Western and Eastern Ghats is at the:
mcqs.explanation: The Nilgiris join the two ghats in the south.

mcqs.q: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is known for:
mcqs.explanation: Alluvium deposited by Indus-Ganga rivers makes it India's breadbasket.

mcqs.q: Lakshadweep islands are of which origin?
mcqs.explanation: Lakshadweep is a coral atoll group in the Arabian Sea.

mcqs.q: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills are in:
mcqs.explanation: These hills form Meghalaya's plateau.

mcqs.q: The Peninsular Plateau is a:
options: part of Gondwana landmass — the oldest physiographic division
mcqs.explanation: The peninsula is a remnant of the ancient Gondwana shield.

mcqs.q: The Purvanchal hills include the:
mcqs.explanation: Eastern extension of the Himalaya — Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo hills.

mcqs.q: The highest peak of the Nilgiris is:
mcqs.explanation: Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the Nilgiri summit; Anamudi is highest south of it in the Anaimalai hills.

mcqs.q: K2, the second highest peak of the world, is in:
mcqs.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) stands in the Karakoram range.

mcqs.q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in:
mcqs.explanation: The Thar spans western Rajasthan into Gujarat and Pakistan.

mcqs.q: The Ganga originates from —
mcqs.explanation: The Bhagirathi, source stream of the Ganga, rises from the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh.

mcqs.q: Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in —
mcqs.explanation: In Tibet it is Tsangpo; it becomes Siang/Dihang in Arunachal and Jamuna in Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: Which peninsular river flows westward into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley?
mcqs.explanation: Narmada (and Tapi) flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries, not deltas.

mcqs.q: Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Project on the Narmada is located in Gujarat (Kevadia).

mcqs.q: Which river is called "Dakshin Ganga"?
mcqs.explanation: Godavari is the largest peninsular river and hence called the Ganga of the South.

mcqs.q: Nashik city is situated on the bank of which river?
mcqs.explanation: Nashik lies on the Godavari; Trimbakeshwar, its origin, is also in Nashik district.

mcqs.q: The river Ganga originates from which glacier?
mcqs.explanation: The Bhagirathi, the headstream of the Ganga, rises from the Gangotri glacier.

mcqs.q: At which confluence do Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet to form the Ganga?
mcqs.explanation: At Devprayag the Alaknanda meets the Bhagirathi and the combined river is called the Ganga.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest tributary of the Ganga?
mcqs.explanation: The Yamuna is the longest tributary of the Ganga, joining it at Prayagraj.

mcqs.q: The Yamuna originates from which place?
mcqs.explanation: The Yamuna rises from the Yamunotri glacier in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: Which river is called the "Sorrow of Bihar"?
mcqs.explanation: The Kosi frequently changes course and floods Bihar, earning it the name "Sorrow of Bihar".

mcqs.q: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bengal"?
mcqs.explanation: The Damodar's floods historically devastated Bengal, so it was called the "Sorrow of Bengal".

mcqs.q: The Brahmaputra enters India through which state?
mcqs.explanation: The Brahmaputra enters India as the Dihang (Siang) in Arunachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Majuli, the largest river island in the world, lies in which river?
mcqs.explanation: Majuli island is situated in the Brahmaputra in Assam.

mcqs.q: Which river is called "Dakshin Ganga" (Ganga of the South)?
mcqs.explanation: The Godavari is the longest peninsular river and is called Dakshin Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Godavari rises from which place?
mcqs.explanation: The Godavari rises from Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: The Krishna river originates from which place?
mcqs.explanation: The Krishna rises from Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats.

mcqs.q: The Kaveri river rises from which hills?
mcqs.explanation: The Kaveri rises from Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Which west-flowing river rises from Amarkantak?
mcqs.explanation: The Narmada rises from Amarkantak and flows west into an estuary (no delta).

mcqs.q: The Tapi river rises from which place?
mcqs.explanation: The Tapi rises from Multai in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Hirakud Dam is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud, one of the longest dams in the world, is on the Mahanadi in Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Sundarban Delta is formed by which rivers?
mcqs.explanation: The Ganga and Brahmaputra together form the Sundarbans, the world's largest delta.

mcqs.q: The Chambal river is a tributary of which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Chambal is the chief tributary of the Yamuna, famous for its badlands.

mcqs.q: The Betwa and Ken are tributaries of which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Betwa and Ken join the Yamuna in the Bundelkhand region.

mcqs.q: The Sutlej is a major tributary of which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Sutlej is the easternmost major tributary of the Indus system.

mcqs.q: Jog Falls on the Sharavathi river is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Jog (Gersoppa) Falls on the Sharavathi lies in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Which river flows through Lucknow?
mcqs.explanation: Lucknow is situated on the banks of the Gomti, a Ganga tributary.

mcqs.q: Cuttack city is located on the banks of which river?
mcqs.explanation: Cuttack lies at the apex of the Mahanadi delta in Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Luni river, which is salty in its lower course, flows through which state?
mcqs.explanation: The Luni drains the arid Rajasthan region west of the Aravallis; it turns saline in its lower course.

mcqs.q: Teesta is a major tributary of which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Teesta joins the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh (earlier a direct Ganga tributary).

mcqs.q: Which river forms the Dhuandhar Falls at Bhedaghat?
mcqs.explanation: The Narmada plunges through the marble rocks at Bhedaghat as the Dhuandhar Falls.

mcqs.q: Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam) is the confluence of which three rivers?
mcqs.explanation: The Sangam at Prayagraj is the mythical confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and the invisible Saraswati.

mcqs.q: Which of the following rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea forming NO delta?
mcqs.explanation: West-flowing peninsular rivers like the Narmada and Tapi form estuaries, not deltas.

mcqs.q: The Sivasamudram Falls is on which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Kaveri falls at Sivasamudram in Karnataka, site of one of Asia's earliest hydro projects.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra by volume within India?
mcqs.explanation: The Subansiri, a north-bank tributary, is the largest tributary of the Brahmaputra.

mcqs.q: The Hooghly river, on which Kolkata stands, is a distributary of which river?
mcqs.explanation: The Hooghly is the westernmost distributary of the Ganga in West Bengal.

mcqs.q: The longest river of India is the:
mcqs.explanation: The Ganga (~2,525 km) is India's longest river.

mcqs.q: The Ganga is formed at Devprayag by the confluence of:
mcqs.explanation: Below Devprayag the combined stream is called the Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and:
mcqs.explanation: The combined Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the world's largest.

mcqs.q: Which river is called 'Dakshin Ganga'?
mcqs.explanation: The Godavari is the peninsula's largest river — 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South).

mcqs.q: The Narmada flows into the:
mcqs.explanation: Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys.

mcqs.q: The Hirakud Dam is built on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud (Odisha) is one of the longest dams in the world.

mcqs.q: The Bhakra Nangal project is on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Bhakra Dam stands on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the:
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada serves Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: The Tehri Dam is constructed on the:
mcqs.explanation: Tehri (Uttarakhand) on the Bhagirathi is India's highest dam.

mcqs.q: The Nagarjuna Sagar project is on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna serves Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The river Yamuna joins the Ganga at:
mcqs.explanation: The Sangam at Prayagraj is the Yamuna-Ganga confluence.

mcqs.q: The longest river in the world is the:
mcqs.explanation: The Nile (~6,650 km) is traditionally the longest; the Amazon the largest by volume.

mcqs.q: The Brahmaputra in Tibet is known as the:
mcqs.explanation: Yarlung Tsangpo enters India as the Siang/Dihang, then Brahmaputra.

mcqs.q: The Indus River originates near Lake Mansarovar in:
mcqs.explanation: It rises near Mansarovar, flows through Ladakh into Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Chambal is a tributary of the:
mcqs.explanation: The Chambal flows into the Yamuna near Etawah.

mcqs.q: The fundamental cause of the Indian monsoon is —
options: melting Himalayan snow pushing air southwards
differential heating of land and sea, creating a pressure gradient that draws ocean winds inland
mcqs.explanation: The passage opens with 'unequal heating': land warms faster than the sea, rising air over land pulls in moisture-laden ocean winds — the primary monsoon engine.
mcqs.passage:
Passage — The Arrival of the Monsoon

Every June, India waits for the same invisible guest. The monsoon is born of unequal heating: as summer sun blazes, the subcontinent's land warms far faster than the surrounding seas, and hot air rising over the plains pulls in moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean. The northward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone — the belt where trade winds meet — drags these winds across the equator, where the Earth's spin bends them into the south-westerly monsoon current. Laden with water, the winds strike the Western Ghats and the Meghalaya hills, and orographic uplift squeezes out torrential rain — which is why Cherrapunji and Mawsynram drown while the Deccan plateau behind the Ghats stays comparatively dry, lying in the rain shadow. The normal onset over Kerala around 1 June is followed by a sweeping advance across the country within weeks. The retreat is gentler: from October, the trough moves south and the reversing winds — now north-easterlies — pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and give Tamil Nadu and the Coromandel coast their main rainy season. Two crops, two economies and a billion timetables hang on this rhythm.

mcqs.q: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) influences the monsoon by —
options: its northward shift dragging winds across the equator into the south-westerly current
blocking cyclones from the Bay of Bengal
mcqs.explanation: 'The northward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone... drags these winds across the equator', where the Coriolis effect bends them into the south-westerly monsoon.

options: orographic uplift of monsoon winds striking the Meghalaya hills
mcqs.explanation: Winds 'strike the Western Ghats and the Meghalaya hills, and orographic uplift squeezes out torrential rain' — the mechanism behind Cherrapunji–Mawsynram's record rainfall.

options: in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats

mcqs.q: Which technology was used in the third generation of computers?
mcqs.explanation: Third generation (1964-1971) computers like IBM 360 were built on Integrated Circuits (ICs).

mcqs.q: 1 Terabyte (TB) is equal to —
mcqs.explanation: Storage units scale by 1,024: 1 TB = 1,024 GB, 1 GB = 1,024 MB.

mcqs.q: The first microprocessor, Intel 4004, was developed in —
mcqs.explanation: Intel 4004 (1971) was the first microprocessor and launched the fourth generation of computers.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a non-volatile memory?
mcqs.explanation: ROM retains data without power; RAM, cache and registers all lose content when power is off.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an impact printer?
mcqs.explanation: Dot Matrix printers strike an inked ribbon against paper — they are impact printers; the rest are non-impact.

mcqs.q: MICR technology is mainly used by banks to —
mcqs.explanation: MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) reads the E-13B code line printed at the bottom of cheques.

mcqs.q: A nibble consists of how many bits?
mcqs.explanation: 1 nibble = 4 bits and 1 byte = 8 bits (2 nibbles).

mcqs.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Computer'?
mcqs.explanation: Charles Babbage (1791-1871) — English mathematician; designed Difference Engine and Analytical Engine; called 'Father of the Computer'.

mcqs.q: The first general-purpose electronic computer was:
mcqs.explanation: ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) — completed 1946 at University of Pennsylvania; 30 tons, 1800 sq ft.

mcqs.q: The first commercial computer was:
mcqs.explanation: UNIVAC-1 (Universal Automatic Computer) — delivered to US Census Bureau in 1951; first commercial computer.

mcqs.q: First generation computers used which electronic component?
mcqs.explanation: First generation (1940-1956) — vacuum tubes; large, generated lots of heat, low storage.

mcqs.q: The microprocessor was introduced in which computer generation?
mcqs.explanation: 4th Generation (1971-Present) — microprocessors (VLSI). Intel 4004 (1971) — first microprocessor.

mcqs.q: The first microprocessor was:
mcqs.explanation: Intel 4004 (released November 1971) — first commercial microprocessor; 4-bit, 740 kHz, 2300 transistors.

mcqs.q: The CPU consists of:
mcqs.explanation: CPU = ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) + Control Unit + Registers (small fast memory inside CPU).

mcqs.q: The full form of ALU is:
mcqs.explanation: ALU — Arithmetic Logic Unit; performs arithmetic (+, -, ×, ÷) and logical (AND, OR, NOT) operations.

mcqs.q: RAM is what type of memory?
mcqs.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) — volatile; loses data when power off; main working memory of computer.

mcqs.q: ROM is what type of memory?
mcqs.explanation: ROM (Read Only Memory) — non-volatile; data preserved even when power off; contains BIOS, firmware.

mcqs.q: The fastest computer in the world is:
mcqs.explanation: Supercomputer — fastest type; used for scientific calculations, weather forecasting, simulations.

mcqs.q: India's first supercomputer was:
mcqs.explanation: PARAM 8000 (1991) — India's first supercomputer; developed by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing).

mcqs.q: The full form of CPU is:
mcqs.explanation: CPU — Central Processing Unit; brain of computer; executes instructions.

mcqs.q: Who was the first computer programmer?
mcqs.explanation: Ada Lovelace (1815-1852) — wrote first algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843; considered first computer programmer.

mcqs.q: Which technology was used in the second generation of computers? (हिंदी: द्वितीय पीढ़ी की तकनीक)
mcqs.explanation: Second-generation computers (1956-1963), such as the IBM 1401, replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making them smaller, faster and more reliable.

mcqs.q: Artificial Intelligence and parallel processing are the base technologies of which computer generation?
mcqs.explanation: The fifth generation (present and beyond) is based on AI, parallel processing and ULSI technology — examples include IBM Watson, robotics and expert systems.

mcqs.q: 1 Gigabyte (GB) is equal to — (हिंदी: 1 GB बराबर है)
mcqs.explanation: Storage units grow by a factor of 1,024: 1 GB = 1,024 MB, and 1 MB = 1,024 KB.

mcqs.q: The word 'Bit' is a short form of —
mcqs.explanation: Bit = Binary digit; it is the smallest unit of data and can hold only 0 or 1.

mcqs.q: Which computer language is written purely in 0s and 1s and needs no translation?
mcqs.explanation: Machine language (the first-generation language) uses only binary 0s and 1s, which the CPU executes directly without any translator.

mcqs.q: Assembly language uses short operation codes such as ADD and SUB, which are called —
mcqs.explanation: Assembly language (a second-generation language) uses mnemonic codes like ADD, SUB; an assembler converts them into machine language.

mcqs.q: FORTRAN, developed mainly for scientific and engineering calculations, is an example of a —
mcqs.explanation: FORTRAN (Formula Translation) and COBOL are high-level languages that came into use from the second generation of computers onwards.

mcqs.q: Which input device reads the pencil bubble marks filled on answer sheets?
mcqs.explanation: OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) detects the position of filled bubbles/marks, so it is used for MCQ answer sheets and surveys.

mcqs.q: A touch screen used at an ATM or information kiosk is an example of a device that is — (हिंदी: टच स्क्रीन)
options: Both an input and an output device
mcqs.explanation: A touch screen displays information (output) and also accepts touch input, so it works as both an input and an output device.

mcqs.q: Which output device is used to print large maps, posters and engineering/CAD drawings?
mcqs.explanation: A plotter produces accurate large-format line drawings; note that a scanner is an input device, not an output device.

mcqs.q: Which small, very fast memory is placed between the CPU and RAM?
mcqs.explanation: Cache memory (built with fast SRAM) stores frequently used data so that the CPU does not have to wait for slower RAM.

mcqs.q: Virtual memory is —
options: A part of the hard disk used as extra RAM
The fastest memory inside the CPU
A backup copy of RAM kept on a pen drive
mcqs.explanation: When RAM fills up, the operating system uses a reserved portion of the hard disk as extra (virtual) memory.

mcqs.q: Which memory chip is erased by passing an electrical charge instead of ultraviolet light? (हिंदी: EEPROM)
mcqs.explanation: EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM) is erased electrically; EPROM, by contrast, must be erased with ultraviolet light.

mcqs.q: The computer mouse was invented by —
mcqs.explanation: Douglas C. Engelbart invented the mouse in the 1960s at the Stanford Research Institute (SRI), USA.

mcqs.q: Which of the following produces a HARD copy of a document? (हिंदी: हार्ड कॉपी)
mcqs.explanation: A printer prints output on paper (hard copy); a monitor, speaker and projector all give only soft-copy output.

mcqs.q: The 'brain' of the computer that performs calculations and decision-making is the:
mcqs.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) executes instructions — hence 'brain of the computer'.

mcqs.q: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to:
mcqs.explanation: In binary terms, 1 KB = 2^10 = 1024 bytes.

mcqs.q: Which memory is volatile — its contents are lost when power is switched off?
mcqs.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile; ROM and disks retain data.

mcqs.q: Second-generation computers used:
mcqs.explanation: 2nd generation (1956-63) replaced vacuum tubes with transistors.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of the Computer'?
mcqs.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, the conceptual ancestor of computers.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an input device?
mcqs.explanation: A scanner feeds data INTO the computer; printer, speaker and plotter are output devices.

mcqs.q: The smallest unit of data in a computer is:
mcqs.explanation: A bit (binary digit, 0 or 1) is the smallest unit; 8 bits = 1 byte.

mcqs.q: The ALU of a CPU performs:
mcqs.explanation: ALU = Arithmetic Logic Unit — it does arithmetic (+, −) and logic (AND, OR, comparisons).

mcqs.q: Which language is directly understood by the computer without translation?
mcqs.explanation: Machine language (binary 0s and 1s) needs no translation.

mcqs.q: Fourth-generation computers (1975 onwards) are based on:
mcqs.explanation: 4th generation uses microprocessors — thousands of circuits on one chip (VLSI).

mcqs.q: ROM stands for:
mcqs.explanation: ROM = Read Only Memory; its data is permanent and non-volatile.

mcqs.q: Cache memory is used to:
options: speed up data access for the CPU
mcqs.explanation: Cache is small, very fast memory placed between CPU and RAM to reduce access time.

mcqs.q: The operating system is:
options: system software that manages hardware and programs
mcqs.explanation: The OS (Windows, Linux) is system software managing all resources.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT an operating system?
mcqs.explanation: Oracle is a database management system, not an OS.

mcqs.q: A nibble consists of:
mcqs.explanation: A nibble = 4 bits (half a byte).

mcqs.q: Which number system does a computer work with internally?
mcqs.explanation: Computers use binary — circuits have two states, ON (1) and OFF (0).

mcqs.q: UNIVAC was a computer of the:
mcqs.explanation: UNIVAC-I (1951) was a first-generation commercial computer using vacuum tubes.

mcqs.q: Booting a computer means:
options: starting it and loading the OS into memory
mcqs.explanation: Boot = startup process where the OS is loaded from disk into RAM.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct ascending order of storage units?
USB stands for:
mcqs.explanation: USB = Universal Serial Bus, the standard plug-and-play interface.

mcqs.q: Compiler is a software that:
options: converts high-level language code into machine language
mcqs.explanation: A compiler translates the whole high-level program into machine code at once.

mcqs.q: Which of the following stores data permanently?
mcqs.explanation: Hard disk is secondary (permanent) storage; RAM, cache and registers are volatile.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT system software?
mcqs.explanation: MS Word is application software; Windows/Linux are operating systems and a compiler is a language translator — all system software.

mcqs.q: In MS Word, "Save As" dialog is opened by —
mcqs.explanation: F12 opens Save As; Ctrl + S performs a simple Save.

mcqs.q: A program is translated line by line by a —
mcqs.explanation: An interpreter converts and executes code line by line (e.g., Python); a compiler translates the entire program at once.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used for an absolute cell reference in MS Excel?
mcqs.explanation: $A$1 is an absolute reference; pressing F4 toggles between relative, mixed and absolute references.

mcqs.q: In MS PowerPoint, Ctrl + M is used to —
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl + M inserts a new slide in PowerPoint (in Word, Ctrl + M increases indent — a classic trap).

mcqs.q: The last column of an Excel 2007+ worksheet is —
mcqs.explanation: Excel 2007 onwards has 16,384 columns, the last being column XFD.

mcqs.q: Pressing Shift + F5 in a PowerPoint presentation —
options: Starts the slide show from the current slide
mcqs.explanation: F5 runs the show from the first slide; Shift + F5 runs it from the slide you are currently on.

mcqs.q: MS Word files have the extension:
mcqs.explanation: MS Word — .docx (newer XML format) or .doc (older binary).

mcqs.q: MS Excel files have the extension:
mcqs.explanation: MS Excel — .xlsx (newer); .xls (older).

mcqs.q: MS Access is which type of software?
mcqs.explanation: MS Access — relational database management system (RDBMS); file extension .accdb.

mcqs.q: MS Outlook is used for:
mcqs.explanation: MS Outlook — email client; also calendar, contacts, tasks, notes.

mcqs.q: Windows operating system is developed by:
mcqs.explanation: Microsoft Windows — most popular desktop OS worldwide; first version 20 November 1985.

mcqs.q: Linux operating system was created by:
mcqs.explanation: Linus Torvalds (Finnish student) created Linux kernel in 1991 — open source OS.

mcqs.q: Android OS is owned by which company?
mcqs.explanation: Android — owned by Google; acquired in 2005; based on Linux; first phone HTC Dream (2008).

mcqs.q: Open source software is:
mcqs.explanation: Open source — software whose source code is freely available; can be modified and redistributed. Examples: Linux, Firefox, LibreOffice.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT an application software?
mcqs.explanation: Operating System is system software; rest are application software.

mcqs.q: Antivirus software is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Antivirus — utility software; protects computer from viruses, malware.

mcqs.q: The first version of Windows was released in:
mcqs.explanation: Windows 1.0 — released 20 November 1985 — first graphical user interface (GUI) OS from Microsoft.

mcqs.q: Adobe Photoshop is used for:
mcqs.explanation: Adobe Photoshop — image editing software; industry standard for graphic design.

mcqs.q: MS Word was first released in:
mcqs.explanation: MS Word — first released on 25 October 1983 — first WYSIWYG word processor.

mcqs.q: First Marathi newspaper:
mcqs.explanation: Darpan — first Marathi newspaper (1832) by Balshastri Jambhekar.

mcqs.q: In MS Word, which shortcut key CUTS the selected content?
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl + X cuts (removes) the selection so it can be moved; Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.

mcqs.q: Which alignment makes text even along BOTH the left and right margins in MS Word? (हिंदी: Ctrl+J)
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl + J applies Justify alignment, stretching text evenly between both margins; do not confuse it with Ctrl + E (Centre).

mcqs.q: Which MS Word feature creates the same letter with different names and addresses for many recipients?
mcqs.explanation: Mail Merge combines one standard template with a data list (names/addresses) to produce personalised copies for many recipients.

mcqs.q: The default page margin on all four sides of an MS Word page is — (हिंदी: डिफ़ॉल्ट मार्जिन)
mcqs.explanation: MS Word applies a default margin of 1 inch (2.54 cm) on all four sides of a page.

mcqs.q: In almost all Windows and MS Office programs, which key opens the Help window?
mcqs.explanation: F1 is the universal Help key; F7 runs the spelling check and F5 refreshes (or starts a slide show in PowerPoint).

mcqs.q: The Excel function =MAX(A1:A10) returns the —
mcqs.explanation: =MAX() returns the highest value in the given range, while =MIN() returns the lowest and =AVERAGE() the mean.

mcqs.q: How many rows does an MS Excel 2007 (or later) worksheet contain?
mcqs.explanation: Excel 2007+ worksheets have 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns (last column XFD); older Excel versions had only 65,536 rows.

mcqs.q: Which Excel function returns the current system date?
mcqs.explanation: =TODAY() returns the current date; =NOW() returns the current date along with the time.

mcqs.q: In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl + Home moves the cell cursor to —
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl + Home always jumps to cell A1, the first cell of the worksheet; F5 opens the Go To dialog.

mcqs.q: The keyboard shortcut for AutoSum in MS Excel is —
mcqs.explanation: Alt + = automatically inserts the =SUM() formula over the adjacent cells; F4 toggles absolute references.

mcqs.q: In the cell address B5, the number 5 indicates the —
mcqs.explanation: A cell address is written as column letter + row number, so in B5 the column is B and the row is 5.

mcqs.q: MS PowerPoint 2010 presentations are saved by default with which extension? (हिंदी: PPT एक्सटेंशन)
mcqs.explanation: From Office 2007 onwards, PowerPoint files use the XML-based .pptx extension; older 97-2003 versions used .ppt.

mcqs.q: In MS Word, the shortcut Shift + F7 opens the —
mcqs.explanation: Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus to find synonyms; plain F7 runs the Spelling & Grammar check.

mcqs.q: Which translator converts an assembly language program into machine language?
mcqs.explanation: An assembler translates assembly-language mnemonics into machine code; compilers and interpreters work on high-level languages.

mcqs.q: Restarting an already switched-on computer without turning the power off is called —
mcqs.explanation: Warm boot = restarting while power is on (e.g., the Restart option); cold boot = starting the machine from a fully powered-off state.

mcqs.q: The keyboard shortcut to BOLD text in MS Word is:
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl+B = Bold, Ctrl+I = Italic, Ctrl+U = Underline.

mcqs.q: In MS Excel, which symbol must begin every formula?
mcqs.explanation: Every Excel formula starts with '=' (e.g., =A1+B1).

mcqs.q: The default file extension of an MS Excel 2016 workbook is:
mcqs.explanation: Excel workbooks save as .xlsx; Word uses .docx; PowerPoint uses .pptx.

mcqs.q: Which MS Office application is used to create slide presentations?
mcqs.explanation: PowerPoint creates presentation slides.

mcqs.q: In MS Excel, the function =SUM(A1:A5) will:
options: add all values from A1 to A5
mcqs.explanation: SUM adds the range A1 through A5 inclusive.

mcqs.q: The shortcut for UNDO in MS Word is:
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action; Ctrl+Y is Redo.

mcqs.q: In MS Excel, the intersection of a row and a column is called a:
mcqs.explanation: Each intersection point is a cell, identified by its address like B3.

mcqs.q: Mail Merge in MS Word is used to:
options: send the same letter to many recipients with personalized details
mcqs.explanation: Mail merge combines a template with a data source (names, addresses) for bulk letters.

mcqs.q: Which Excel feature summarizes large data quickly into a report?
mcqs.explanation: Pivot tables group and summarize data dynamically.

mcqs.q: In PowerPoint, a prepared design applied to all slides is called a:
mcqs.explanation: A template provides consistent background, colors and fonts.

mcqs.q: In MS Excel, $A$1 is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Dollar signs before column and row make the reference absolute (fixed on copying).

mcqs.q: The default extension of an MS Word 2016 document is:
mcqs.explanation: Word saves documents as .docx.

mcqs.q: Which Excel function counts only cells containing numbers?
mcqs.explanation: COUNT counts numeric cells; COUNTA counts all non-empty cells.

mcqs.q: To run a slide show from the beginning in PowerPoint, press:
mcqs.explanation: F5 starts the slideshow from the first slide; Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

mcqs.q: In MS Word, the feature that checks spelling as you type marks errors with:
mcqs.explanation: Red wavy = spelling error; green wavy = grammar error.

mcqs.q: The maximum number of columns in an Excel 2016 worksheet is:
mcqs.explanation: Excel 2016 sheets have 16,384 columns (XFD) and 1,048,576 rows.

mcqs.q: Ctrl + Enter in MS Word inserts:
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl+Enter forces a new page (page break).

mcqs.q: Which one is NOT a presentation view in PowerPoint?
mcqs.explanation: Datasheet View belongs to MS Access, not PowerPoint.

mcqs.q: In Excel, to freeze the top row, use:
options: View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row
mcqs.explanation: Freeze Panes keeps the header row visible while scrolling.

mcqs.q: A pre-recorded set of actions in Excel/Word is called a:
mcqs.explanation: A macro records steps and replays them to automate repetitive tasks.

mcqs.q: In Excel, =AVERAGE(10, 20, 30) returns:
Thesaurus in MS Word is used to find:
mcqs.explanation: Shift+F7 opens the thesaurus for word alternatives.

mcqs.q: In which network topology are all computers connected to a single central hub?
mcqs.explanation: Star topology connects every node to a central hub/switch; if the hub fails, the whole network stops.

mcqs.q: The default port number for HTTPS is —
mcqs.explanation: HTTPS (secure HTTP using SSL/TLS) works on port 443; plain HTTP uses port 80.

mcqs.q: FTP stands for —
mcqs.explanation: FTP = File Transfer Protocol, used to transfer files between computers (port 21).

mcqs.q: The largest WAN in the world is —
mcqs.explanation: The Internet is the network of networks — the largest Wide Area Network in existence.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a GUIDED (wired) transmission medium?
mcqs.explanation: Optical fibre is guided media — it transmits light through a physical cable; the others are unguided (wireless).

mcqs.q: The main function of DNS is to —
options: Convert domain names into IP addresses
mcqs.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) is the "phonebook of the Internet" — it maps names like google.com to IP addresses.

mcqs.q: SMTP protocol is used for —
mcqs.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, port 25) SENDS mail; POP3/IMAP receive it.

mcqs.q: The inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW) is:
mcqs.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW in 1989 at CERN (Switzerland); first website 6 August 1991.

mcqs.q: Internet was first introduced in India in:
mcqs.explanation: Internet in India started on 15 August 1995 by VSNL (Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited).

mcqs.q: HTTP stands for:
mcqs.explanation: HTTP — HyperText Transfer Protocol; HTTPS = HTTP + SSL (Secure).

mcqs.q: DNS stands for:
mcqs.explanation: DNS — Domain Name System; converts domain names (google.com) to IP addresses (142.250.x.x).

mcqs.q: Which protocol is used for sending emails?
mcqs.explanation: SMTP — Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (for sending); POP3/IMAP (for receiving).

mcqs.q: Which company owns Google Chrome browser?
mcqs.explanation: Chrome — Google's web browser; released September 2008; ~65% market share.

mcqs.q: Which company was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin?
mcqs.explanation: Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google on 4 September 1998 — while PhD students at Stanford.

mcqs.q: 5G was launched in India on:
mcqs.explanation: 5G launched in India on 1 October 2022 by PM Modi — Indian Mobile Congress.

mcqs.q: The domain .in refers to:
mcqs.explanation: .in — country code top-level domain for India.

mcqs.q: The domain .gov is used for:
mcqs.explanation: .gov — government websites; .com — commercial; .org — organisation; .edu — education.

mcqs.q: FTP stands for:
mcqs.explanation: FTP — File Transfer Protocol; used to upload/download files between client and server.

mcqs.q: Which is the most popular web browser?
mcqs.explanation: Google Chrome — most popular browser (~65% market share); released September 2008.

mcqs.q: The first website was launched on:
mcqs.explanation: First website went live on 6 August 1991 — created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN.

mcqs.q: IPv4 address uses how many bits?
mcqs.explanation: IPv4 — 32-bit address (~4.3 billion addresses); IPv6 — 128-bit address.

mcqs.q: Which is the most popular search engine?
mcqs.explanation: Google — most popular search engine (~90%+ market share); founded 4 September 1998.

mcqs.q: In which network topology is every node connected directly to every other node?
mcqs.explanation: Mesh topology links every node to every other node — it needs n(n-1)/2 links, making it the most reliable but also the costliest topology.

mcqs.q: Which topology connects all computers to a single backbone cable?
options: A single backbone cable shared by all nodes
A central hub with separate cables
Direct links between every pair of nodes
mcqs.explanation: Bus topology attaches all nodes to one backbone cable; a break anywhere in that cable brings the whole network down.

mcqs.q: Which network device sends incoming data ONLY to the intended device using its MAC address?
mcqs.explanation: A switch is an "intelligent hub" that forwards frames using MAC addresses; a dumb hub broadcasts to all ports.

mcqs.q: The full form of MODEM is —
mcqs.explanation: MODEM = MOdulator-DEModulator; it converts digital signals to analog and back for transmission over telephone lines.

mcqs.q: A Bluetooth connection between your mobile and laptop forms which type of network? (हिंदी: PAN)
mcqs.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) covers a few metres around one person — Bluetooth is its classic example.

mcqs.q: Which network device regenerates and amplifies a weak signal to extend the transmission distance?
mcqs.explanation: A repeater boosts/regenerates signals on a line; a gateway instead converts between different protocols.

mcqs.q: Which TCP/IP protocol ensures reliable, ordered delivery of data between computers?
mcqs.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) guarantees reliable, sequenced delivery; IP handles addressing and routing.

mcqs.q: The default port number used by POP3 for receiving e-mail is —
mcqs.explanation: POP3 works on port 110; SMTP (sending mail) uses 25, FTP uses 21 and DNS uses 53.

mcqs.q: The Internet evolved from which experimental network project started in 1969?
mcqs.explanation: ARPANET (1969, US Department of Defence) was the seed of today's Internet; the WWW came later, in 1989.

mcqs.q: URL stands for —
mcqs.explanation: URL = Uniform Resource Locator, the unique address of a web page, e.g., https://www.example.com.

mcqs.q: BSNL, Jio and Airtel, which provide Internet connections to users, are examples of —
mcqs.explanation: An ISP (Internet Service Provider) sells Internet access to users; browsers and search engines are software used after connecting.

mcqs.q: E-mail recipients added to which field remain hidden from all other recipients? (हिंदी: BCC)
mcqs.explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) hides the recipient list; CC (Carbon Copy) recipients are visible to everyone.

mcqs.q: Who sent the first network e-mail in 1971 and popularised the @ symbol in addresses?
mcqs.explanation: Ray Tomlinson sent the first e-mail on ARPANET in 1971 and chose the @ symbol for the user@domain format.

mcqs.q: Which device connects two networks that use DIFFERENT protocols (a "protocol converter")?
mcqs.explanation: A gateway links networks with different protocols; a router connects similar networks and routes by IP address.

mcqs.q: OLX, where individual consumers sell to other consumers, is which e-commerce model? (हिंदी: C2C)
mcqs.explanation: C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer) trades between consumers, as on OLX; B2C is business-to-consumer like Amazon retail.

mcqs.q: HTML is used to:
mcqs.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) structures web pages.

mcqs.q: WWW stands for:
mcqs.explanation: WWW = World Wide Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

mcqs.q: An IP address is:
options: a person's name on the internet
a unique numerical address identifying a device on a network
mcqs.explanation: Every device on a network gets a unique IP (e.g., 192.168.1.1).

mcqs.q: Which of these is a web browser?
mcqs.explanation: Firefox is a browser; Google and Yahoo are search engines/portals; Windows is an OS.

mcqs.q: LAN stands for:
mcqs.explanation: LAN connects devices in a small area like an office or building.

mcqs.q: The device that connects your home network to the internet is a:
mcqs.explanation: A router directs traffic between your local network and the internet.

mcqs.q: HTTPS is more secure than HTTP because it:
mcqs.explanation: HTTPS encrypts communication using SSL/TLS.

mcqs.q: DNS is used to:
options: translate domain names into IP addresses
mcqs.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) converts www.example.com into its IP address.

mcqs.q: Which network type covers the largest geographical area?
mcqs.explanation: WAN (Wide Area Network) spans cities/countries — the internet is the biggest WAN.

mcqs.q: An email address has the format:
mcqs.explanation: Standard format: name@provider.com — '@' separates user from domain.

mcqs.q: ISP stands for:
mcqs.explanation: An ISP provides internet connectivity (e.g., Jio, Airtel, BSNL).

mcqs.q: The protocol used to transfer web pages is:
mcqs.explanation: HTTP/HTTPS fetches web pages; FTP moves files; SMTP/POP3 handle email.

mcqs.q: A modem's main function is:
options: to convert digital signals to analog and vice versa
mcqs.explanation: Modem = MOdulator-DEModulator, converting signals for transmission over phone/cable lines.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a search engine?
mcqs.explanation: Bing is a search engine; Chrome is a browser; Outlook is an email client.

mcqs.q: Bandwidth measures:
options: the data-carrying capacity of a network
mcqs.explanation: Bandwidth = amount of data transferable per second (Mbps).

mcqs.q: TCP/IP is:
options: the basic protocol suite of the internet
mcqs.explanation: TCP/IP defines how data is packetized, addressed and delivered across networks.

mcqs.q: The first page displayed after opening a website is called the:
mcqs.explanation: The home/index page is the entry page of a website.

mcqs.q: Firewall in networking terms is:
options: hardware/software that filters incoming and outgoing traffic
mcqs.explanation: A firewall blocks unauthorized traffic based on security rules.

mcqs.q: Bluetooth is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Bluetooth connects devices over short range — a personal area network.

mcqs.q: Downloading means:
options: sending files from your device to a server
receiving files from a server to your device
mcqs.explanation: Download = receive; upload = send.

mcqs.q: A hyperlink in a web page:
options: clickable text/image that opens another location
mcqs.explanation: Hyperlinks navigate to other pages, files or sections.

mcqs.q: VoIP technology is used for:
options: making voice calls over the internet
mcqs.explanation: VoIP (Voice over IP) carries calls as internet data — used by WhatsApp/Skype calls.

mcqs.q: A malicious program that hides inside a genuine-looking useful software is called —
mcqs.explanation: A Trojan Horse masquerades as legitimate software (like the wooden horse of Troy) and does not self-replicate.

mcqs.q: Which malware can self-replicate and spread over a network WITHOUT needing a host file?
mcqs.explanation: Worms are standalone programs that copy themselves across networks; viruses need a host file.

mcqs.q: A keylogger is an example of —
mcqs.explanation: A keylogger secretly records every keystroke (including passwords), which makes it spyware.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an ASYMMETRIC encryption algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: RSA uses a public-private key pair (asymmetric); AES, DES and Blowfish use a single shared key (symmetric).

mcqs.q: Fraudulent SMS messages containing malicious links are known as —
mcqs.explanation: Smishing = SMS phishing; vishing is via voice calls and phishing via e-mail.

mcqs.q: Which organisation is India's national cyber incident-response agency?
mcqs.explanation: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, 2004) under MeitY handles cyber security incidents.

mcqs.q: A digital signature is created with the sender's —
mcqs.explanation: In asymmetric cryptography, the sender signs with their private key and receivers verify with the sender's public key.

mcqs.q: The first computer virus was:
mcqs.explanation: Creeper (1971) — first computer virus; displayed 'I'm the creeper, catch me if you can'.

mcqs.q: Ransomware ___:
mcqs.explanation: Ransomware — encrypts files, demands ransom (usually cryptocurrency) for decryption key.

mcqs.q: Phishing is:
mcqs.explanation: Phishing — fraudulent emails/websites impersonating legitimate organisations to steal credentials.

mcqs.q: The WannaCry ransomware attack occurred in:
mcqs.explanation: WannaCry ransomware attack (May 2017) — affected 200,000+ computers in 150 countries.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a type of malware?
mcqs.explanation: Firewall — security system, NOT malware; Virus, Worm, Trojan are malware types.

mcqs.q: The Information Technology Act in India was passed in:
mcqs.explanation: IT Act, 2000 — India's first cyber law; amended in 2008.

mcqs.q: CERT-In was established in:
mcqs.explanation: CERT-In — Computer Emergency Response Team India; established 19 November 2002.

mcqs.q: A firewall in computer security is:
options: A security system that monitors and filters network traffic
mcqs.explanation: Firewall — network security system; monitors and filters incoming/outgoing traffic.

mcqs.q: A Trojan is:
mcqs.explanation: Trojan — malware disguised as legitimate software; creates backdoor for attackers.

mcqs.q: DDoS stands for:
mcqs.explanation: DDoS — Distributed Denial of Service attack; overwhelms server with traffic from multiple sources.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a strong password?
mcqs.explanation: Strong password — 8+ characters, mix of uppercase, lowercase, digits, special characters; not a dictionary word.

mcqs.q: VPN stands for:
mcqs.explanation: VPN — Virtual Private Network; creates secure encrypted connection over internet.

mcqs.q: 2FA stands for:
mcqs.explanation: 2FA — Two-Factor Authentication; requires two forms of identity verification (password + OTP/biometric).

mcqs.q: Aadhaar is issued by:
mcqs.explanation: Aadhaar — 12-digit unique identity number; issued by UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India).

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a cyber crime?
mcqs.explanation: Banking online — legitimate activity; Phishing, Hacking, Identity theft — cyber crimes.

mcqs.q: WannaCry ransomware attack year:
mcqs.explanation: WannaCry ransomware — May 2017; 200,000+ computers in 150 countries.

mcqs.q: Which malware needs to attach itself to a host file and spreads when that file is shared? (हिंदी: वायरस)
mcqs.explanation: A virus requires a host file/program and spreads through sharing (pen drives, downloads); worms self-spread over networks without a host.

mcqs.q: Which type of malware floods a screen with unwanted advertisements?
mcqs.explanation: Adware throws unwanted pop-up ads and tracks browsing habits; spyware secretly steals data instead.

mcqs.q: Hackers who test a system's security WITH the owner's permission are called —
mcqs.explanation: White Hat hackers are ethical security professionals; Black Hats break in for malicious gain and Crackers break passwords/copyright protection.

mcqs.q: Which of the following best describes an ANTIVIRUS program?
options: Software that detects, quarantines and removes malware
A browser plug-in for faster downloads
mcqs.explanation: Antivirus software scans for, quarantines and removes malicious programs; compression is done by tools like WinZip.

mcqs.q: Withdrawing cash from an ATM requires both the card and the PIN. This is an example of —
mcqs.explanation: Two-factor authentication (2FA) combines two independent proofs — here, possession (card) and knowledge (PIN), like password + OTP.

mcqs.q: Before entering card details on a shopping site, a secure connection is indicated by — (हिंदी: सुरक्षित वेबसाइट)
options: https:// and a padlock icon in the address bar
A pop-up asking for your OTP
mcqs.explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure over SSL/TLS, port 443) with the padlock icon means the traffic is encrypted; never pay on plain http:// pages.

mcqs.q: An attack that secretly redirects users from a genuine website to a fake one by poisoning DNS entries is called —
mcqs.explanation: Pharming uses DNS poisoning to send users to a fake site even with the correct address; phishing lures through e-mails instead.

mcqs.q: An attacker secretly intercepts messages between two parties who believe they are talking to each other directly. This attack is —
mcqs.explanation: In a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack the intruder sits between sender and receiver; DoS floods a server and spoofing only fakes an identity.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a SYMMETRIC encryption algorithm (same key to encrypt and decrypt)?
mcqs.explanation: AES (like DES) uses one shared secret key — symmetric; RSA, DSA and ECC use public-private key pairs — asymmetric.

mcqs.q: A person who maliciously breaks passwords or copyright protection is called a —
mcqs.explanation: A cracker breaks security for harmful or illegal purposes, unlike ethical (White Hat) hackers who work with permission.

mcqs.q: The national helpline number in India to report cyber fraud and freeze fraudulent transactions is — (हिंदी: साइबर हेल्पलाइन)
mcqs.explanation: Helpline 1930 (and portal cybercrime.gov.in) is used to report online financial fraud quickly so transactions can be frozen.

mcqs.q: Which type of virus infects documents such as MS Word or Excel files?
mcqs.explanation: A macro virus hides in document macros (Word/Excel files); a boot-sector virus infects the disk's boot area instead.

mcqs.q: Malicious code that stays dormant and activates only when a specific event or date occurs is called a —
mcqs.explanation: A logic bomb detonates on a trigger condition (date, event, record count) and is often planted by disgruntled employees.

mcqs.q: A network of malware-infected "zombie" computers remotely controlled to launch DDoS attacks is a —
mcqs.explanation: A botnet is an army of infected machines commanded by an attacker, commonly used for DDoS flooding attacks.

mcqs.q: Under the IT Act 2000, punishment for identity theft is provided under which Section?
mcqs.explanation: Section 66C covers identity theft; 43 is penalty for unauthorised access, 66 for hacking and 67 for obscene electronic content.

mcqs.q: Which is the strongest password?
mcqs.explanation: Strong passwords mix length with upper/lowercase, digits and symbols.

mcqs.q: A firewall protects a computer by:
mcqs.explanation: Firewalls allow or block traffic based on security rules.

mcqs.q: Ransomware is malware that:
mcqs.explanation: Ransomware encrypts the victim's data and demands ransom for release.

mcqs.q: Two-factor authentication (2FA) requires:
options: a password plus a second proof (OTP/biometric)
mcqs.explanation: 2FA adds a second verification step beyond the password.

mcqs.q: HTTPS in a website's address indicates:
mcqs.explanation: The padlock + HTTPS means data is encrypted end-to-end.

mcqs.q: Antivirus software mainly:
mcqs.explanation: Antivirus scans, quarantines and removes malware.

mcqs.q: Spyware is a program that:
mcqs.explanation: Spyware hides in the background, stealing data like keystrokes and logins.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a safe practice on public Wi-Fi?
options: Use a VPN or avoid sensitive logins
mcqs.explanation: Public Wi-Fi can be sniffed; a VPN encrypts your traffic.

mcqs.q: A hacker who breaks into systems to steal data for profit is called a:
mcqs.explanation: Black-hat hackers act maliciously; white-hats test security with permission.

mcqs.q: Backing up data regularly protects against:
options: data loss from attacks or hardware failure
mcqs.explanation: Backups let you restore data after ransomware, theft or disk failure.

mcqs.q: An OTP (One Time Password) is secure because:
options: it expires after single use and a short time
mcqs.explanation: Even if leaked, a used OTP cannot be reused.

mcqs.q: 'Social engineering' attacks exploit:
mcqs.explanation: Attackers manipulate people into revealing secrets or granting access.

mcqs.q: A digital signature is used to:
options: verify the sender's identity and data integrity
mcqs.explanation: Digital signatures confirm authenticity and detect tampering.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of biometric authentication?
mcqs.explanation: Biometrics use body features — fingerprint, face, iris.

mcqs.q: Malware is best defined as:
options: any software designed to harm or exploit systems
mcqs.explanation: Malware covers viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, etc.

mcqs.q: A trojan horse differs from a virus because it:
mcqs.explanation: Trojans do not self-replicate; they trick users by posing as useful programs.

mcqs.q: Incognito/private browsing mode mainly:
options: does not save browsing history on your device
mcqs.explanation: Private mode avoids local history/cookies but does not anonymize you online.

mcqs.q: The practice of updating software regularly is important because updates:
mcqs.explanation: Updates fix vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit.

mcqs.q: Cyberbullying means:
options: using digital means to harass or threaten someone
mcqs.explanation: Cyberbullying is harassment through digital platforms.

mcqs.q: The table lists common keyboard shortcuts. Which shortcut PASTES copied content?
mcqs.explanation: Ctrl + V pastes; Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + X cuts, Ctrl + Z undoes.

mcqs.explanation: In a star topology every node links to a central switch/hub that relays traffic.

mcqs.q: In the star topology shown, if the CENTRAL device fails, what happens?
options: PCs connect to each other directly
mcqs.explanation: All traffic passes through the centre; if it fails, no node can exchange data with another.

mcqs.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on —
mcqs.explanation: RBI came into existence on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, following the Hilton Young Commission (1926).

mcqs.q: The State Bank of India was formed by renaming which bank?
mcqs.explanation: The three Presidency Banks merged into the Imperial Bank (1921), which became SBI on 1 July 1955.

mcqs.q: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to the —
mcqs.explanation: CRR is the percentage of NDTL that banks must deposit as cash with the RBI; it earns no interest.

mcqs.q: India's flexible inflation targeting framework targets CPI inflation of —
mcqs.explanation: The MPC targets 4% CPI inflation with a tolerance band of ±2% (2%-6%), as per the RBI Act amended in 2016.

mcqs.q: Payments Banks in India —
mcqs.explanation: Payments banks accept deposits up to ₹2 lakh and issue debit cards but are prohibited from lending or issuing credit cards.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of the RBI?
mcqs.explanation: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor; C.D. Deshmukh (1943) was the first Indian Governor.

mcqs.q: Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which —
mcqs.explanation: Under reverse repo, commercial banks park surplus funds with the RBI — i.e., the RBI borrows from banks.
