mcqs.q: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on:
mcqs.explanation: RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934; nationalised on 1 January 1949.

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of RBI located?
mcqs.explanation: RBI headquarters — Mumbai (originally Kolkata, moved to Mumbai in 1937).

mcqs.q: Who was the first Governor of RBI?
mcqs.explanation: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of RBI (1935-1937).

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of RBI?
mcqs.explanation: Chintaman Dwarkanath Deshmukh (C.D. Deshmukh) — first Indian Governor of RBI (1943-1949).

mcqs.q: How many banks were nationalised in 1969?
mcqs.explanation: 14 commercial banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969 — first batch of bank nationalisation.

mcqs.q: In 1980, how many more banks were nationalised?
mcqs.explanation: 6 more banks were nationalised on 15 April 1980 — second batch; total 20 nationalised banks (later New Bank of India merged with PNB in 1993).

mcqs.q: What is CRR?
mcqs.explanation: CRR — Cash Reserve Ratio; % of deposits banks must keep with RBI in cash form; currently 4.5% (2024).

mcqs.q: What is SLR?
mcqs.explanation: SLR — Statutory Liquidity Ratio; % of deposits banks must invest in approved securities (govt bonds, gold, cash); currently 18% (2024).

mcqs.q: Repo Rate is the rate at which:
mcqs.explanation: Repo Rate — rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks against government securities; current 6.5% (2024).

mcqs.q: Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which:
mcqs.explanation: Reverse Repo Rate — rate at which RBI borrows from commercial banks; currently 3.35% (2024).

mcqs.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of RBI has how many members?
mcqs.explanation: MPC has 6 members — 3 from RBI (Governor, Dy Governor, 1 officer) + 3 external members appointed by Government.

mcqs.q: Currency notes of which denomination are issued by Ministry of Finance (not RBI)?
mcqs.explanation: ₹1 notes — issued by Government of India (Ministry of Finance); signed by Finance Secretary. ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500, ₹1000, ₹2000 — by RBI.

mcqs.q: Who is the current Governor of RBI (as of 2024-25)?
mcqs.explanation: Shaktikanta Das has been RBI Governor since 12 December 2018.

mcqs.q: Bank Rate is:
options: Rate at which banks lend to public
Rate at which RBI borrows from banks
Rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks without security
mcqs.explanation: Bank Rate — rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks without any security; usually higher than Repo Rate.

mcqs.q: What is the full form of MSF?
mcqs.explanation: MSF — Marginal Standing Facility; banks can borrow from RBI overnight against govt securities; rate = Repo + 0.25%.

mcqs.q: Repo Rate is:
options: Rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks
Rate at which banks lend to RBI
Rate at which banks lend to public
mcqs.explanation: Repo Rate — RBI lends to banks against govt securities; current 6.5%.

mcqs.q: Reverse Repo is:
options: Rate at which RBI borrows from banks
mcqs.explanation: Reverse Repo — RBI borrows from banks; rate lower than Repo.

mcqs.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) refer to:
mcqs.explanation: OMO — RBI buys/sells govt securities to control money supply.

mcqs.q: Inflation in India is measured by:
mcqs.explanation: CPI (Consumer Price Index) — main measure of retail inflation in India.

mcqs.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on:
mcqs.explanation: RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.

mcqs.q: The RBI was nationalized in:
mcqs.explanation: RBI was transferred to government ownership on 1 January 1949.

mcqs.q: The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India is in:
mcqs.explanation: RBI's central office has been in Mumbai since its inception.

mcqs.q: Who appoints the Governor of the RBI?
mcqs.explanation: The RBI Governor is appointed by the Central Government (Appointments Committee of the Cabinet).

mcqs.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of India has how many members?
mcqs.explanation: MPC has 6 members — 3 from RBI (incl. Governor as chair) and 3 external appointees.

mcqs.q: India's flexible inflation targeting framework targets CPI inflation of:
mcqs.explanation: The target is 4% CPI with a tolerance band of +/− 2% (i.e., 2%–6%).

mcqs.q: CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) is the fraction of deposits that banks must:
options: keep as cash reserves with the RBI
mcqs.explanation: CRR is maintained as cash balances with RBI; it earns no interest.

mcqs.q: SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) requires banks to maintain liquid assets in the form of:
options: gold, cash and approved government securities
mcqs.explanation: SLR is held as liquid assets — cash, gold and SLR-eligible G-secs — with the bank itself.

mcqs.q: The repo rate is the rate at which:
options: RBI lends short-term funds to banks against securities
mcqs.explanation: Repo = RBI's short-term lending rate to banks against government securities.

mcqs.q: The reverse repo rate is the rate at which:
options: banks lend to RBI against securities
mcqs.explanation: In reverse repo, banks park surplus funds with the RBI and earn that rate.

mcqs.q: To fight inflation, the RBI generally:
mcqs.explanation: Higher repo makes borrowing costlier, cooling demand and prices.

mcqs.q: Which body prints currency notes in India (except one-rupee notes)?
mcqs.explanation: The RBI issues banknotes; the one-rupee note is issued by the Finance Ministry.

mcqs.q: The RBI Act under which it functions was passed in:
mcqs.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India Act was enacted in 1934; the bank started in 1935.

mcqs.q: Which is the central bank of India?
mcqs.explanation: RBI is India's central bank — banker to banks and to the government, and monetary authority.

mcqs.q: Bank rate differs from repo rate because bank rate is:
options: an unsecured long-term rate with no collateral
mcqs.explanation: Bank rate is the RBI's unsecured lending rate without collateral; repo involves repossession of securities.

mcqs.q: 14 major commercial banks were nationalized in India in:
mcqs.explanation: The first wave of bank nationalization (14 banks) occurred in July 1969; six more followed in 1980.

mcqs.q: NABARD was established in 1982 to focus on:
mcqs.explanation: NABARD is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development.

mcqs.q: The 'lender of last resort' for Indian banks is:
mcqs.explanation: When banks exhaust all funding options, the RBI lends to them as lender of last resort.

mcqs.q: MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) allows banks to borrow overnight by dipping into:
options: SLR by up to a permitted limit
mcqs.explanation: Under MSF banks can borrow overnight against excess SLR securities (within the allowed ceiling).

mcqs.q: SEBI regulates:
mcqs.explanation: SEBI (1988; statutory 1992) regulates stock exchanges, brokers and listed companies.

mcqs.q: The 'base rate' and MCLR concepts relate to:
options: minimum lending rates below which banks generally cannot lend
mcqs.explanation: MCLR is the internal floor rate below which lending (except permitted cases) is not allowed.

mcqs.q: External benchmark (EBLR) linked retail loans are pegged mainly to:
mcqs.explanation: Since October 2019, new retail/MSME floating loans are linked to an external benchmark — mostly the repo rate.

mcqs.q: Financial Stability Report (FSR) is published by:
mcqs.explanation: The RBI's FSR assesses risks to the financial sector half-yearly.

mcqs.q: Which entity insures bank deposits in India?
mcqs.explanation: DICGC (a subsidiary of RBI) insures deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

mcqs.q: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched in —
mcqs.explanation: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 to provide universal access to zero-balance bank accounts.

mcqs.q: PMJJBY provides —
mcqs.explanation: PMJJBY (Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana) offers ₹2 lakh life insurance for ₹436 annual premium (age 18-50).

mcqs.q: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is administered by —
mcqs.explanation: APY is administered by PFRDA (Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority), launched 9 May 2015.

mcqs.q: Which bank account normally does NOT pay any interest?
mcqs.explanation: Current accounts, used by businesses for frequent transactions, pay no interest but offer overdraft facilities.

mcqs.q: UPI is developed and operated by —
mcqs.explanation: UPI (2016) is built and operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which also runs RuPay and IMPS.

mcqs.q: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) doubles the invested amount in —
mcqs.explanation: KVP is designed to double the investment in 115 months (about 9 years 7 months) at the notified rate.

mcqs.q: Under the DICGC insurance scheme, bank deposits are insured up to —
mcqs.explanation: Since February 2020, DICGC insures up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (earlier it was only ₹1 lakh).

mcqs.q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on:
mcqs.explanation: PMJDY launched on 28 August 2014 — world's largest financial inclusion programme; provides zero-balance bank accounts.

mcqs.q: UPI was launched by which organization?
mcqs.explanation: UPI — Unified Payments Interface; launched by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) on 11 April 2016.

mcqs.q: RTGS minimum transaction amount is:
mcqs.explanation: RTGS — minimum ₹2 lakh; real-time gross settlement; no upper limit.

mcqs.q: NEFT has which minimum transaction limit?
mcqs.explanation: NEFT — no minimum or maximum limit; batch processing.

mcqs.q: IMPS is available for how many hours?
mcqs.explanation: IMPS — Immediate Payment Service; available 24×7 including holidays.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a UPI app?
mcqs.explanation: Whatsapp Pay — payment service within WhatsApp (also UPI-based); PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm — major UPI apps.

mcqs.q: PMJJBY provides life cover of:
mcqs.explanation: PMJJBY — ₹2 lakh life cover for ₹330/year premium; age 18-50 years.

mcqs.q: MUDRA loans up to how much?
mcqs.explanation: MUDRA — loans up to ₹10 lakh; three categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh).

mcqs.q: APY (Atal Pension Yojana) was launched in:
mcqs.explanation: Atal Pension Yojana — launched 9 May 2015; pension scheme for unorganised sector workers; age 18-40.

mcqs.q: Savings account provides:
mcqs.explanation: Savings account — interest on deposits (currently 2.5-4%); allows limited transactions; minimum balance required.

mcqs.q: Fixed Deposit (FD) is:
options: A deposit with fixed term and higher interest
mcqs.explanation: FD — fixed deposit for a fixed term (7 days to 10 years); higher interest than savings (5-7%); lock-in period.

mcqs.q: Credit Card allows:
mcqs.explanation: Credit Card — borrows money from bank up to credit limit; repay by due date; high interest if delayed.

mcqs.q: NRE account is for:
mcqs.explanation: NRE — Non-Resident External; for NRIs; foreign currency; tax-free interest; freely repatriable.

mcqs.q: What does NPCI stand for?
mcqs.explanation: NPCI — National Payments Corporation of India; founded 2008; operates UPI, IMPS, RuPay, BHIM, FASTag.

mcqs.q: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched in which year?
mcqs.explanation: PMJDY, the financial-inclusion scheme with zero-balance accounts and RuPay cards, was launched on 28 August 2014.

mcqs.q: Under PMJDY, depositors get accidental insurance of —
mcqs.explanation: PMJDY RuPay debit cards carry an inbuilt ₹2 lakh accidental cover (raised from ₹1 lakh in 2018).

mcqs.q: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) primarily targets —
mcqs.explanation: APY guarantees a fixed pension (₹1,000–5,000) mostly for unorganised-sector workers after 60.

mcqs.q: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account matures after how many years (from opening)?
mcqs.explanation: SSY matures 21 years from opening, with partial withdrawal allowed for the girl's education/marriage.

mcqs.q: MUDRA loan categories are —
mcqs.explanation: MUDRA (PMMY) collateral-free loans come in Shishu (≤₹50k), Kishore (₹50k–5L) and Tarun (₹5–10L) tiers.

mcqs.q: DICGC insures bank deposits of a depositor per bank up to —
mcqs.explanation: Since Feb 2020, DICGC insurance covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal + interest).

mcqs.q: PPF (Public Provident Fund) has a tenure of —
mcqs.explanation: PPF runs for 15 years, extendable in 5-year blocks, with EEE tax status.

mcqs.q: PMJJBY and PMSBY are respectively —
mcqs.explanation: PMJJBY is ₹2 lakh life cover; PMSBY is ₹2 lakh accidental-death/disability cover.

mcqs.q: Which account type is meant for business transactions with no interest usually?
mcqs.explanation: Current accounts suit businesses with unlimited transactions and generally pay no interest.

mcqs.q: RTGS is best described as —
options: real-time gross settlement of large-value payments
batch settlement at end of day
mcqs.explanation: RTGS settles high-value transfers individually and instantly (minimum ₹2 lakh).

mcqs.q: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) primarily provides —
mcqs.explanation: KCC gives farmers timely short-term working capital for cultivation and allied activities.

mcqs.q: PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana) aims at —
mcqs.explanation: PMAY provides credit-linked subsidies for urban (PMAY-U) and rural (PMAY-G) housing.

mcqs.q: A Recurring Deposit (RD) requires —
options: fixed monthly deposits for a fixed term
mcqs.explanation: In an RD you deposit a fixed amount monthly and earn interest close to FD rates.

mcqs.q: Which payment system works only ONCE A DAY in batches (historically)?
mcqs.explanation: NEFT historically settled in half-hourly batches (now 24x7), unlike RTGS which is real-time — UPI/IMPS are instant.

mcqs.q: An Overdraft (OD) facility means —
options: withdraw more than the account balance up to a limit
mcqs.explanation: OD lets a current-account holder draw beyond the balance up to an agreed limit; interest is charged only on used amount.

mcqs.q: RTGS is meant for transfers of:
options: ₹2 lakh and above, settled in real time
mcqs.explanation: RTGS handles large-value transfers of minimum ₹2 lakh, settlement instant and gross.

mcqs.q: NEFT settlements are:
mcqs.explanation: NEFT works in batches; since Dec 2019 it runs 24x7 in half-hourly cycles.

mcqs.q: UPI is developed by:
mcqs.explanation: UPI was built by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in 2016.

mcqs.q: IMPS differs from NEFT because IMPS is:
mcqs.explanation: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) is an instant, round-the-clock transfer channel.

mcqs.q: A current account is best suited for:
mcqs.explanation: Current accounts allow unlimited transactions and usually pay no interest.

mcqs.q: In a Fixed Deposit (FD), interest is generally:
options: higher than a savings account because money is locked for a term
mcqs.explanation: FDs pay a higher rate in return for locking the amount for a fixed period.

mcqs.q: In a Recurring Deposit (RD), the depositor:
options: deposits a fixed amount every month
mcqs.explanation: RD = fixed monthly installments for a chosen tenure with FD-like interest.

mcqs.q: Overdraft facility means:
options: the bank deposits money into your account as a gift
withdrawing more than the account balance up to a sanctioned limit
mcqs.explanation: Overdraft lets a current-account holder draw beyond balance up to an agreed limit; interest is charged on the used amount.

mcqs.q: KYC in banking stands for:
mcqs.explanation: KYC norms require identity and address verification before opening accounts.

mcqs.q: CIBIL score in India ranges from:
mcqs.explanation: CIBIL scores run from 300 to 900; above 750 is considered good.

mcqs.q: An EMI consists of:
mcqs.explanation: Equated Monthly Installment = fixed monthly payment covering both principal and interest.

mcqs.q: PPF (Public Provident Fund) currently has a lock-in of:
mcqs.explanation: PPF matures in 15 years with partial withdrawals allowed after specific years.

mcqs.q: MUDRA loans under PMMY are given mainly to:
options: micro and small enterprises / small businesses
mcqs.explanation: MUDRA (Shishu/Kishor/Tarun) funds small non-farm income-generating activities.

mcqs.q: PM Jan Dhan Yojana primarily aims at:
options: universal access to bank accounts for every household
mcqs.explanation: PMJDY drives financial inclusion — zero-balance accounts, RuPay card, overdraft.

mcqs.q: A demat account is used to:
options: hold shares and securities in electronic form
mcqs.explanation: Dematerialized (demat) accounts hold shares/bonds electronically with a depository participant.

mcqs.q: SIP in mutual funds means:
options: investing a fixed amount at regular intervals
mcqs.explanation: Systematic Investment Plan automates periodic (usually monthly) investments.

mcqs.q: Collateral is:
options: an asset pledged against a loan
mcqs.explanation: If the borrower defaults, the bank can seize the pledged (collateral) asset.

mcqs.q: FCNR(B) accounts are maintained by:
mcqs.explanation: Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits let NRIs hold FDs in foreign currency.

mcqs.q: The Atal Pension Yojana targets:
options: unorganized sector workers with a guaranteed pension
mcqs.explanation: APY gives ₹1,000–₹5,000 monthly pension (age 60) to unorganized-sector subscribers.

mcqs.q: A cheque marked 'crossed' means:
options: payment only through bank account credit, not cash over the counter
mcqs.explanation: Two parallel lines = crossing; amount goes only to the payee's bank account.

mcqs.q: Positive Pay System is used for:
mcqs.explanation: For cheques above ₹50,000 (optional), details are re-confirmed by the issuer to stop fraud.

mcqs.q: Which account typically earns the LEAST interest?
mcqs.explanation: Current accounts usually pay no interest as they are meant for business transactions.

mcqs.q: A credit card's 'grace period' means:

mcqs.passage:
Passage — The Reserve Bank and the Price of Money

The Reserve Bank of India is the economy's thermostat. Its Monetary Policy Committee — six members, chaired by the RBI Governor, meeting at least four times a year — sets the policy repo rate, the interest at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks. That single price ripples outward: cheaper repo borrowing lets banks cut lending rates for home, auto and business loans, stoking spending; a costlier rate cools credit and cools, with it, inflation. India's framework targets consumer-price inflation at 4 per cent, with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent — above the band, the RBI must explain to the Government why it failed and how it will return. The Bank also manages the money supply directly: the Cash Reserve Ratio forces banks to park a share of deposits with the RBI, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio ties up funds in approved securities, and open market operations buy or sell government bonds to inject or absorb cash. Rate policy moves slowly and works with a lag; that is why committees vote on outlooks, not headlines, and why a governor's sentence is weighed as carefully as a budget.

mcqs.q: The monetary policy repo rate is —
options: the rate banks pay depositors on savings accounts
the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks
the rate at which banks lend to the RBI
the exchange rate between rupee and dollar
mcqs.explanation: 'The policy repo rate, the interest at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks' — the reverse repo/standing deposit facility is the opposite direction.

mcqs.explanation: Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin) — southernmost point of Indian mainland. Indira Point is southernmost of India (in Andaman).

mcqs.explanation: Wular Lake (J&K) — largest freshwater lake in India.

mcqs.q: Largest saltwater lake in India:
mcqs.explanation: Chilika Lake (Odisha) — largest brackish water lake in India.

mcqs.q: Highest dam in India:
mcqs.explanation: Tehri Dam (260 m high, Uttarakhand) — highest dam in India.

mcqs.q: Who was the first human to travel into space?
mcqs.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok-1 on 12 April 1961.

mcqs.q: The first woman to climb Mount Everest was —
mcqs.explanation: Japanese climber Junko Tabei summited Everest in 1975; Bachendri Pal was the first Indian woman (1984).

mcqs.q: Sputnik-1, the first artificial satellite of the Earth, was launched by —
mcqs.explanation: USSR launched Sputnik-1 on 4 October 1957, starting the space age.

mcqs.q: Who performed the world's first successful heart transplant?
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Christiaan (Christian) Barnard performed the first heart transplant in Cape Town, South Africa, in December 1967.

mcqs.q: The first woman President of the UN General Assembly was —
mcqs.explanation: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (India) was elected the first woman President of the UNGA in 1953.

mcqs.q: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 at —
mcqs.explanation: Athens, Greece hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896, revived by Pierre de Coubertin.

mcqs.q: Who was the first man to set foot on the moon?
mcqs.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped on the moon on 20 July 1969 (Apollo-11), followed by Buzz Aldrin.

mcqs.q: The first man to reach the South Pole was:
mcqs.explanation: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole in December 1911, beating Captain Scott.

mcqs.q: The first country to win the FIFA Football World Cup was:
mcqs.explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup in 1930, defeating Argentina 4–2.

mcqs.q: The first woman in space was:
mcqs.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova flew aboard Vostok-6 in June 1963.

mcqs.q: The first cricketer to receive the Padma Bhushan was:
mcqs.explanation: C.K. Nayudu, India's first Test captain, received the Padma Bhushan in 1956.

mcqs.q: The first blind man to scale Mount Everest was:
mcqs.explanation: American Erik Weihenmayer climbed Everest in 2001 despite being blind. (Mark Inglis was the first double-amputee; Bachendri Pal was the first Indian woman.)

mcqs.q: The first American President to visit India was:
mcqs.explanation: President Dwight D. Eisenhower visited India in December 1959.

mcqs.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
mcqs.explanation: Neil Armstrong on 21 July 1969 (Apollo 11).

mcqs.q: Who was the first woman to climb Mount Everest?
mcqs.explanation: Junko Tabei (Japan) — 16 May 1975. Bachendri Pal was first Indian woman (1984).

mcqs.q: Who was the first man to fly an aeroplane?
mcqs.explanation: Wright Brothers (Orville & Wilbur) — 17 December 1903.

mcqs.q: Who was the first President of the USA?
mcqs.explanation: George Washington (1789-1797).

mcqs.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Britain?
mcqs.explanation: Sir Robert Walpole (1721) — first PM of Britain.

mcqs.q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
mcqs.explanation: Marie Curie won Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 (with Pierre Curie).

mcqs.q: Who was the first man to reach South Pole?
mcqs.explanation: Roald Amundsen (Norway) — 14 December 1911.

mcqs.q: Who was the first to climb Mount Everest?
mcqs.explanation: Edmund Hillary (NZ) & Tenzing Norgay (India) — 29 May 1953.

mcqs.q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister in the world?
mcqs.explanation: Sirimavo Bandaranaike (Sri Lanka, 1960) — first woman PM in the world.

mcqs.q: Who was the first astronaut to go into space?
mcqs.explanation: Yuri Gagarin (USSR) — 12 April 1961 (Vostok 1).

mcqs.q: Who was the first woman in space?
mcqs.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova (USSR) — 16 June 1963 (Vostok 6).

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian to win Nobel Prize?
mcqs.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian woman to win Nobel Prize?
mcqs.explanation: Mother Teresa (1979, Peace) — first Indian woman Nobel laureate.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian to go into space?
mcqs.explanation: Rakesh Sharma — 2 April 1984 aboard Soyuz T-11.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
mcqs.explanation: Bachendri Pal — 23 May 1984.

mcqs.q: The first man to walk on the Moon was:
mcqs.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969 (Apollo 11).

mcqs.q: The first woman Prime Minister in the world was:
mcqs.explanation: Sri Lanka's Sirimavo Bandaranaike (1960) was the world's first woman PM.

mcqs.q: The first man to climb Mt Everest was (along with Tenzing Norgay):
mcqs.explanation: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay summited on 29 May 1953.

mcqs.q: The first woman to climb Mt Everest was:
mcqs.explanation: Bachendri Pal (India) reached the top on 23 May 1984.

mcqs.q: The first Indian in space was:
mcqs.explanation: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma flew aboard Soyuz T-11 in 1984.

mcqs.q: The first President of the USA was:
mcqs.explanation: George Washington (1789-1797).

mcqs.q: The first woman President of India was:
mcqs.explanation: Pratibha Patil (2007-2012) was India's first woman President.

mcqs.q: The first President of India was:
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad served 1950-1962.

mcqs.q: The first woman Governor of an Indian state was:
mcqs.explanation: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of United Provinces in 1947.

mcqs.q: The first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal was:
mcqs.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting (Sydney 2000); P.T. Usha missed by inches in 1984.

mcqs.q: The first person to reach the South Pole was:
mcqs.explanation: Norwegian Roald Amundsen reached it on 14 December 1911.

mcqs.q: The first country to give women the right to vote was:
mcqs.explanation: New Zealand granted women's suffrage in 1893.

mcqs.q: The first Muslim woman to become President of a country (via election in her own right) was:
mcqs.explanation: Indonesia's Megawati Sukarnoputri became president in 2001; Benazir was PM (1988).

mcqs.q: The first human heart transplant was performed in 1967 by:
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Christiaan Barnard, Cape Town, South Africa.

mcqs.q: Jim Corbett National Park is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Jim Corbett NP is in Nainital–Pauri districts of Uttarakhand; it was India's first National Park (1936).

mcqs.q: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Kaziranga lies on the Brahmaputra floodplains of Assam and also holds the highest density of tigers among Indian reserves.

mcqs.q: The world's only floating National Park is —
mcqs.explanation: Keibul Lamjao NP (Manipur) floats on phumdis (decaying vegetation) of Loktak Lake and protects the Sangai deer.

mcqs.q: Dachigam National Park is famous for —
mcqs.explanation: Dachigam NP near Srinagar (J&K) is the last refuge of the Hangul, or Kashmir stag.

mcqs.q: Project Tiger was launched in which year?
mcqs.explanation: Project Tiger started in 1973 from Jim Corbett NP; the Wildlife Protection Act came in 1972 and Project Elephant in 1992.

mcqs.q: Bandhavgarh National Park, known for the highest tiger density, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Bandhavgarh NP is in Madhya Pradesh — the "Tiger State" of India, which also has the most National Parks (11).

mcqs.q: The only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion is:
mcqs.explanation: Gir National Park (Gujarat) is the last natural home of the Asiatic lion.

mcqs.q: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for the one-horned rhino.

mcqs.q: India's oldest national park (established 1936) is:
mcqs.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand), established in 1936 as Hailey National Park.

mcqs.q: The Hangul (Kashmir stag) is protected in:
mcqs.explanation: Dachigam National Park (J&K) is the sanctuary of the Hangul deer.

mcqs.q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park, a world-famous bird sanctuary, is located at:
mcqs.explanation: Keoladeo Ghana at Bharatpur, Rajasthan — a UNESCO site famous for migratory birds like the Siberian crane.

mcqs.q: The lion-tailed macaque is protected in Silent Valley National Park in:
mcqs.explanation: Silent Valley (Kerala) in the Nilgiris protects the endangered lion-tailed macaque.

mcqs.q: Hemis National Park, famous for the snow leopard, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Hemis (Ladakh) is called the 'snow leopard capital' of India.

mcqs.q: Bharat Ratna was instituted in:
mcqs.explanation: Bharat Ratna — India's highest civilian award; instituted 1954.

mcqs.q: First recipient of Bharat Ratna:
mcqs.explanation: First recipients of Bharat Ratna (1954): C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman.

mcqs.q: Nobel Prize is named after:
mcqs.explanation: Alfred Nobel (Swedish inventor of dynamite); Nobel Prizes started 1901.

mcqs.q: Ramon Magsaysay Award is given by:
mcqs.explanation: Ramon Magsaysay Award — given by Philippines (since 1958); 'Asian Nobel Prize'.

mcqs.q: India's first national park (1936) is:
mcqs.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand), originally Hailey National Park.

mcqs.q: Kaziranga National Park is famous for:
mcqs.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) hosts the great Indian one-horned rhino.

mcqs.q: The Sundarbans National Park is famous for:
mcqs.explanation: West Bengal's mangrove delta — Royal Bengal tigers.

mcqs.q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park, a bird sanctuary, is located at:
mcqs.explanation: Bharatpur (Rajasthan) — UNESCO site for migratory birds.

mcqs.q: Ranthambore National Park is in:
mcqs.explanation: Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan) is a famous tiger reserve.

mcqs.q: Kanha National Park inspired which famous work's setting?
mcqs.explanation: Kanha (MP) sal-bamboo forest is linked to Rudyard Kipling's Jungle Book.

mcqs.q: The Great Indian Bustard sanctuary 'Desert National Park' is in:
mcqs.explanation: Near Jaisalmer, Rajasthan — critical habitat of the endangered bustard.

mcqs.q: Periyar National Park is known for elephants and tigers and is in:
mcqs.explanation: Periyar Tiger Reserve, Thekkady (Kerala).

mcqs.q: Bandipur National Park lies in the state of:
mcqs.explanation: Bandipur (Karnataka) adjoins Mudumalai and Wayanad.

mcqs.q: The Project Tiger was launched in:
mcqs.explanation: Project Tiger began in 1973 from Jim Corbett with 9 reserves.

mcqs.q: Manas National Park, a UNESCO site with golden langurs, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Manas (Assam) — also a tiger reserve and biosphere reserve.

mcqs.q: The wild ass (ghudkhar) sanctuary is located at:
mcqs.explanation: Wild Ass Sanctuary, Little Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Hemis National Park, famous for snow leopards, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Hemis (Ladakh) — high-altitude snow leopard habitat.

mcqs.q: Namdapha National Park, with all four big cats, lies in:
mcqs.explanation: Namdapha (Arunachal) — tiger, leopard, snow leopard, clouded leopard.

mcqs.q: "Birdie" and "Bogey" are terms of which sport?
mcqs.explanation: Birdie (one under par), Eagle (two under), Bogey (one over) and Par are Golf terms.

mcqs.q: How many players does a Kabaddi team field on the mat?
mcqs.explanation: Kabaddi is played with 7 players on each side; Kho-Kho has 9, Volleyball 6, Basketball 5.

mcqs.q: "Half Nelson" is a term used in —
mcqs.explanation: Half Nelson and Full Nelson are wrestling holds; boxing uses jab, uppercut and clinch.

mcqs.q: The Durand Cup, the oldest football tournament of Asia, was first held in —
mcqs.explanation: Durand Cup started in 1888 at Shimla; it is Asia's oldest football tournament.

mcqs.q: "Chukker" is associated with which sport?
mcqs.explanation: A chukker (chukka) is one playing period of a Polo match; Derby belongs to horse racing.

mcqs.q: "Bull's eye" is related to which sport?
mcqs.explanation: Bull's eye is the centre of the target in shooting; darts also uses the term, but the classic exam answer is Shooting.

mcqs.q: The term 'Bully' is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Bully is a restarting method in hockey.

mcqs.q: In tennis, 'Love' means:
mcqs.explanation: Love = zero in tennis scoring (e.g., 30–love).

mcqs.q: The term 'Gambit' is related to:
mcqs.explanation: Gambit is a chess opening in which a pawn is sacrificed for advantage.

mcqs.q: 'Birdie' is a term of:
mcqs.explanation: In golf, a birdie means one stroke under par for a hole.

mcqs.q: The famous Eden Gardens cricket stadium is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Eden Gardens, Kolkata — India's most iconic cricket ground.

mcqs.q: The term 'Golden Goal' was associated with:
mcqs.explanation: In football, a golden goal decided the match instantly in extra time (now abolished).

mcqs.q: 'Lona' is a scoring term of:
mcqs.explanation: In kabaddi, a lona is a bonus of two points when the rival team is completely all-out.

mcqs.q: "Googly" is a term associated with —
mcqs.explanation: A googly is a leg-spinner's ball that turns the opposite way (invented by Bernard Bosanquet).

mcqs.q: "Bully" is a term used in —
mcqs.explanation: A bully restarts play in hockey, like a face-off in ice hockey.

mcqs.q: "Deuce" is a term used in —
mcqs.explanation: In tennis, deuce means 40-40; a player must win two straight points from there.

mcqs.q: "Bull's eye" is associated with —
mcqs.explanation: The bull's eye is the exact centre of the target in shooting/archery.

mcqs.q: "Love" in tennis means —
mcqs.explanation: A zero score in tennis is called love.

mcqs.q: "Birdie" and "Eagle" are terms from —
mcqs.explanation: In golf, birdie = one under par and eagle = two under par on a hole.

mcqs.q: "Checkmate" and "Gambit" belong to —
mcqs.explanation: A gambit is an opening sacrifice and checkmate ends a chess game.

mcqs.q: "Penalty corner" is a set play in —
mcqs.explanation: The penalty (short) corner is a major scoring opportunity in hockey.

mcqs.q: The Duckworth–Lewis–Stern method is used in —
mcqs.explanation: DLS recalculates targets in limited-overs cricket interrupted by weather.

mcqs.q: The "Ranji Trophy" is associated with —
mcqs.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier first-class cricket championship.

mcqs.q: The "Durand Cup" is related to —
mcqs.explanation: The Durand Cup (1888) is Asia's oldest football tournament.

mcqs.q: "Thomas Cup" and "Uber Cup" are championships of —
mcqs.explanation: Thomas Cup is the men's world team badminton championship; Uber Cup is the women's.

mcqs.q: "Sultan Azlan Shah Cup" is an annual tournament in —
mcqs.explanation: The Azlan Shah Cup is a famous invitational hockey tournament in Malaysia.

mcqs.q: "Grand Slam" in tennis means winning —
options: All four majors in one year
mcqs.explanation: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open in a calendar year = Grand Slam.

mcqs.q: "Slam dunk" is a scoring move in —
mcqs.explanation: A slam dunk forces the ball through the hoop with one or both hands in basketball.

mcqs.q: 'Bull's eye' is a term associated with:
mcqs.explanation: The target centre in shooting/archery is the bull's eye.

mcqs.q: 'Grand Slam' is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Winning all four majors — Australian, French, Wimbledon, US Open.

mcqs.q: 'Love' in tennis means:
mcqs.explanation: Love = no points (0).

mcqs.q: 'Duck' in cricket refers to:
mcqs.explanation: Zero score; 'golden duck' = first ball dismissal.

mcqs.q: 'Checkmate' terminates a game of:
mcqs.explanation: The king attacked with no legal escape ends the chess game.

mcqs.q: Wimbledon is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: The oldest tennis Grand Slam, on grass in London.

mcqs.q: The Ranji Trophy is related to:
mcqs.explanation: India's premier first-class cricket tournament.

mcqs.q: The Santosh Trophy is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Indian states' football championship.

mcqs.q: The Olympic Games are held every:
mcqs.explanation: Quadrennial; Winter and Summer offset by 2 years.

mcqs.q: The Arjuna Award is given for:
mcqs.explanation: Consistent outstanding performance in sports; Khel Ratna is the top honour.

mcqs.q: 'Penalty corner' is a term in:
mcqs.explanation: A set-piece scoring chance in field hockey.

mcqs.q: 'Stonewalling' or 'castling' belongs to:
mcqs.explanation: Castling is the king-rook special move in chess.

mcqs.q: The FIFA World Cup is held every:
mcqs.explanation: Every four years; 2022 was Qatar, 2026 is USA-Canada-Mexico.

mcqs.q: 'Deuce' is a term in:
mcqs.explanation: Tie at 40-40 (tennis) or 20-20 (badminton).

mcqs.q: The Thomas Cup is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Men's world team badminton championship; India won 2022.

mcqs.q: Which classical dance form is performed in the Satras (monasteries) of Assam?
mcqs.explanation: Sattriya was created by Srimanta Sankardeva and preserved in Vaishnavite Satras of Assam.

mcqs.q: Kathakali is the classical dance of which state?
mcqs.explanation: Kathakali, a story-play with elaborate makeup (vesham), belongs to Kerala along with Mohiniyattam.

mcqs.q: Which school of Chhau dance does NOT use masks?
mcqs.explanation: Mayurbhanj Chhau of Odisha is performed without masks, unlike Seraikella (Jharkhand) and Purulia (West Bengal).

mcqs.q: Ghoomar and Kalbelia are folk dances of —
mcqs.explanation: Ghoomar and Kalbelia belong to Rajasthan; Garba-Dandiya belong to Gujarat; Bhangra-Gidda to Punjab.

mcqs.q: Who among the following is a famous proponent of Kuchipudi?
mcqs.explanation: Raja & Radha Reddy (and Yamini Krishnamurthy) are Kuchipudi exponents; Birju Maharaj = Kathak, Sonal Mansingh = Odissi.

mcqs.q: Yakshagana, a folk theatre form with heavy costumes, belongs to —
mcqs.explanation: Yakshagana is the classical-folk theatre of Karnataka; Kathakali is Kerala's similar-looking but distinct form.

mcqs.q: Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam are classical dances of:
mcqs.explanation: Both Kathakali (story-play) and Mohiniyattam (dance of the enchantress) belong to Kerala.

mcqs.q: The Bihu dance is performed during the festival of:
mcqs.explanation: Bihu is the harvest festival of Assam; Rongali Bihu in April is the main one.

mcqs.q: Ghoomar is a famous folk dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Ghoomar — the graceful women's dance of Rajasthan (Bhil community origin).

mcqs.q: Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of:
mcqs.explanation: Kuchipudi takes its name from the village Kuchelapuram in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The Chhau dance is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: Chhau — a semi-classical masked dance of eastern India (Seraikella, Mayurbhanj, Purulia styles).

mcqs.q: Sattriya, a classical dance, developed in the monasteries (Satras) of:
mcqs.explanation: Sattriya was created by saint Srimanta Sankardeva in the Vaishnavite Satras of Assam.

mcqs.q: Bharatanatyam originated in:
mcqs.explanation: Tamil Nadu's temple dance tradition (Thanjavur).

mcqs.q: Kathakali, with elaborate makeup and mudras, belongs to:
mcqs.explanation: Kathakali is Kerala's classical dance-drama.

mcqs.q: Odissi is the classical dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Odissi traces to Odisha's temples (Maharis, Gotipuas).

mcqs.q: Kuchipudi is the classical dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Kuchipudi village (Andhra) gave the dance its name.

mcqs.q: Manipuri dance is associated with the Ras Leela of:
mcqs.explanation: Manipuri enacts Radha-Krishna Ras Leela devotionally.

mcqs.q: Kathak, emphasizing footwork and spins, flourished in:
mcqs.explanation: Kathak evolved in North Indian courts and temples.

mcqs.q: Mohiniyattam, the 'dance of the enchantress', is from:
mcqs.explanation: Kerala's lasya-style classical dance.

mcqs.q: Garba is the famous folk dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Garba is danced during Navratri in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Lavani, a rhythmic folk dance with dholki, belongs to:
mcqs.explanation: Lavani is Maharashtra's spirited folk form.

mcqs.q: Bihu dance is performed during the festival of the same name in:
mcqs.explanation: Bihu celebrates Assamese harvest festivals (Rongali etc.).

mcqs.q: Bhangra is the energetic harvest dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Punjabi Bhangra accompanies harvest celebrations.

mcqs.q: Ghoomar is a traditional dance of:
mcqs.explanation: Rajasthani Ghoomar — women in swirling ghaghras.

mcqs.q: Yakshagana, a dance-drama with costumes and music, belongs to:
mcqs.explanation: Coastal Karnataka's Yakshagana enacts epics.

mcqs.q: Sattriya, a classical dance from monasteries (satras), belongs to:
mcqs.explanation: Founded by Sankardeva in Vaishnavite satras of Assam.

mcqs.q: Chhau dance is performed in which states?
mcqs.explanation: Chhau (Seraikella, Purulia, Mayurbhanj styles) — masked martial dance.

mcqs.q: Which river is known as "Dakshin Ganga"?
mcqs.explanation: Godavari, rising from Trimbakeshwar (Nashik) and the longest Peninsular river, is called Dakshin Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Narmada river originates from —
mcqs.explanation: Narmada rises from Amarkantak (MP); Mahabaleshwar = Krishna, Trimbakeshwar = Godavari, Sihawa = Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: Hirakud Dam, one of the longest earthen dams in the world, is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud Dam (~25.8 km) stands on the Mahanadi at Sambalpur, Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Dhuandhar Falls at Bhedaghat are located on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Dhuandhar ("smoke cascade") falls are on the Narmada at Bhedaghat near Jabalpur, MP.

mcqs.q: Talakaveri, the source of the Kaveri, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Kaveri rises from Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Under the Indus Water Treaty (1960), India has full rights over which rivers?
mcqs.explanation: India received the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej; Pakistan received the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

mcqs.q: The longest river of Southern India is:
mcqs.explanation: Godavari (about 1,465 km) — honoured as 'Dakshin Ganga'.

mcqs.q: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
mcqs.explanation: The Kosi changes course frequently and floods north Bihar — 'Sorrow of Bihar'. Damodar is the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.

mcqs.q: The Brahmaputra river originates in:
mcqs.explanation: It rises in Tibet as Tsangpo, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Dihang.

mcqs.q: Narmada and Tapi flow into the:
mcqs.explanation: Both west-flowing rift-valley rivers join the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries instead of deltas.

mcqs.q: The Triveni Sangam — confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and (mythical) Saraswati — is at:
mcqs.explanation: Prayagraj (Allahabad) hosts the Triveni Sangam and the Kumbh Mela.

mcqs.q: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon of India, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Chilika (Odisha) — famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins. Vembanad (Kerala) is the longest lake; Pulicat is second-largest lagoon.

mcqs.q: Which river is called the "Vridha (Old) Ganga"?
mcqs.explanation: The Godavari, the longest peninsular river, is also respectfully called Vridha Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Gomti, on which Lucknow stands, is a tributary of —
mcqs.explanation: The Gomti joins the Ganga near Saidpur (Ghazipur), UP.

mcqs.q: The Son river joins which major river?
mcqs.explanation: The Son is a large south-bank tributary of the Ganga near Patna.

mcqs.q: Which river's badlands (ravines) are famous along the MP–UP border?
mcqs.explanation: The Chambal ravines are famous as a beehive habitat and former dacoit territory.

mcqs.q: Srisailam Dam is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Srisailam lies on the Krishna in the Nallamala hills (AP/Telangana).

mcqs.q: Rajahmundry town is situated on the banks of —
mcqs.explanation: Rajahmundry (AP) stands on the Godavari, site of the Dowleswaram barrage.

mcqs.q: The Mahi river is unique because it —
options: crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice
mcqs.explanation: The Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice on its way to the Gulf of Khambhat.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest river of Kerala?
mcqs.explanation: The Periyar (244 km) is Kerala's longest river; Idukki dam stands on it.

mcqs.q: The Subarnarekha flows through which group of states?
mcqs.explanation: Subarnarekha ("streak of gold") drains Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.

mcqs.q: Which pair of rivers forms estuaries instead of deltas?
mcqs.explanation: West-flowing Narmada and Tapi meet the Arabian Sea through estuaries.

mcqs.q: The Indus Water Treaty (1960) gave India rights over which rivers?
mcqs.explanation: India got the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej); Pakistan got the western three.

mcqs.q: The Teesta river originates from which glacier?
mcqs.explanation: The Teesta rises from Zemu glacier in Sikkim.

mcqs.q: Which river is associated with the Hampi ruins?
mcqs.explanation: Hampi, capital of Vijayanagara, stands on the Tungabhadra in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: The Saryu (Ghaghara system) flows through which famous city?
mcqs.explanation: Ayodhya is situated on the Saryu (a Ghaghara tributary system river).

mcqs.q: Mandovi and Zuari are principal rivers of —
mcqs.explanation: The Mandovi and Zuari are Goa's lifeline rivers, joined by the Cumbarjua canal.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest dam in India?
mcqs.explanation: Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand is about 260 m high — India's tallest.

mcqs.q: The Nagarjuna Sagar dam is constructed on the river —
mcqs.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar lies on the Krishna river between Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Tarapur, India's first nuclear power station, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Tarapur in Palghar district, Maharashtra, started operation in 1969.

mcqs.q: The Sardar Sarovar Project is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Sarovar is a major multipurpose project on the Narmada in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant has been built with the cooperation of —
mcqs.explanation: Kudankulam's VVER reactors were built with Russian (Rosatom) cooperation.

mcqs.q: Which dam creates the Gobind Sagar reservoir?
mcqs.explanation: The Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej creates the Gobind Sagar lake.

mcqs.q: The Hirakud Dam, the longest dam of India, is built on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi (Odisha) — about 25.8 km long with dykes.

mcqs.q: India's first nuclear power plant was established at:
mcqs.explanation: Tarapur (Maharashtra) — commissioned in 1969.

mcqs.q: The Sardar Sarovar Project is built on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada at Kevadia, Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, the largest in India, is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu), built with Russian cooperation.

mcqs.q: The Mettur Dam is built on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Mettur Dam — on the Kaveri in Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest in India.

mcqs.q: Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Bhakra Dam stands on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh, with Nangal downstream in Punjab.

mcqs.q: Sardar Sarovar Dam is constructed on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada in Gujarat near the Statue of Unity site.

mcqs.q: Hirakud Dam (one of the world's longest) is on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud Dam near Sambalpur, Odisha, spans the Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: Tehri Dam, India's highest, is built on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Tehri Dam (260.5 m) stands on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar lies on the Krishna between Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Indira Sagar Dam, with one of India's largest reservoirs, is on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Indira Sagar is on the Narmada at Punasa in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Mettur Dam is located on which river in Tamil Nadu?
mcqs.explanation: Mettur (Stanley Reservoir) is on the Kaveri in Salem district.

mcqs.q: Tarapur Atomic Power Station, India's first nuclear plant (1969), is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Tarapur NPP in Maharashtra (Boisar, Palghar) began operation in 1969.

mcqs.q: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Kudankulam NPP (with Russian VVER reactors) is in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: Kaiga Atomic Power Station is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Kaiga lies in the Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Rawatbhata (Rajasthan Atomic Power Station) is near which city?
mcqs.explanation: RAPS is located near Kota on the Chambal river in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Kalpakkam (Madras Atomic Power Station) is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Kalpakkam, south of Chennai, also hosts the prototype fast breeder reactor.

mcqs.q: Bhadla Solar Park, one of the world's largest, is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Bhadla Solar Park (~2,245 MW) is in the Jodhpur district of Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Nathpa Jhakri, India's largest hydroelectric station, is on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Nathpa Jhakri (1,500 MW) harnesses the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Koyna Hydroelectric Project is located in which state?
mcqs.explanation: The Koyna project uses the Koyna (a Krishna tributary) in the Sahyadris of Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: The Bhakra Dam is situated on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Bhakra on the Sutlej — the Gobind Sagar reservoir.

mcqs.q: One of the world's longest dams, Hirakud, is on the:
mcqs.explanation: Hirakud (Odisha) spans the Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: The Kalpak/Kudankulam-type nuclear power plants generate:
mcqs.explanation: Kudankulam (TN) is India's largest nuclear plant by capacity.

mcqs.q: Tehri Dam is India's highest dam at about:
mcqs.explanation: Tehri's height ≈ 260 m on the Bhagirathi.

mcqs.q: The Koyna hydroelectric project is in:
mcqs.explanation: Koyna dam on the Koyna river (Maharashtra) — Shivsagar reservoir.

mcqs.q: K2, the second highest peak of the world, belongs to which range?
mcqs.explanation: K2 (Godwin-Austen) lies in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan.

mcqs.q: Kalsubai, the highest peak of Maharashtra, is located in which range?
mcqs.explanation: Kalsubai (1,646 m) is the highest point of the Sahyadri range in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of South India?
mcqs.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala's Anaimalai hills is the highest of peninsular India.

mcqs.q: Eden Gardens, the historic cricket stadium, is situated in —
mcqs.explanation: Eden Gardens in Kolkata (est. 1864) is India's oldest and most famous cricket ground.

mcqs.q: Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium is associated with which sport?
mcqs.explanation: The Dhyan Chand National Stadium in New Delhi is a hockey venue.

mcqs.q: The world's largest cricket stadium by seating capacity is —
mcqs.explanation: Narendra Modi (Motera) Stadium, Ahmedabad has ~1,32,000 seats, the largest in the world.

mcqs.q: Guru Shikhar, the highest peak of the Aravalli Range, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) stands near Mount Abu in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Anamudi, the highest peak of South India, is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) rises in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala.

mcqs.q: The world's largest cricket stadium — Narendra Modi Stadium — is at:
mcqs.explanation: Narendra Modi (Motera) Stadium, Ahmedabad — capacity about 132,000.

mcqs.q: Dhupgarh, the highest point of the Satpura Range, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Dhupgarh (1,350 m) lies in Madhya Pradesh near Pachmarhi.

mcqs.q: Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium in Delhi is associated with:
mcqs.explanation: It is the home of Indian hockey, named after the legendary Dhyan Chand.

mcqs.q: K2, the world's second highest peak, is also called —
mcqs.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is known as Godwin Austen; it lies in POK.

mcqs.q: Kangchenjunga lies in which Indian state?
mcqs.explanation: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) stands on the Sikkim–Nepal border — India's highest peak.

mcqs.q: Nanda Devi, India's second highest peak, is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Nanda Devi (7,816 m) rises in Uttarakhand inside a famous biosphere reserve.

mcqs.q: Saltoro Kangri, among India's highest peaks, is part of which range?
mcqs.explanation: Saltoro Kangri is in the Saltoro sub-range of the Karakoram near Siachen.

mcqs.q: Anamudi, the highest peak south of the Vindhyas, is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) stands in Kerala's Eravikulam region.

mcqs.q: Guru Shikhar, the highest point of the Aravallis, is located at —
mcqs.explanation: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) lies on the Mount Abu plateau in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Mahendragiri, a notable Eastern Ghats peak, is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Mahendragiri is in Gajapati district, Odisha (part of the Eastern Ghats).

mcqs.q: Wankhede Stadium is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Wankhede Stadium, venue of the 2011 World Cup final, is in Mumbai.

mcqs.q: Eden Gardens, India's oldest and largest cricket ground by capacity, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Eden Gardens in Kolkata is the home of Cricket Association of Bengal.

mcqs.q: Narendra Modi Stadium, the world's largest cricket stadium, is in —
mcqs.explanation: The Motera stadium in Ahmedabad seats about 1,32,000 spectators.

mcqs.q: The Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium (hockey) is in —
mcqs.explanation: The iconic hockey stadium named after Dhyan Chand is in New Delhi.

mcqs.q: Kalinga Stadium, a major hockey venue, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Bhubaneswar's Kalinga Stadium hosted the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup (Rourkela co-hosted 2023).

mcqs.q: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru is run by the Karnataka State Cricket Association.

mcqs.q: Salt Lake Stadium, a football venue, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Salt Lake (Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan) in Kolkata hosted the 2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup final.

mcqs.q: HPCA Stadium, set in the Himalayan foothills, is at —
mcqs.explanation: The scenic HPCA cricket stadium is in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The highest peak in India's Himalaya proper (within Indian-controlled territory claims vary) is often cited as:
mcqs.explanation: Exam convention: K2 in Karakoram; Kanchenjunga is the highest fully within Indian borders.

mcqs.q: Wankhede Stadium is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Wankhede (Mumbai) hosted the 2011 World Cup final.

mcqs.q: Eden Gardens, a famous cricket ground, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Eden Gardens, Kolkata — India's iconic cricket venue.

mcqs.q: The Indian Museum, established in 1814, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: The Indian Museum in Kolkata is the oldest and largest multipurpose museum in India.

mcqs.q: Salar Jung Museum is situated at —
mcqs.explanation: Salar Jung Museum, Hyderabad holds the collection of Nawab Salar Jung III, including "Veiled Rebecca".

mcqs.q: Which of the following is the deepest, landlocked and protected port of India?
mcqs.explanation: Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh is described as the deepest, landlocked and protected port.

mcqs.q: Which port of India is known as the largest private commercial port?
mcqs.explanation: Mundra Port in Gujarat, operated by Adani Group, is India's largest private commercial port.

mcqs.q: Which Indian airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport?
mcqs.explanation: Cochin International Airport (CIAL), Kerala runs entirely on solar energy.

mcqs.q: The only riverine major port of India is —
mcqs.explanation: Kolkata Port (Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, with Haldia docks) is the only riverine major port.

mcqs.q: India's largest and oldest museum, the Indian Museum (1814), is in:
mcqs.explanation: Indian Museum, Kolkata — founded in 1814.

mcqs.q: The Salar Jung Museum is located at:
mcqs.explanation: Salar Jung Museum, Hyderabad — built on the one-man collection of Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan.

mcqs.q: India's largest container port is:
mcqs.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva, Maharashtra) leads container traffic.

mcqs.q: The deepest landlocked and protected port of India is:
mcqs.explanation: Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) — the deepest landlocked protected port.

mcqs.q: Which Indian airport is the first in the world to run fully on solar power?
mcqs.explanation: Cochin International Airport (Kerala) — fully solar-powered since 2015.

mcqs.q: Kandla Port (Deendayal Port) is famous as a:
mcqs.explanation: Kandla (Gujarat) works on tides — a classic tidal port.

mcqs.q: The Indian Museum, the country's oldest, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Indian Museum, Kolkata (1814).

mcqs.q: JNPT, India's largest container port, is near:
mcqs.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) handles the most containers.

mcqs.q: Kandla (Deendayal) port is in the state of:
mcqs.explanation: Deendayal (Kandla) Port, Gujarat — major west-coast port.

mcqs.q: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport is in:
mcqs.explanation: Hyderabad's RGIA (Shamshabad).

mcqs.q: Which is the highest waterfall in India?
mcqs.explanation: Kunchikal Falls on the Varahi river in Karnataka (~455 m) is India's highest.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of India?
mcqs.explanation: Wular lake in J&K, fed by the Jhelum, is India's largest freshwater lake.

mcqs.q: Chilika lake, famous for Irrawaddy dolphins, lies in —
mcqs.explanation: Chilika, India's largest lagoon, is on the Odisha coast.

mcqs.q: Loktak lake with its floating "phumdis" is in which state?
mcqs.explanation: Loktak lake in Manipur hosts Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park.

mcqs.q: Jog (Gersoppa) Falls is formed on which river?
mcqs.explanation: Jog Falls is created by the Sharavathi river falling in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Lonar lake, formed by meteorite impact, is located in —
mcqs.explanation: Lonar crater lake is in Buldhana district, Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: The highest waterfall of India, Kunchikal Falls, is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Kunchikal Falls (455 m) on the Varahi river, Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Jog Falls is formed on the river:
mcqs.explanation: Jog (Gersoppa) Falls — the Sharavathi river plunges 253 m in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Which waterfall is known as the 'Niagara of India'?
mcqs.explanation: Chitrakote on the Indravati (Chhattisgarh) — India's widest fall, horseshoe-shaped.

mcqs.q: Wular Lake, India's largest freshwater lake, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Wular Lake (J&K) — fed by the Jhelum river.

mcqs.q: Loktak Lake, famous for its floating islands (phumdis), is in:
mcqs.explanation: Loktak (Manipur) — Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park, lies on it.

mcqs.q: Dhuandhar Falls on the Narmada river is located near:
mcqs.explanation: Dhuandhar — the 'smoke cascade' at Bhedaghat's marble rocks, Jabalpur (MP).

mcqs.q: The Jog Falls are formed by the river:
mcqs.explanation: Jog (Gersoppa) Falls on the Sharavathi, Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Chilika Lake, Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Chilika (Odisha) — Irrawaddy dolphins, migratory birds.

mcqs.q: Wular Lake is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Wular in J&K is among Asia's largest freshwater lakes.

mcqs.q: Sambhar Lake, India's largest inland salt lake, is in:
mcqs.explanation: Sambhar (Rajasthan) — salt production and flamingos.

mcqs.q: As of July 2024, how many UNESCO World Heritage Sites does India have?
mcqs.explanation: With the Moidams of Assam added in July 2024, India has 43 World Heritage Sites.

mcqs.q: Which of these was among India's first World Heritage Sites inscribed in 1983?
mcqs.explanation: Taj Mahal, along with Ajanta, Ellora and Agra Fort, was inscribed in 1983.

mcqs.q: Kaziranga National Park, a World Heritage Site, is famous for —
mcqs.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam, 1985) is home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos.

mcqs.q: The Ramappa Temple, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021, is in —
mcqs.explanation: Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple in Warangal, Telangana is that state's first WHS.

mcqs.q: Dholavira, added to the UNESCO list in 2021, belongs to which civilisation/era?
mcqs.explanation: Dholavira in Gujarat is India's first Harappan-era site on the World Heritage list.

mcqs.q: Santiniketan, added in 2023, is associated with which personality?
mcqs.explanation: Santiniketan in West Bengal was Rabindranath Tagore's home and the base of Visva-Bharati.

mcqs.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites does India have (as of 2025)?
mcqs.explanation: India has 43 sites after the Moidams of Assam were added in 2024.

mcqs.q: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple — India's 39th World Heritage Site — is in:
mcqs.explanation: Ramappa Temple, Warangal (Telangana) — inscribed in 2021.

mcqs.q: Dholavira, the Harappan-era World Heritage Site (2021), is located in:
mcqs.explanation: Dholavira — a Harappan city on Khadir Bet island, Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Which was the first Indian city to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage City?
mcqs.explanation: Ahmadabad (2017) — first; Jaipur (2019) — second.

mcqs.q: Rani-ki-Vav, the stepwell World Heritage Site (2014), is at:
mcqs.explanation: Rani-ki-Vav at Patan, Gujarat — built by Queen Udayamati for Bhima I.

mcqs.q: Santiniketan, associated with Rabindranath Tagore, became a World Heritage Site in:
mcqs.explanation: Santiniketan (West Bengal) — inscribed in September 2023.

mcqs.q: The Taj Mahal and Agra Fort are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the state of:
mcqs.explanation: Both are in Uttar Pradesh (Agra).

mcqs.q: Ajanta and Ellora Caves are in:
mcqs.explanation: Near Aurangabad, Maharashtra — rock-cut Buddhist, Hindu, Jain caves.

mcqs.q: The Konark Sun Temple is in:
mcqs.explanation: Konark (Odisha) — 13th-century Sun Temple chariot.

mcqs.q: Hampi, the Vijayanagara capital ruins, is a heritage site in:
mcqs.explanation: Hampi on the Tungabhadra, Karnataka.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र राज्यात सध्या एकूण किती जिल्हे आहेत?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्रात 36 जिल्हे आहेत; 2014 मध्ये पालघर हा नवीनतम जिल्हा तयार झाला.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रशासकीय विभागांची संख्या किती?
mcqs.explanation: कोकण, पुणे, नाशिक, छत्रपती संभाजीनगर, अमरावती व नागपूर — एकूण 6 प्रशासकीय विभाग.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रात पंचायत राज व्यवस्था कोणत्या दिवशी सुरू झाली?
mcqs.explanation: जिल्हा परिषद व पंचायत समित्या 1 मे 1962 रोजी स्थापन झाल्या; देशातील पंचायत राजाची सुरुवात राजस्थानमध्ये (नागौर) 2 ऑक्टोबर 1959 रोजी झाली.

mcqs.q: ग्रामपंचायतीचे सदस्य संख्या लोकसंख्येनुसार किती असू शकते?
mcqs.explanation: बॉम्बे ग्रामपंचायत अधिनियम, 1958 नुसार लोकसंख्येनुसार ग्रामपंचायतीत 7 ते 17 निवडून आलेले सदस्य असतात.

mcqs.q: राज्य नोकरशाहीतील सर्वोच्च पद कोणते?
mcqs.explanation: मुख्य सचिव (Chief Secretary) हे राज्य नोकरशाहीचे सर्वोच्च पद असून ते मंत्रालयाचे प्रशासकीय प्रमुख असतात.

mcqs.q: जिल्हा परिषदेत किती विषय समित्या (स्थायी समित्या) असतात?
mcqs.explanation: जिप्स अधिनियमानुसार जिल्हा परिषदेत 10 विषय समित्या असतात; त्या विकास कामांचे परीक्षण करतात.

mcqs.q: 73वी घटनादुरुस्ती (पंचायत राज) कोणत्या वर्षी लागू झाली?
mcqs.explanation: 73वी घटनादुरुस्ती 1992 मध्ये स्वीकृत झाली व 24 एप्रिल 1993 रोजी लागू झाली; म्हणून 24 एप्रिल हा राष्ट्रीय पंचायत राज दिवस आहे.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र विधानसभेत किती सदस्य आहेत?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्र विधानसभेत २८८ सदस्य आहेत — विधानसभा निवडणुकीतून निवडले जातात.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र विधानपरिषदेत किती सदस्य आहेत?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्र विधानपरिषदेत ७८ सदस्य आहेत — स्थायी सदन; कार्यकाळ ६ वर्षे.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील पंचायत राज व्यवस्थेतील सर्वात वरील स्तर कोणता आहे?
mcqs.explanation: जिल्हा परिषद — महाराष्ट्र पंचायत राज व्यवस्थेतील सर्वात वरील स्तर; CEO (मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी) प्रमुख.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र लोकसेवा आयोगाचे (MPSC) मुख्यालय कोठे आहे?
mcqs.explanation: MPSC चे मुख्यालय नाशिक येथे आहे — स्थापना १ मे १९६०.

mcqs.q: बॉम्बे उच्च न्यायालयाची स्थापना कोणत्या वर्षी झाली?
mcqs.explanation: बॉम्बे उच्च न्यायालयाची स्थापना १८६२ मध्ये झाली — भारतातील तीन आद्य उच्च न्यायालयांपैकी एक (कलकत्ता, मद्रास, बॉम्बे).

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्राचे पहिले मुख्यमंत्री कोण होते?
mcqs.explanation: यशवंतराव चव्हाण — महाराष्ट्राचे पहिले मुख्यमंत्री (१ मे १९६० ते १९ नोव्हेंबर १९६२).

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील जिल्हा प्रशासकाचे पद कोणते आहे?
mcqs.explanation: जिल्हाधिकारी (Collector / District Magistrate) — जिल्ह्याचा प्रमुख प्रशासक; IAS अधिकारी.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रात जिल्हा परिषदेचे प्रमुख अधिकारी कोण असतात?
mcqs.explanation: CEO (मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी) — जिल्हा परिषदेचा प्रमुख अधिकारी; IAS अधिकारी.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र लोकसेवा आयोग (MPSC) कोणत्या परीक्षा घेते?
mcqs.explanation: MPSC — राज्यसेवा (State Services), PSI (पोलीस उपनिरीक्षक), STI (राज्य कर निरीक्षक), ASO (सहाय्यक विभागीय अधिकारी) परीक्षा घेते.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र विधानसभेचा कार्यकाळ किती वर्षांचा असतो?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्र विधानसभा कार्यकाळ ५ वर्षांचा — बहुमतावर आधारित; विधानपरिषद स्थायी (६ वर्ष).

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील ग्रामपंचायतीचा प्रमुख कोण असतो?
mcqs.explanation: सरपंच — ग्रामपंचायतीचा निर्वाचित प्रमुख; ग्रामविकास अधिकारी (गटविकास अधिकारी) व्यवस्थापन करतात.

mcqs.q: बॉम्बे उच्च न्यायालयाची खंडपीठे कोठे आहेत?
mcqs.explanation: बॉम्बे उच्च न्यायालयाची खंडपीठे — औरंगाबाद व नागपूर येथे; मुख्य न्यायालय मुंबई.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्राचे राज्यपाल कसे नियुक्त होतात?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्राचे राज्यपाल — भारताचे राष्ट्रपती द्वारे नियुक्त; ५ वर्ष कार्यकाळ; राज्याचा संवैधानिक प्रमुख.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील पंचायत समितीची स्तर कोणता आहे?
mcqs.explanation: पंचायत समिती — तालुका स्तरावर; ब्लॉक विकास अधिकारी (BDO) प्रमुख; ग्रामपंचायत व जिल्हा परिषद दरम्यान.

mcqs.q: MPSC चे सदस्य किती असतात?
mcqs.explanation: MPSC मध्ये अध्यक्ष व ६ सदस्य असतात — राज्यपाल द्वारे ६ वर्ष कार्यकाळासाठी नियुक्त.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र औद्योगिक विकास महामंडळ (MIDC) ची स्थापना कोणत्या वर्षी झाली?
mcqs.explanation: MIDC ची स्थापना 1962 मध्ये झाली; ती औद्योगिक वसाहती व मूलभूत सुविधा उभ्या करते.

mcqs.q: आशियातील सर्वांत जुनी शेअर बाजार संस्था कोणती?
mcqs.explanation: बॉम्बे शेअर बाजार (BSE) ची स्थापना 1875 मध्ये झाली — ती आशियातील सर्वांत जुनी शेअर बाजार संस्था आहे.

mcqs.q: उजनी प्रकल्प कोणत्या नदीवर बांधलेला आहे?
mcqs.explanation: उजनी प्रकल्प भीमा नदीवर सोलापूर जिल्ह्यात (माढा तालुका) आहे.

mcqs.q: भारताचे सर्वांत मोठे कंटेनर बंदर कोणते?
mcqs.explanation: न्हावा शेवा येथील जवाहरलाल नेहरू बंदर (JNPT, 1989) हे भारताचे सर्वांत मोठे कंटेनर बंदर आहे.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वांत मोठा जलविद्युत प्रकल्प कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: सातारा जिल्ह्यातील कोयना प्रकल्प (शिवसागर जलाशय) हा महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वांत मोठा जलविद्युत प्रकल्प आहे.

mcqs.q: "केळी शहर" म्हणून कोणते महाराष्ट्रातील शहर प्रसिद्ध आहे?
mcqs.explanation: जळगाव जिल्हा केळी उत्पादनासाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे; नागपूर संत्र्यासाठी व नाशिक कांदा-द्राक्षांसाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे.

mcqs.q: चंद्रपूर अतिताप विद्युत प्रकल्प हा महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वांत मोठा ______ आहे.
mcqs.explanation: चंद्रपूर अतिताप विद्युत प्रकल्प (CTPS) हा राज्यातील सर्वांत मोठा औष्णिक विद्युत प्रकल्प आहे; तारापूर हा अणु प्रकल्प आहे.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्र हे कोणत्या उत्पादनात भारतात अग्रेसर आहे?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्र — भारतात सर्वात जास्त साखर उत्पादन; कोल्हापूर, सातारा प्रमुख ऊस भाग.

mcqs.q: नाशिक शहर कशासाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे?
mcqs.explanation: नाशिक — कांदा (भारतात सर्वात जास्त) व द्राक्ष उत्पादन; 'वाईन कॅपिटल ऑफ इंडिया'.

mcqs.q: मुंबई शहर कशासाठी ओळखले जाते?
mcqs.explanation: मुंबई — भारताची आर्थिक राजधानी; BSE, NSE, RBI मुख्यालय; बॉलिवुड चित्रपट उद्योग.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्राचे GSDP भारताच्या GDP मध्ये किती टक्के योगदान देते?
mcqs.explanation: महाराष्ट्र — भारताच्या GDP मध्ये सुमारे १५% योगदान; भारतातील सर्वात मोठी राज्य अर्थव्यवस्था.

mcqs.q: पिंपरी-चिंचवड हे कोणत्या उद्योगासाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे?
mcqs.explanation: पिंपरी-चिंचवड — महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठे ऑटोमोबाइल केंद्र; टाटा मोटर्स, बजाज ऑटो, मर्सिडीज़ बेंज़.

mcqs.q: नागपूर शहर कशासाठी प्रसिद्ध आहे?
mcqs.explanation: नागपूर — 'संत्रा नगरी' म्हणून ओळख; संत्रे उत्पादनात अग्रेसर; विदर्भाची द्वितीय राजधानी.

mcqs.q: भारतीय चित्रपट उद्योग (बॉलिवुड) कोठे केंद्रित आहे?
mcqs.explanation: बॉलिवुड (हिंदी चित्रपट उद्योग) — मुंबई मध्ये केंद्रित; फिल्म सिटी (गोरेगाव), अँडेरी.

mcqs.q: बॉम्बे स्टॉक एक्सचेंज (BSE) कोठे आहे?
mcqs.explanation: BSE (बॉम्बे स्टॉक एक्सचेंज) — मुंबई येथे दलाल स्ट्रीट; आशियातील सर्वात जुना स्टॉक एक्सचेंज (१८७५).

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील जायकवाडी धरण कोणत्या नदीवर आहे?
mcqs.explanation: जायकवाडी धरण — गोदावरी नदीवर; औरंगाबाद जिल्हा; महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठे धरण एक.

mcqs.q: कोयना धरण कोणत्या नदीवर बांधले आहे?
mcqs.explanation: कोयना धरण — कोयना नदीवर; सातारा जिल्हा; महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठे जलविद्युत प्रकल्प.

mcqs.q: सम्रुद्धि महामार्ग कोणत्या दोन शहरांना जोडतो?
mcqs.explanation: सम्रुद्धि महामार्ग (Hindu Hrudaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray Maharashtra Samruddhi Mahamarg) — नागपूर ते मुंबई ७०१ किमी.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्राच्या अर्थव्यवस्थेतील सर्वात मोठा क्षेत्र कोणता आहे?
mcqs.explanation: सेवा क्षेत्र — महाराष्ट्राच्या GSDP मध्ये सुमारे ६०% योगदान; IT, बँकिंग, चित्रपट प्रमुख.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रात द्राक्षेचे उत्पादन सर्वात जास्त कोणत्या भागात होते?
mcqs.explanation: नाशिक-पुणे भागात द्राक्षेचे उत्पादन सर्वात जास्त; नाशिक — भारतात सर्वात जास्त.

mcqs.q: महाराष्ट्रातील कापसाचे उत्पादन मुख्यतः कोणत्या भागात होते?
mcqs.explanation: विदर्भ-मराठवाडा भागात कापसाचे उत्पादन मुख्यतः; 'श्वेत सोना' म्हणून ओळख.

mcqs.q: RBI चे मुख्यालय कोठे आहे?
mcqs.explanation: RBI (भारतीय रिझर्व्ह बँक) चे मुख्यालय मुंबई येथे आहे — स्थापना १ एप्रिल १९३५.

mcqs.q: पैठणी साडी कोणत्या शहरात बनते?
mcqs.explanation: पैठणी साडी — पैठण (औरंगाबाद जिल्हा) येथे बनते; रेशम साडी; महाराष्ट्राची हस्तकला.

mcqs.q: भारताचा पहिला वित्तीय केंद्र कोणते शहर आहे?
mcqs.explanation: मुंबई — भारताची आर्थिक राजधानी; BSE, NSE, RBI मुख्यालय; बँकिंग व वित्तीय केंद्र.

mcqs.q: "गोदावरी" ही कोणत्या प्रकारची संज्ञा आहे?
mcqs.explanation: गोदावरी हे एका विशिष्ट नदीचे खास नाव असल्याने ती विशेष नाम आहे; "नदी" ही जातिवाचक संज्ञा होत.

mcqs.q: "कुटुंब" ही संज्ञा कोणत्या प्रकारात येते?
mcqs.explanation: कुटुंब हा अनेक व्यक्तींचा समूह दर्शवणारा शब्द असल्याने ती समूहवाचक संज्ञा आहे.

mcqs.q: खालीलपैकी "प्रथम पुरुष" सर्वनाम कोणते?
mcqs.explanation: "आपण" हे प्रथम पुरुषाचे (आदरार्थी/समावेशी) रूप आहे; "तो" उत्तम व "तू" मध्यम पुरुष.

mcqs.q: "मुलगी गाणे म्हणते" — या वाक्यातील क्रियापद ओळखा.
mcqs.explanation: "काय करते?" या प्रश्नाची उत्तरे देणारा शब्द "म्हणते" — हा क्रियापद आहे (वर्तमानकाळ).

mcqs.q: "तो पुस्तक वाचत बसला" — येथील क्रियापदाचा प्रकार कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: "वाचत बसणे" येथे दोन क्रिया एकत्र येऊन एक अर्थ साधतात — म्हणून संयुक्त क्रिया.

mcqs.q: "शाळेत" या शब्दातील "शाळा" कोणत्या प्रकारची संज्ञा आहे?
mcqs.explanation: शाळा ही सर्वसाधारण शाळा दर्शवते (विशिष्ट नाव नाही) — म्हणून जातिवाचक संज्ञा.

mcqs.q: "राम उद्या शहरात जाईल." — या वाक्यातील क्रियापद कोणत्या काळात आहे?
mcqs.explanation: "जाईल" हे काम भविष्यात होणार दर्शवते — म्हणून भविष्यकाळ; "उद्या" हा शब्दही त्याची खूण आहे.

mcqs.q: 'मुलगा' या शब्दाचे लिंग कोणते आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'मुलगा' हा पुल्लिंगी शब्द आहे. स्त्रीलिंगी रूप: मुलगी.

mcqs.q: 'घरे' या शब्दाचे एकवचन काय आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'घरे' हे 'घर' या एकवचन शब्दाचे अनेकवचन आहे.

mcqs.q: 'तू कुठे जात आहेस?' हे कोणते वाक्य आहे?
mcqs.explanation: प्रश्नार्थी वाक्य — प्रश्न विचारला आहे.

mcqs.q: 'तो लिहितो' — या क्रियापदाचा प्रकार कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'लिहिणे' ही सकर्मक क्रिया आहे — कर्माची गरज आहे (काय लिहितो?).

mcqs.q: 'मी' हा कोणत्या प्रकारचा शब्द आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'मी' हे उत्तम पुरुषी सर्वनाम आहे.

mcqs.q: 'सुंदर फूल' — यात 'सुंदर' हा कोणता शब्द आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'सुंदर' हे गुणवाचक विशेषण आहे — फुलाचा गुण सांगते.

mcqs.q: 'पाणी' या शब्दाचा प्रकार कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'पाणी' ही द्रव्यवाचक संज्ञा आहे — द्रव्याचे नाव.

mcqs.q: 'माणसे' या शब्दाचे एकवचन काय?
mcqs.explanation: 'माणूस' या एकवचनाचे अनेकवचन 'माणसे'.

mcqs.q: 'आणि' हा कोणत्या प्रकारचा शब्द आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'आणि' हे उभयान्वयी अव्यय आहे — दोन वाक्ये जोडते.

mcqs.q: 'इथे बस' हे कोणते वाक्य आहे?
mcqs.explanation: आज्ञार्थी वाक्य — आज्ञा/हुकूम दर्शवते.

mcqs.q: 'सोने' या शब्दाचा प्रकार कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'सोने' (gold) ही द्रव्यवाचक संज्ञा आहे.

mcqs.q: 'हा फूल सुंदर आहे' — यात किती शब्द आहेत?
mcqs.explanation: चार शब्द: हा, फूल, सुंदर, आहे.

mcqs.q: मराठी भाषेचा उगम कोणत्या भाषेतून झाला?
mcqs.explanation: मराठी भाषेचा उगम संस्कृतपासून महाराष्ट्री प्राकृत मार्गे झाला.

mcqs.q: मराठी भाषेचा पहिला शिलालेख कोणत्या ठिकाणी आढळला?
mcqs.explanation: श्रवणबेळगोली (कर्नाटक) येथे ९८३ CE मध्ये पहिला मराठी शिलालेख आढळला.

mcqs.q: मराठी भाषेला 'शास्त्रीय भाषा' दर्जा कोणत्या वर्षी मिळाला?
mcqs.explanation: मराठीला फेब्रुवारी २०२४ मध्ये भारताची ८वी शास्त्रीय भाषा म्हणून मान्यता मिळाली.

mcqs.q: 'मी गावाला जातो' — या वाक्यात 'गावाला' शब्दातील प्रत्यय कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'ला' हा कर्म/संप्रदान कारक प्रत्यय आहे.

mcqs.q: 'चांगला मुलगा' — यात 'चांगला' हे कोणते विशेषण?
mcqs.explanation: 'चांगला' हे गुणवाचक विशेषण आहे — गुण सांगते.

mcqs.q: 'तीन फुले' — यात 'तीन' हे कोणते विशेषण?
mcqs.explanation: 'तीन' हे संख्यावाचक विशेषण आहे — संख्या सांगते.

mcqs.q: 'ते पुस्तक वाचतो' — या वाक्यात भूतकाळाचे रूप काय?
mcqs.explanation: भूतकाळ: त्याने पुस्तक वाचले (साधा भूतकाळ).

mcqs.q: 'मी जेवत आहे' — हे कोणता काळ आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'मी जेवत आहे' हा साधा वर्तमानकाळ आहे — आत्ता होत आहे.

mcqs.q: 'तो गेला' या वाक्यात 'गेला' क्रियापदाचा काळ कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'गेला' हे भूतकाळी क्रियापद आहे.

mcqs.q: 'तू काय करशील?' हे कोणता काळ आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'करशील' हे भविष्यकाळी क्रियापद आहे.

mcqs.q: 'आम्ही' हे कोणत्या पुरुषाचे सर्वनाम आहे?
mcqs.explanation: 'आम्ही' हे उत्तम पुरुषी बहुवचन सर्वनाम आहे.

mcqs.q: 'फुलांचा माळ' यात 'फुलांचा' चा कारक कोणता?
mcqs.explanation: 'फुलांचा' हा संबंध कारक आहे — संबंध दर्शवतो.

mcqs.q: What are the main types of Samas (compound)?
mcqs.explanation: Compounds have four main types - Avyayibhav, Tatpurush (with sub-types like Karmadharaya and Dvigu), Dvandva and Bahuvrihi.

mcqs.q: Which of the following 'sanketakshare' (abbreviations) is correct?
options: क.ख. - काही खरे, ड.घ. - डाह्या घराण्याचे
mcqs.explanation: Traditional abbreviations (sanketakshare) like 'ka.kha.' mean 'some truth' and 'da.gha.' mean 'of a good family'.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a difference between reflexive and personal 'aapan'?
options: पुरुषवाचक आपण फक्त प्रथम व द्वितीय पुरुषांत येते
mcqs.explanation: Reflexive 'aapan' never works as an object, while personal 'aapan' can - hence statement (क) is wrong.

mcqs.q: Which are the first four parts of speech?
mcqs.explanation: The first four parts of speech - noun, pronoun, adjective and verb - are inflected words, while the remaining four are uninflected (indeclinables).

mcqs.q: What are the main types of adjectives?
options: गुणविशेषण, संख्याविशेषण, सार्वनामिक विशेषण, नामापासून विशेषण
mcqs.explanation: Adjectives are classified into qualitative, numeral (cardinal, ordinal, iterative), pronominal and noun-derived adjectives.

mcqs.q: What are the main types of pronouns?
options: प्रथम पुरुष, द्वितीय पुरुष, तृतीय पुरुष, आत्मवाचक, अनिश्चित, प्रश्नार्थक, निश्चित
mcqs.explanation: Pronouns are first person (I, we), second person (you), third person (he, she, it), reflexive (self), indefinite, interrogative and definite.

mcqs.q: What are the types of verbs?
options: सकर्मक, अकर्मक, संयुक्त, सहाय्यक, प्रयोजक, शक्य
mcqs.explanation: Verbs are of six types - transitive, intransitive, compound, auxiliary, causative and potential.

mcqs.q: What are the main types of nouns?
options: प्रथम पुरुष, द्वितीय पुरुष, तृतीय पुरुष
mcqs.explanation: Nouns are common, proper, abstract, collective and material/liquid nouns.

mcqs.q: What is a 'vidhanpurak' (complement) word?
options: वाक्याच्या पूर्ततेसाठी आवश्यक असलेला शब्द ब) क्रियापद
A word necessary for completing the sentence (ब) A verb (क) Subject (ड) Object
mcqs.explanation: A complement is the word needed to complete the sentence's meaning, e.g. 'singer' in 'He is a singer'.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between direct and indirect objects?
options: क्रियेचा थेट कारभार ज्यावर होतो ते प्रत्यक्ष कर्म; त्याच्याशी संबंधित दुसरे पात्र अप्रत्यक्ष कर्म
mcqs.explanation: The direct object directly receives the action (book), while the indirect object (to the boy) is the related participant.

mcqs.q: Match the transformations : 1. Anand → Anandi; 2. Hushar → Hushari; 3. Kes → Kesal
options: अ व क विशेषणापासून, ब नामापासून ब) सर्व नामापासून विशेषण
सर्व विशेषणापासून नाम ड) फक्त ब नामापासून विशेषण
1 and 3 are noun-to-adjective; 2 is adjective-to-abstract-noun (ब) All are noun-to-adjective (क) All are adjective-to-noun (ड) Only 2 is noun-to-adjec
नामापासून विशेषण 2. हुशार → हुशारी - ब) विशेषणापासून भाववाचक नाम 3. केस → केसाळ - क) नामापासून विशेषण
mcqs.explanation: Anand-Anandi and Kes-Kesal show noun-to-adjective formation, while Hushar-Hushari shows adjective-to-abstract-noun formation.

mcqs.q: Match the verb types with examples : 1. Transitive - (a) I read a book; 2. Intransitive - (b) It rains; 3. Causative - (c) I got this work done
options: मी पुस्तक वाचतो. 2. अकर्मक क्रियापद - ब) पाऊस पडतो. 3. प्रयोजक क्रियापद - क) हे काम मी करून घेतले.
mcqs.explanation: Transitive verbs take an object ('I read a book'), intransitive verbs complete without one ('It rains') and causative verbs imply getting work done through another.

mcqs.q: When did Jyotiba Phule write 'Gulamgiri' and to whom did he dedicate it?
mcqs.explanation: Jyotiba wrote 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery) in 1873 in question-answer form and dedicated it to the Black Americans fighting slavery. The same year, he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj on 24 September 1873.

mcqs.q: What demand did Jyotiba Phule make while deposing before the Hunter Commission of 1882?
options: 12 वर्षांखालील मुलांना प्राथमिक शिक्षण मोफत व सक्तीने द्यावे
mcqs.explanation: Mahatma Phule deposed before the Hunter Commission (1882) demanding free and compulsory primary education for children below 12 years.

mcqs.q: What was the root cause of differences between Agarkar and Tilak?
options: सामाजिक सुधारणा आधी की राजकीय सुधारणा आधी
mcqs.explanation: In 1886, Tilak and Agarkar differed on whether social or political reform should come first. Agarkar became known as the radical of social reform, Tilak as the radical of political action.

mcqs.q: Which of the following pairs is correct?
mcqs.explanation: Astamba (1325 m) is the highest Satpuda peak within Maharashtra; Kalsubai (1646 m) is the highest Sahyadri peak and Dhupgad the highest Satpuda peak (in MP).

mcqs.q: When and where was the Indian National Congress founded?
options: 28 डिसेंबर 1885 - गोकुळदास तेजपाल संस्कृत शाळा, मुंबई
28 डिसेंबर 1886 - गोकुळदास तेजपाल संस्कृत शाळा, मुंबई
mcqs.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded on 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit School, Mumbai, through the efforts of A. O. Hume and others; 72 delegates attended.

mcqs.q: How did Acharya Jawdekar describe Jaggannath Shankarsheth?
options: लोकांच्या वतीने सरकारशी बोलणारे व मध्यस्थी करणारे मुंबईतील पहिले पुढारी
mcqs.explanation: Acharya Jawdekar called Jaggannath Shankarsheth Mumbai's first public spokesman to the government, while Acharya Atre called him the 'uncrowned emperor of Mumbai'.

mcqs.q: Into how many broad types are Marathi words divided?
mcqs.explanation: Marathi words are broadly of two types - Vikari (inflected words that change form in a sentence, e.g. 'manushya, ti') and Avikari (uninflected words that never change, e.g. 'halu, tara, parantu').

mcqs.q: How many parts of speech are there in Marathi grammar?
mcqs.explanation: There are eight parts of speech in Marathi - noun, pronoun, adjective, verb and four indeclinables (adverb, word-connective, conjunctive, absolute). The first four are inflected, the last four uninflected.

mcqs.q: 'Svatah' and 'Aapan' belong to which type of pronouns?
mcqs.explanation: 'Svatah' (self) and 'Aapan' (oneself) are reflexive pronouns, e.g. 'I will study myself'. When 'aapan' means 'we/you all' it is a person-pronoun; when it means 'self' it is reflexive.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly illustrates an indefinite (general) pronoun?
options: आंबा कोणी खाल्ला ते माहीत नाही.
mcqs.explanation: When 'who/what' are used outside questions without a definite reference, they become indefinite pronouns, e.g. 'Who ate the mango is unknown'.

mcqs.q: How many genders are there in Marathi grammar?
mcqs.explanation: Marathi has three genders - masculine (mulga), feminine (mulgi) and neuter (pustak, pani), where no male/female distinction applies.

mcqs.q: Which of the following are abstract nouns that do not have plural forms?
mcqs.explanation: Abstract nouns like cleverness, goodness and courage do not take plural forms. Similarly, collective nouns (crowd, meeting) and liquid nouns (milk, oil, water) also have no plurals.

mcqs.q: The indication of one or many objects through a word is called :
mcqs.explanation: Number (vachan) indicates whether a word refers to one or many objects; it has two forms - singular and plural.
